### Current behavior

The create API/service inserts scale rules as separate rows with unique IDs. `scale_rule.metric_name` has no unique constraint in the supported initialization schemas, and `ScaleRuleServiceImpl.create()` does not reject duplicate metric names. However, `ScaleRuleCache.initialize()` and `addOrUpdateRuleToCache()` key rules by metric name, silently retaining only the last rule for a metric.

`MetricsMonitor.monitorMetrics()` evaluates only `getAllRules()` from that cache, so the runtime does not evaluate all successfully persisted enabled rules.

### Locations

- [ScaleRuleCache.java:31–49](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/scale/monitor/subject/cache/ScaleRuleCache.java#L31)
- [ScaleRuleServiceImpl.create():111–120](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/service/impl/ScaleRuleServiceImpl.java#L111)
- [MetricsMonitor.java:65–75](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/scale/monitor/subject/MetricsMonitor.java#L65)
- [MySQL scale_rule schema](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/db/init/mysql/schema.sql#L2331); the H2 definition has the same lack of metric-name uniqueness.

### Trigger / validation

Create two rules with different IDs/thresholds/sorts but the same metric name (e.g. `cpu_usage`). The API/schema accept them as separate rows, but only the last cached one is evaluated. Disabling or deleting the surviving rule does not restore the other persisted rule to the cache.

A standalone probe compiled the current cache, initialized two independent DOs with IDs a/b and the same metric, and then removed b by ID:

```text
INPUT_RULES=2 CACHE_RULES=1 SURVIVING_ID=b
AFTER_DELETING_B_CACHE_RULES=0 REMAINING_DB_RULE_ID=a
```

Database acceptance is established by schema/service inspection, not a full deployed Admin request. An independent reviewer confirmed the cache key, persistence constraints and monitor consumer.

### Impact / priority

**P2 / Medium; high confidence in the persistence/runtime mismatch.** Operators can save enabled rules that never participate in scaling decisions. At startup the winner depends on initialization ordering; after edits it depends on the last cache update.

### Suggested fix / contract decision

Make persistence, API validation and runtime identity consistent. If multiple rules per metric are supported, store them by rule ID (or group a list per metric) and preserve all during rename/delete. If one rule per metric is intended, reject duplicates before success and enforce the uniqueness invariant in the database, including a migration strategy for existing duplicates. Either contract should avoid silently accepting then dropping a rule.

### Related existing work

#6972 addresses deletion not evicting a rule by its primary key, #6710 premature cache publication before commit, and #6623 double-generated IDs. Those do not address accepted same-metric rows collapsing into a single runtime entry. Searched complete issue titles and live ScaleRuleCache/duplicate-metric queries.


### Reviewed revision

Apache ShenYu 2.7.2-SNAPSHOT, `master@66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4`. Unit-test and CI issue categories excluded.

## Problem
[InstanceCheckService](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/service/impl/InstanceCheckService.java#L149) marks long-missing instances `DELETED` but retains entries in its in-memory table. [syncDB](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/service/impl/InstanceCheckService.java#L174) subsequently processes all entries every round; startup loads persisted records again. There is no expiry cleanup in this service. A deployment with changing container addresses can accumulate historical identities and recurring persistence work.

This is a lifecycle/capacity enhancement; no production memory leak or load threshold has been measured.

## Scope and acceptance criteria
- [ ] Define configurable retention for expired observations, separate from liveness/offline thresholds and audit/history requirements.
- [ ] Bound in-memory retention and database cleanup work, including a policy for legacy rows and optional archival.
- [ ] Prevent an old cleanup task from deleting a newly renewed/restarted identity; preserve namespace isolation and define the cluster authority for cleanup.
- [ ] Never purge an active instance merely because it is absent from one Admin node's local map.
- [ ] Test expiration, renewal concurrent with cleanup, restart, multiple namespaces and master changes with controlled time.
- [ ] Measure recurring database work and retained identities under address churn; document retention and operator expectations.

Related: #7694 defines expired-state semantics; #7697 covers status-query authority; #6496 covers persistence task failure. Do not conflate this policy with deleting gateway configuration or backend service registrations.

- [ ] Bound in-memory retention and database cleanup work, including a policy for legacy rows and optional archival.
- [ ] Prevent an old cleanup task from deleting a newly renewed/restarted identity; preserve namespace isolation and define the cluster authority for cleanup.
- [ ] Never purge an active instance merely because it is absent from one Admin node's local map.
- [ ] Test expiration, renewal concurrent with cleanup, restart, multiple namespaces and master changes with controlled time.
- [ ] Measure recurring database work and retained identities under address churn; document retention and operator expectations.

Related: #7694 defines expired-state semantics; #7697 covers status-query authority; #6496 covers persistence task failure. Do not conflate this policy with deleting gateway configuration or backend service registrations.

## Goal
Let Admin distinguish a recently reporting gateway from one ready to serve traffic. Current [instance status handling](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/service/impl/InstanceCheckService.java#L122) derives ONLINE from heartbeat arrival/age. It does not report startup completion, readiness reason or draining status.

The gateway already has an opt-in [WebSocket initial-sync readiness indicator](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-spring-boot-starter/shenyu-spring-boot-starter-sync-data-center/shenyu-spring-boot-starter-sync-data-websocket/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/springboot/starter/sync/data/websocket/WebsocketSyncHealthConfiguration.java#L58). Reuse established readiness semantics instead of inventing a second contradictory health check.

## Scope
- Reuse existing status-reporting channels and define a backward-compatible, versioned optional status extension.
- Report readiness independently of liveness, with observation time, a bounded reason code and supported capability indicators. Missing/old data means unknown, not ready.
- Define stable deployment instance identity and per-start boot identity so reports from a prior process cannot overwrite the current observation.
- Distinguish configuration channel connectivity from readiness and allow an explicit serving/draining state if supported by the runtime.
- In Admin list/detail show liveness, readiness, last observation age and reason separately. Keep legacy numeric status compatible.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Initializing, ready, readiness-failed and stale observations are distinguishable while heartbeat stays healthy.
- [ ] Reconcile with Actuator and initial synchronization behavior; do not claim that initial sync completion alone proves every dependency healthy.
- [ ] Test legacy reporters, unknown fields, incompatible report versions, restart identity, out-of-order observations and namespace isolation.
- [ ] Test two Admin nodes and failover against a documented authoritative status view.
- [ ] Telemetry/reporting failure does not break gateway request processing; payload size/cadence and diagnostic content are bounded.
- [ ] Coordinate dashboard changes, schema/API compatibility and documentation.

Related: #7692/#7693/#7694/#7696/#7697 are existing status correctness fixes. #7652 adds local file mode: it should be able to report local startup readiness without falsely requiring Admin synchronization.

body_text:
## Goal
Allow operators to see whether a configuration change was actually applied by a gateway. A live sync connection or successful server send must not be displayed as proof of application.

Current [instance reporting](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/service/impl/InstanceCheckService.java#L122) tracks presence, while [WebSocket synchronization](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-sync-data-center/shenyu-sync-data-websocket/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/plugin/sync/data/websocket/client/ShenyuWebsocketClient.java#L438) has configuration application and recovery behavior. Reuse these boundaries and existing reporting transports.

## Scope
1. Define channel-neutral observation fields: configuration source, connection state, last successful application time, applied digest/revision where meaningful, bounded failure reason/count and configuration object counts.
2. Before adding a desired-versus-applied display, define version/revision ownership and granularity. Per-group/per-namespace versions must not imply one atomic global configuration transaction.
3. Send application acknowledgements only after relevant subscriber/handler application succeeds. Audit error-swallowing paths so failed updates cannot generate false success.
4. In Admin show applied, pending, failed, stale/unknown and unsupported distinctly, with request/change correlation and received observation time.
5. Compare only instances belonging to the selected deployment/namespace/source. For file/Kubernetes modes, display the source-specific state without inventing an Admin desired revision.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A connected gateway with failed configuration application shows failure rather than synchronized.
- [ ] Sent-but-unacknowledged, applied, unsupported and stale cases are tested.
- [ ] Snapshot, empty-snapshot deletion, incremental updates, partial failures, reconnect, duplicate/out-of-order acknowledgements and restart identities have defined semantics.
- [ ] Backward-compatible optional frames/fields do not break older clients or Admins.
- [ ] Status remains coherent across Admin failover and preserves namespace isolation.
- [ ] Report traffic/storage is bounded; acknowledgements do not create a second configuration writer or block business traffic.
- [ ] Dashboard shows rollout progress with accurate denominators and explains unsupported channels; initial support may be WebSocket with other channels explicitly marked.

Related: #7692/#7697, snapshot performance #7645, file mode #7652. This is a new operational capability, not a claim that current synchronization lacks reconnect/full-snapshot recovery.

## Scope
1. Define channel-neutral observation fields: configuration source, connection state, last successful application time, applied digest/revision where meaningful, bounded failure reason/count and configuration object counts.
2. Before adding a desired-versus-applied display, define version/revision ownership and granularity. Per-group/per-namespace versions must not imply one atomic global configuration transaction.

5. Compare only instances belonging to the selected deployment/namespace/source. For file/Kubernetes modes, display the source-specific state without inventing an Admin desired revision.

- [ ] A connected gateway with failed configuration application shows failure rather than synchronized.
- [ ] Sent-but-unacknowledged, applied, unsupported and stale cases are tested.
- [ ] Snapshot, empty-snapshot deletion, incremental updates, partial failures, reconnect, duplicate/out-of-order acknowledgements and restart identities have defined semantics.
- [ ] Backward-compatible optional frames/fields do not break older clients or Admins.
- [ ] Status remains coherent across Admin failover and preserves namespace isolation.
- [ ] Report traffic/storage is bounded; acknowledgements do not create a second configuration writer or block business traffic.
- [ ] Dashboard shows rollout progress with accurate denominators and explains unsupported channels; initial support may be WebSocket with other channels explicitly marked.

Related: #7692/#7697, snapshot performance #7645, file mode #7652. This is a new operational capability, not a claim that current synchronization lacks reconnect/full-snapshot recovery.

## Goal
Make Admin an entry point to existing observability tools from instance diagnostics. Keep high-volume metrics, logs and spans in the configured backend rather than storing them in heartbeat payloads or the Admin relational database.

## Current boundary
The instance page has presence/basic machine information. General tracing is tracked by #7566, and #7614 covers tracing plugin control-plane registration rather than querying trace data. Agent Gateway already has an optional [logical MCP call span bridge](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-plugin/shenyu-plugin-agent-gateway/README.md#L512); enabling that bridge alone does not supply SDK export, inbound/outbound propagation or an Admin trace explorer.

## Initial scope
- Define correlation metadata shared by status reports, metric resources, logs and traces: namespace, service/deployment, stable instance identity and boot identity where supported.
- Add operator-configured metric/log/trace navigation links in instance detail with explicit time-window filters. For exact request links use an actual trace ID from a request/log record; do not invent one for an instance.
- Support existing Grafana/Prometheus, logging and tracing deployments through configured URL templates/adapters. Begin with navigation, not a new analytics storage engine.
- Display collection/SDK configuration only to the extent it can be observed reliably. Do not claim successful end-to-end telemetry delivery merely because an exporter is configured.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test fixture correlates one gateway instance across its status, metrics, access log and exported trace using documented identifiers.
- [ ] Selected namespace/instance/time range is correctly encoded in configured links; no credentials or sensitive payload data are embedded in URLs.
- [ ] Missing backend configuration and unavailable data have clear states and do not break status pages or proxy traffic.
- [ ] Namespace authorization is retained; navigation does not pretend to grant access to the destination platform.
- [ ] Dashboard changes have tests for filtering, link generation and legacy instances without correlation fields.
- [ ] Metric label cardinality is budgeted; raw trace IDs/request paths are not added as general metric labels.

Related: #7566/#7614 and #7650. Reuse deployed instrumentation and backend integration rather than duplicating tracing implementation.

## Current behavior
`InstanceInfoServiceImpl.createOrUpdate` assigns `lastHeartBeatTime` on the Java entity for updates, but the instance mapper's column list, result map, insert and update statements contain no heartbeat timestamp. The reviewed initialization schemas also lack this column. The create conversion does not copy the value either. Database reads therefore produce the Java default `0` for a primitive long.

The instance list overlays this with a live local map, masking the omission. Detail queries read the database, and `InstanceCheckService.fetchInstanceData` restores database values on startup/master election. A restored record consequently has no durable last-seen observation, and the checker can age it from epoch zero if no new report arrives. Do not use `date_updated` as a substitute: periodic persistence updates that field independently of receiving a heartbeat.

## Source evidence
- [Mapper and column/result definitions](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/resources/mappers/instance-info-sqlmap.xml#L21)
- [Service assigns the value before calling mapper](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/service/impl/InstanceInfoServiceImpl.java#L70)
- [Create conversion omits heartbeat](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/model/entity/InstanceInfoDO.java#L272)
- [Startup restore](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/service/impl/InstanceCheckService.java#L95)

A local XML inspection confirmed that Base_Column_List, BaseResultMap, insert and updateById omit this field. No database/runtime reproduction was executed during issue preparation.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Define durable last-seen semantics and persist/read the heartbeat observation consistently through create, update, list and detail paths.
- [ ] Add initialization/upgrade changes for supported database dialects and explicit handling of historical rows with no observation.
- [ ] Mapper integration tests round-trip a fixed nonzero timestamp through insert and update; mock-only service tests are insufficient.
- [ ] Test Admin restart/master handover, with and without a subsequent heartbeat; unknown/stale observations are represented explicitly rather than fabricated as fresh.
- [ ] Preserve namespace identity and distinguish last report time from last persistence time.

Related: #7697 concerns missing local-map entries; #7718 concerns readiness; neither repairs the persistence contract.

## Database verification update (2026-10-17)

Reproduced using the H2 instance-table DDL and MyBatis XML mapper from `66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4`, plus recompiled current `InstanceInfoServiceImpl`, entity, VO and mapper interface. This probe used a real H2 database and MyBatis sessions, not a mocked mapper.

A nonzero heartbeat (`1700000000000`) was supplied on create; the database-backed entity and detail service read `0`. Updating the heartbeat to `1700000009999` still read `0`. Assertions confirmed both insert and update round-trip omission.

No production source was modified. Other database dialects and Admin restart were not executed; this verifies the persistence omission underlying those scenarios.

`InstanceInfoServiceImpl.createOrUpdate` assigns `lastHeartBeatTime` on the Java entity for updates, but the instance mapper's column list, result map, insert and update statements contain no heartbeat timestamp. The reviewed initialization schemas also lack this column. The create conversion does not copy the value either. Database reads therefore produce the Java default `0` for a primitive long.

The instance list overlays this with a live local map, masking the omission. Detail queries read the database, and `InstanceCheckService.fetchInstanceData` restores database values on startup/master election. A restored record consequently has no durable last-seen observation, and the checker can age it from epoch zero if no new report arrives. Do not use `date_updated` as a substitute: periodic persistence updates that field independently of receiving a heartbeat.

## Source evidence
- [Mapper and column/result definitions](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/resources/mappers/instance-info-sqlmap.xml#L21)
- [Service assigns the value before calling mapper](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/service/impl/InstanceInfoServiceImpl.java#L70)
- [Create conversion omits heartbeat](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/model/entity/InstanceInfoDO.java#L272)
- [Startup restore](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/service/impl/InstanceCheckService.java#L95)

A local XML inspection confirmed that Base_Column_List, BaseResultMap, insert and updateById omit this field. No database/runtime reproduction was executed during issue preparation.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Define durable last-seen semantics and persist/read the heartbeat observation consistently through create, update, list and detail paths.
- [ ] Add initialization/upgrade changes for supported database dialects and explicit handling of historical rows with no observation.
- [ ] Mapper integration tests round-trip a fixed nonzero timestamp through insert and update; mock-only service tests are insufficient.
- [ ] Test Admin restart/master handover, with and without a subsequent heartbeat; unknown/stale observations are represented explicitly rather than fabricated as fresh.
- [ ] Preserve namespace identity and distinguish last report time from last persistence time.

Related: #7697 concerns missing local-map entries; #7718 concerns readiness; neither repairs the persistence contract.

## Database verification update (2026-10-17)

Reproduced using the H2 instance-table DDL and MyBatis XML mapper from `66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4`, plus recompiled current `InstanceInfoServiceImpl`, entity, VO and mapper interface. This probe used a real H2 database and MyBatis sessions, not a mocked mapper.

A nonzero heartbeat (`1700000000000`) was supplied on create; the database-backed entity and detail service read `0`. Updating the heartbeat to `1700000009999` still read `0`. Assertions confirmed both insert and update round-trip omission.

No production source was modified. Other database dialects and Admin restart were not executed; this verifies the persistence omission underlying those scenarios.

## Current behavior
`HeartbeatListener` caches each Admin login token for a hard-coded 24 hours. `sendHeartbeat` catches send errors and retries on the next tick, but never invalidates the cached token or requests a new login after authentication rejection. Admin token validity is configurable. With a shorter lifetime, or after token invalidation, every subsequent heartbeat can reuse the rejected token until cache expiry or process restart.

Concrete test: obtain a token, configure a shorter Admin token lifetime or make the test Admin reject it, then observe multiple heartbeat ticks. Login succeeds initially, heartbeat is rejected, and the same cached token is repeatedly sent without reauthentication.

## Source evidence
- [Token cache lifetime and loader](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-register-center/shenyu-register-client-beat/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/register/client/beat/HeartbeatListener.java#L87)
- [Send/retry path without invalidation](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-register-center/shenyu-register-client-beat/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/register/client/beat/HeartbeatListener.java#L114)
- [Heartbeat response validation](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-register-center/shenyu-register-common/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/register/common/utils/RegisterUtils.java#L104)
- [Configured expiry used when issuing tokens](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/utils/JwtUtils.java#L99)

Source-based finding; a controlled authentication-expiry regression has not yet been run. This is availability/recovery behavior, not an authentication bypass claim.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Refresh using actual expiry metadata where available and/or invalidate the affected Admin's cache entry after a reliably identified authentication rejection.
- [ ] Preserve enough response/status information to distinguish auth rejection from network failures or unrelated server errors; do not relogin on every IOException.
- [ ] Retry reauthentication with bounded work/backoff so invalid credentials do not create a login storm.
- [ ] Test expiry/rejection, successful renewal, unavailable Admin, multiple independent Admin tokens and repeated invalid credentials without long sleeps.
- [ ] The reporter resumes successful heartbeats without waiting 24 hours or restarting; failure at one Admin does not suppress the others.

Related: #7696 fixes heartbeat instance type; #6608 covers periodic-task exception resilience. Neither handles cached credential rejection.

## Current behavior
Independent `HeartbeatListener` starts a periodic reporter from its constructor and fills `instancePort` from `ServerProperties.getPort()`. The WebSocket sync service likewise passes `serverProperties.getPort()` into its client. These are configured values rather than the port actually bound by the running web server.

When `server.port=0`, the server obtains a real ephemeral port, but the report/client header carries 0. Admin identity includes the reported port, so instance information cannot identify the actual listener and multiple processes behind the same reported address can collide. The independent reporter also schedules immediately, before receiving a server-initialized event.

## Source evidence
- [Independent reporter initialization and report](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-register-center/shenyu-register-client-beat/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/register/client/beat/HeartbeatListener.java#L74)
- [WebSocket client construction](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-sync-data-center/shenyu-sync-data-websocket/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/plugin/sync/data/websocket/WebsocketSyncDataService.java#L206)
- [Admin instance identity](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/service/impl/InstanceCheckService.java#L106)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Use the actual bound application-server port after server initialization; account for a distinct management port without reporting it as the gateway listener.
- [ ] Do not publish a placeholder port before initialization. Define startup/stop ordering and reject invalid/unavailable port observations consistently.
- [ ] Integration-test `server.port=0` and explicit fixed ports for the independent and WebSocket paths; verify two processes receive distinct appropriate identities.
- [ ] Audit the HTTP sync path for the same configuration-versus-bound-port assumption and explicitly cover it if affected.
- [ ] Preserve reporting shutdown/cancellation and avoid adding a second heartbeat scheduler.

Source-based finding; no ephemeral-port deployment was run during issue preparation. Related: #7696 corrects the instance type, and #7718 defines richer instance identity/readiness; neither supplies the actual bound port.

## Current behavior
`InstanceInfoServiceImpl.createOrUpdate` performs `selectOneByQuery` and then inserts an entity with a new random primary key when absent. The instance table has a primary key on id but no unique constraint for the queried logical identity `(namespace_id, instance_ip, instance_port, instance_type)`.

If two writers observe the same absent identity before either insert completes, both insert different ids successfully. Subsequent `selectOneByQuery` uses `LIMIT 1` without selecting a canonical duplicate, so persistence can update only one row while list/count/history retain both.

This race requires overlapping writers (for example concurrent service invocations or multiple standalone Admin writers sharing a database). It is not asserted to occur in the normal single-master, single-scheduler path. A database concurrency reproduction is required.

## Source evidence
- [Check-then-insert](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/service/impl/InstanceInfoServiceImpl.java#L53)
- [Identity lookup and insert](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/resources/mappers/instance-info-sqlmap.xml#L111)
- [Random primary key creation](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/model/entity/InstanceInfoDO.java#L272)
- [MySQL table constraints](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/db/init/mysql/schema.sql#L2371); equivalent reviewed Oracle/H2/PostgreSQL schemas likewise lack identity uniqueness.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Define canonical instance identity and enforce it at the database boundary, using a dialect-compatible atomic upsert or duplicate-conflict recovery; a JVM lock alone does not cover separate Admin processes.
- [ ] Provide a safe deterministic cleanup/migration policy for existing duplicates before adding a unique constraint.
- [ ] A barrier-controlled database integration test makes two writers observe absence and verifies one logical row remains; test repeated updates and namespace separation.
- [ ] Preserve the most recent valid observation on conflict; do not silently swallow duplicate errors and lose a newer report.
- [ ] Validate key lengths/index limits and migration on supported dialects, including Oracle compatibility work #7724.

Related: #7717 tracks retention, #7697 status-query authority and #7723 heartbeat persistence. Those fixes do not enforce identity uniqueness.

## Database concurrency verification update (2026-10-17)

Reproduced using the current H2 instance-table DDL, actual MyBatis mapper and recompiled `InstanceInfoServiceImpl` at `66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4`. Two independent auto-commit sessions queried the same absent identity; a barrier released both writers only after both lookups completed.

Observed: both real inserts succeeded with different primary keys. A direct count for the same namespace/IP/port/type returned **2** rows. Sessions and worker threads were closed in `finally`.

The barrier only coordinates the interleaving; it does not replace SQL operations. This confirms the overlapping-writer race and does not claim the usual single-master scheduler necessarily overlaps. No application source was changed; other dialects and a deployed multi-Admin cluster were not exercised.

## Current behavior
Independent `HeartbeatListener` runs a single periodic reporting task with a five-second target period. `sendHeartbeat` loops over the configured Admin list sequentially; token loading/login and `RegisterUtils.doHeartBeat` are synchronous network calls. Catching a failure allows the loop to continue only after that call returns or times out.

A slow first Admin therefore delays reports to otherwise healthy later Admins and delays the next reporting round. An endpoint that streams an unfinished response slowly enough to avoid individual read timeouts can occupy the call well beyond the twenty-second Admin liveness threshold. Several ordinary timeout delays can also accumulate across the list. This can cause healthy destinations to observe stale/missing heartbeats even though they are reachable.

## Source evidence
- [Single scheduled task and sequential send loop](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-register-center/shenyu-register-client-beat/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/register/client/beat/HeartbeatListener.java#L102)
- [Synchronous heartbeat operation](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-register-center/shenyu-register-common/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/register/common/utils/RegisterUtils.java#L104)
- [HTTP timeout configuration and blocking response-body read](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-register-center/shenyu-register-common/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/register/common/utils/OkHttpTools.java#L46)

Source-confirmed serialization of work; no real multi-Admin fault test was run during issue preparation. Impact depends on the duration of the blocked operation and reporting policy.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Use a controlled slow/stalled first Admin and a healthy second Admin to demonstrate the reporting delay, without long sleeps.
- [ ] Define an end-to-end deadline for each destination, covering login, network phases and response consumption.
- [ ] Isolate destinations using bounded independent scheduling/asynchronous work or a similarly bounded design. Prevent overlapping retries and unbounded work queues.
- [ ] A slow/unreachable destination does not starve reports to a healthy destination beyond the documented liveness budget.
- [ ] Test token-loading stalls, slow bodies, ordinary failures, recovery and shutdown cancellation; retain per-destination token ownership.
- [ ] Report cadence/deadline settings and resource bounds are documented; do not simply add an unbounded thread pool.

Related: #7725 concerns reauthentication after token rejection; #6608 concerns uncaught exceptions cancelling schedules. Neither isolates long-running successful/pending calls.

body_text:
## Current behavior
`InstanceCheckService.setup` schedules both the periodic state checker and `syncDB` on one `ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor(1)`. `syncDB` synchronously persists every cached instance through mapper lookups and writes. While database access is slow or blocked, no state-check task can run on that executor.

Concrete failure scenario: an instance was ONLINE, database synchronization blocks, then its heartbeats stop. The map can continue to expose ONLINE past the normal timeout because the checker is queued behind persistence. A large database batch also increases health-state age even when every query eventually succeeds. Catching exceptions alone cannot resolve this coupling.

## Source evidence
- [Both tasks share one executor](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/service/impl/InstanceCheckService.java#L85)
- [Synchronous per-instance persistence loop](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/service/impl/InstanceCheckService.java#L174)
- [Database lookup/write implementation](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/service/impl/InstanceInfoServiceImpl.java#L53)

Source-based scheduling finding; blocked-database integration behavior has not been reproduced during issue preparation.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A latch-controlled persistence fake/database fault test blocks one synchronization round while the independently scheduled checker still advances liveness states on time.
- [ ] Isolate or bound blocking persistence work so its latency cannot occupy the liveness scheduling lane; preserve bounded queueing and prevent overlapping full persistence rounds.
- [ ] Define consistent observation snapshots/order so an older persistence completion cannot overwrite newer state.
- [ ] Test persistence recovery, shutdown, multiple namespaces and cluster lifecycle/authority; do not create multiple uncontrolled state writers.
- [ ] Measure/report check scheduling lag, persistence duration and state age for large instance populations.

Related: #6496 tracks an exception cancelling the persistence schedule; #7717 tracks retention and recurring work. This issue concerns a still-running slow operation starving the health checker, even when no exception occurs.

## Fault verification update (2026-10-17)

Reproduced against `66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4` using the current checker source and its real single-thread executor. A latch held `syncDB` inside a controlled persistence implementation, while an already-expired instance's existing checker method was submitted to the same executor.

Observed: the checker could not complete while persistence was blocked and the state remained ONLINE. Releasing the latch let the checker run, changing the state to OFFLINE. The fixture used a 100ms threshold and a heartbeat one second in the past, with cancelled startup delays; it verifies starvation rather than measuring production timeout duration. All owned tasks/threads were cleaned up.

No application source was changed, no real slow database was used for this scheduler probe, and this is not a full deployment test.

Reproduced against `66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4` using the current checker source and its real single-thread executor. A latch held `syncDB` inside a controlled persistence implementation, while an already-expired instance's existing checker method was submitted to the same executor.

Observed: the checker could not complete while persistence was blocked and the state remained ONLINE. Releasing the latch let the checker run, changing the state to OFFLINE. The fixture used a 100ms threshold and a heartbeat one second in the past, with cancelled startup delays; it verifies starvation rather than measuring production timeout duration. All owned tasks/threads were cleaned up.

body_text:
## Current behavior
`InstanceCheckService.close()` invokes `syncDB()` before clearing the local map and calling `executor.shutdown()`. There is no finally block. When `InstanceInfoService.createOrUpdate` throws during the final flush, execution exits before executor cleanup.

The checker executor is created with non-daemon threads. This can leave scheduled checking/persistence work active after the bean's shutdown callback fails and can interfere with graceful process/context shutdown. This path also appears when `close()` is called during cluster error handling. The exact process-exit effect depends on the surrounding shutdown lifecycle.

## Source evidence
- [Close ordering without finally](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/service/impl/InstanceCheckService.java#L183)
- [Non-daemon executor creation](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/service/impl/InstanceCheckService.java#L85)
- [Database call can throw on update](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/service/impl/InstanceInfoServiceImpl.java#L70)
- [Cluster error cleanup caller](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/mode/cluster/service/ShenyuClusterService.java#L104)

## Deterministic regression scenario
Initialize the checker and add an observed instance. Configure a mock persistence service to throw during the final synchronization. Invoke `close()` and verify the owned executor is shut down and cleanup completes even though persistence failed. Clean up any test-owned threads unconditionally. No long sleeps or real database outage is needed for this regression.

This issue was verified by source/control-flow inspection; the regression and a process-level graceful-shutdown test were not run during issue preparation.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Executor/resource cleanup runs regardless of final persistence success or failure.
- [ ] Stop accepting/scheduling new work and bound any waiting for outstanding work; preserve explicit behavior for failure of the best-effort final flush.
- [ ] Avoid clearing state while still-running tasks can repopulate or persist it without a documented lifecycle policy.
- [ ] Test final-flush failure, normal shutdown, repeated close and close-before-setup with deterministic executor assertions.
- [ ] Test cleanup ordering in the cluster error path without masking the original cause; no non-daemon checker thread remains after the documented shutdown bound.

Related: #6496 covers periodic sync cancellation after an exception, not cleanup in `close`. #6705 fixed the null executor when setup never ran; its existing no-setup test does not cover final-flush failure. #7744 concerns scheduler starvation by slow persistence.

## Fault verification update (2026-10-17)

Reproduced against `66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4` using the current `InstanceCheckService` source recompiled on Java 17, with a controlled persistence implementation throwing from `createOrUpdate` during `close()`.

Observed: `close()` threw the injected exception and `executor.isShutdown()` was still `false`. The fixture then explicitly shut down/awaited its executor in `finally`. This verifies skipped cleanup; a full process shutdown hang was not tested.

The normal startup-delayed tasks were cancelled in the fixture to avoid waiting; no production source was changed. Supporting dependencies came from local build artifacts. This is a focused reproduction, not a full Maven/deployment test.

body_text:
### Current behavior

After an OPEN breaker's wait window expires, `isRequestAllowed()` returns true while leaving state OPEN. `DividePlugin.filterByCircuitBreaker()` adds those upstreams to its normal allowed list and returns before reaching `tryAcquireHalfOpenProbe()`.

Consequently, the recovery window admits ordinary traffic without acquiring a single probe. Even if state is explicitly HALF_OPEN, `isRequestAllowed()` still returns true and the same filter admits further requests while the first probe has no outcome.

### Locations / actual consumer

- [UpstreamCircuitBreaker.java:233–251](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-plugin/shenyu-plugin-base/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/plugin/base/circuitbreaker/UpstreamCircuitBreaker.java#L233)
- [DividePlugin.java:210–225](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-plugin/shenyu-plugin-proxy/shenyu-plugin-divide/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/plugin/divide/DividePlugin.java#L210)

The class and route-filter comments explicitly describe a single half-open probe. The filter is called by normal Divide `doExecute()` before load balancing/forwarding.

### Reproduction / validation

A probe compiled the current breaker, DividePlugin and its data handler. It opened the actual singleton breaker's state using its configured failure threshold, verified blocking before expiry, then backdated only its private open timestamp to simulate the elapsed wait window without sleeping ten seconds. It invoked the actual route filter twenty times before recording any outcome:

```text
BEFORE_WAIT allowed=false
AFTER_WAIT admissionsBeforeOutcome=20 state=OPEN
EXPLICIT_PROBE_ACQUIRED=true
WHILE_HALF_OPEN admissionsBeforeOutcome=20 state=HALF_OPEN
```

Independent review confirmed the early-return/eligibility interaction. This is a route-admission/state-machine reproduction, not twenty network calls or a measured outage/load benchmark. The probe reset its singleton key afterward.

### Impact / expected behavior

A burst of requests can hit a recovering or still-failing upstream immediately after the wait period, defeating the intended single-probe protection. HALF_OPEN should limit forwarding until that probe succeeds/fails rather than behave like normal availability.

### Suggested fix

Separate candidate eligibility from atomic forwarding permission. Acquire a half-open permit for the upstream actually selected to receive a request and suppress further admissions until its outcome. Avoid consuming permits for candidate upstreams that are never selected, and define cancellation/error release behavior. Keep normal healthy upstream traffic available.

### Locations / actual consumer

- [UpstreamCircuitBreaker.java:233–251](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-plugin/shenyu-plugin-base/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/plugin/base/circuitbreaker/UpstreamCircuitBreaker.java#L233)

body_text:
## Summary

The `e2e` aggregator and its `e2e-case` / `e2e-storage` children fail across many **unrelated** PRs. Because `e2e` is a required check, otherwise-approved PRs show red (`BLOCKED` / `UNSTABLE`) and cannot be merged.

## Evidence

Failing checks aggregated across currently-approved open PRs:

| check | occurrences |
| --- | --- |
| `e2e-case (...)` (e.g. `e2e-*-sync-compose`, `e2e-logging-*-compose`) | 89 |
| `e2e` (aggregator) | 21 |
| `e2e-storage (...)` (h2/mysql/opengauss/postgres) | 14 |

### Root cause 1 — artifact cascade from `build-docker-images`

`e2e-case` fails with (e.g. #7091):
```
##[error]Unable to download artifact(s): Artifact not found for name: shenyu-images
```
because the separate `build-docker-images` job failed (see the Maven-Central issue).

### Root cause 2 — config-sync timing race

`e2e-storage` (#7668) creates a divide selector and immediately calls `/anything`, but the gateway has not yet synced the selector:
```
ERROR org.apache.shenyu.plugin.api.utils.WebFluxResultUtils - can not match selector data: divide , path is /anything
```
The selector is created and then deleted while assertions are still in flight.

### Root cause 3 — external service / MQ timing

- `e2e-storage` assertions target the external `httpbin.org`.
- `e2e-case (e2e-logging-rocketmq-compose)` / `...-logging-rabbitmq-...` flake on log-consumption timing (cf. closed #7417).

## Affected open PRs (sample)

#7038, #7080, #7088, #7091, #7183, #7188, #7189, #7191, #7192, #7198, #7236, #7387, #7513, #7666, #7668, #7699.

## Proposed mitigations

- Decouple e2e from `build-docker-images` (build images inline or gate explicitly) so a Maven flake does not cascade.
- Replace the external `httpbin.org` dependency with the in-repo local httpbin fixture for all e2e suites (as introduced in #7661).
- Ensure a unique RocketMQ/RabbitMQ consumer group per run + `seekToBegin`.
- Make the `e2e` aggregator non-required (the individual cases already carry signal) or auto-retry flaky cases.

Relates to #6281 (flaky-test tracking).

### Current behavior

`TagServiceImpl.update()` creates a partial TagDO from the DTO without `ext`. It then calls `updateSubTags()`, which replaces the edited node in its working map with another partial object lacking the persisted extension state. Descendants are rebuilt from this incomplete parent.

On a parent move, the edited node's final selective update changes `parent_tag_id` but leaves its old `ext` in the database because the new object's ext is null. Descendants meanwhile get a truncated extension chain that contains the edited node but omits its old/new ancestors.

### Locations / actual entry

- [TagServiceImpl.java:95–100,172–240](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/service/impl/TagServiceImpl.java#L95)
- [TagDO.buildTagDO():158–176](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/model/entity/TagDO.java#L158) does not populate ext.
- [tag-sqlmap.xml:151–174](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4/shenyu-admin/src/main/resources/mappers/tag-sqlmap.xml#L151) selectively retains an old ext when the update supplies null.
- `PUT /tag/id/{id}` calls `tagService.update(tagDTO)`.

### Reproduction / validation

A Java probe compiled the current service and TagDO, created root tags A/B, C under A, and D under C through the actual service create methods. It then moved C under B using actual `update()`.

Mapper I/O was replaced by an in-memory store with copy-on-read and the same selective-update semantics as the XML. The service's extension construction and recursion ran unchanged:

```text
BEFORE C.ext=[A] D.ext=[C, A]
AFTER C.parent=B C.ext=[A] D.ext=[C]
```

Expected: C's extension ancestry refers to B, and D's ancestry is C → B. The before state is the passing create control. An independent reviewer confirmed the partial-parent replacement and selective persistence behavior. No deployed database or frontend was used.

### Impact / scope

Successful edits can leave `parentTagId` and the API's serialized extension ancestry inconsistent, and remove ancestor metadata from descendants. Even a rename of a non-root node can rebuild descendants from a parent object missing its previous ext. This report does not claim a specific Swagger pull failure or data loss beyond the observed extension state.

### Suggested fix

Merge the update with the persisted edited node, rebuild its own extension from the effective new parent when needed, and use that complete node as the recursion parent. Persist parent/descendant extension state consistently within the existing transaction while preserving unrelated extension fields.

### Related existing work

#6552 fixed missing transaction rollback around recursive updates. This mismatch occurs when every write succeeds, so adding a transaction does not fix it. #6520 concerns creating a tag whose parent does not exist. Current-tag ancestry reconstruction is a separate deterministic correctness defect.


### Reviewed revision

Apache ShenYu 2.7.2-SNAPSHOT, `master@66d7d954ca37d651a5ad916f988a8081157a7ab4`. P2 / Medium; high confidence. Unit-test and CI issue categories excluded.

body_text:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I searched existing issues. #6610 and #7463 concern queue rejection/offer behavior, but do not cover JVM committed heap versus maximum heap headroom.

### Current Behavior

Starting a gateway with `-Xms256m -Xmx768m` can cause its shared wheel timer to reject scheduled tasks even when several hundred MiB remain available below `-Xmx`.

During a local Docker deployment, the gateway HTTP health endpoint was UP, but the timer logged task rejection and gateway heartbeat registration did not progress normally. Increasing the initial heap to 1 GiB made the scheduled work and heartbeat registration work.

A standalone reproduction against the same built ShenYu classes produced:

```text
# -Xms256m -Xmx768m
committedMiB=256
freeCommittedMiB=156
headroomToXmxMiB=668
accepted=false

# -Xms1g -Xmx1536m
committedMiB=1024
freeCommittedMiB=970
headroomToXmxMiB=1482
accepted=true
```

This is a custom small-heap deployment, not a claim that the stock Docker entrypoint's 2 GiB defaults fail.

### Expected Behavior

Task admission should account for genuinely available heap, including memory that the JVM can commit up to `-Xmx`, or clearly validate/document a minimum initial heap. An otherwise healthy gateway should not silently lose recurring timer/heartbeat work because its initial committed heap is below a fixed queue threshold.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Build the current gateway distribution.
2. Run the following with `-Xms256m -Xmx768m` and the distribution's `lib/*` on the classpath:

```java
import org.apache.shenyu.common.concurrent.MemorySafeLinkedBlockingQueue;

public class HeapAdmissionRepro {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Runtime runtime = Runtime.getRuntime();
        long used = runtime.totalMemory() - runtime.freeMemory();
        MemorySafeLinkedBlockingQueue<Runnable> queue =
                new MemorySafeLinkedBlockingQueue<>(256 * 1024 * 1024);
        System.out.println("committedMiB=" + runtime.totalMemory() / 1024 / 1024);
        System.out.println("freeCommittedMiB=" + runtime.freeMemory() / 1024 / 1024);
        System.out.println("headroomToXmxMiB=" + (runtime.maxMemory() - used) / 1024 / 1024);
        System.out.println("accepted=" + queue.offer(() -> {}));
        System.exit(0);
    }
}
```

3. Observe `accepted=false` despite sufficient maximum-heap headroom. A bootstrap using `HierarchicalWheelTimer` exhibits the timer rejection below.
4. Compare with a larger initial heap.

### Environment

- ShenYu: `2.7.2-SNAPSHOT`, master `04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac`
- Local deployment: ARM64 Linux containers, Eclipse Temurin Java 17, macOS/OrbStack host
- Standalone admission check: Java 17

### Debug logs

```text
WARN HierarchicalWheelTimer - Dropping the expired timer task because the timer task queue has no remaining memory
java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException: Queue capacity is full.
    at org.apache.shenyu.common.concurrent.ShenyuThreadPoolExecutor.execute(...)
    at org.apache.shenyu.common.timer.HierarchicalWheelTimer.addTimerTaskEntry(...)
```

### Code evidence

- [MemoryLimitCalculator.java, lines 56–58](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-common/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/common/concurrent/MemoryLimitCalculator.java#L56-L58) sets its available-memory value to `Runtime.freeMemory()`, which describes unused **committed** heap.
- [MemorySafeLinkedBlockingQueue.java, lines 84–95](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-common/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/common/concurrent/MemorySafeLinkedBlockingQueue.java#L84-L95) gates admission on this value.
- [HierarchicalWheelTimer.java, lines 90–95](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-common/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/common/timer/HierarchicalWheelTimer.java#L90-L95) fixes the queue threshold at `THE_256_MB`.

Please cover `Xms < Xmx` in regression tests and review the admission calculation and the timer's fixed threshold. A possible calculation to evaluate is `maxMemory - (totalMemory - freeMemory)`; this issue does not prescribe it without reviewing the intended memory protection policy.

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I searched existing issues for ClusterForwardFilter, chunked responses and Transfer-Encoding. Previous data-plane response/header issues such as #5788 and #1861 are different paths; this report concerns Admin follower-to-master HTTP forwarding.

### Current Behavior

An authenticated HTTP API request sent to an Admin **follower** with `Connection: close` receives `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` but an unchunked JSON body. Python urllib raises `http.client.IncompleteRead` while trying to parse the opening JSON bytes as a chunk size.

The same request sent directly to the master is correctly chunk-encoded. With keep-alive, the follower body is chunk-encoded but the response contains duplicate Transfer-Encoding headers and duplicated Connection values.

This was verified from raw TCP response bytes, not inferred solely from a client exception.

### Expected Behavior

A follower should emit a valid HTTP response independently of the master-to-follower connection framing. Transfer-Encoding and Connection must describe the follower-to-client hop. Both close and keep-alive clients should be able to read the complete JSON response.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Start two Admin nodes in JDBC cluster mode against the same MySQL database, with matching JWT and cluster event secrets.
2. Identify the elected master and follower. Obtain a normal Admin login token.
3. Send the same authenticated GET to each node:

```python
import os
import urllib.request

for port in (9095, 9096):
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/selector?pluginId=5&currentPage=1&pageSize=100",
        headers={
            "X-Access-Token": os.environ["ADMIN_TOKEN"],
            "Connection": "close",
        },
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as response:
        print(port, response.status, response.headers.get("Transfer-Encoding"))
        print(len(response.read()))
```

4. The master's response is readable; reading the follower response raises IncompleteRead. A matching request using keep-alive may be readable but still exhibits duplicated framing headers.

### Raw Response Evidence

With master on port 9095 and follower on port 9096 in this run:

| Node / request | Response headers | Raw body prefix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| master / close | `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, `Connection: close` | `5fb\r\n{"code":200,...}` |
| follower / close | `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, `Connection: close` | `{"code":200,...}` — no chunk-size line |
| follower / keep-alive | two `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` header lines; `Connection: keep-alive, keep-alive` | `5fb\r\n{"code":200,...}` |

The chunk size above depends on the selector data present. The relevant invariant is that the follower/close response advertises chunked encoding without transmitting it.

### Environment

- ShenYu `2.7.2-SNAPSHOT`, master `04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac`
- Java 17, ARM64 Linux Docker containers, MySQL 8.0
- Two Admin nodes with JDBC cluster mode enabled

### Code Evidence / Suggested Scope

[ClusterForwardFilter.java](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/mode/cluster/filter/ClusterForwardFilter.java#L132-L149):

1. Line 138 buffers the master response as `ResponseEntity<byte[]>`; the HTTP client has already decoded the master's transfer framing.
2. Line 143 copies the master response headers to the follower Servlet response.
3. Line 148 writes the decoded byte array to the Servlet output stream.
4. [The header-copy helper](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/mode/cluster/filter/ClusterForwardFilter.java#L182-L199) does not filter hop-by-hop/framing headers.

Please filter connection-specific/framing headers at the forwarding boundary and let the Servlet container produce the client-facing framing. Review request-side forwarding as well. Preserve ordinary representation headers and ensure Content-Length, if set, matches the actual forwarded bytes.

Regression coverage should include real HTTP master/follower responses for both Connection modes. A mocked Servlet output stream alone will not exercise Tomcat's framing decisions.

body_text:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I searched existing issues for masterCheck, WebSocket failover and Admin restart.
- Related: #6461 reports repeated reconnection/Broken pipe after restart; #6784 fixed orphaned clients during removal. This report isolates delayed configuration convergence after an otherwise successful master election on current master.

### Current Behavior

After stopping the elected Admin master in a two-Admin JDBC cluster, the remaining Admin became master and accepted a rule update, but both gateways continued applying the old rule until approximately the next 60-second service-level WebSocket master check.

Measured in a real local cluster:

```text
admin-master-failover:
    election_seconds = 0.156
new-admin-master-publishes-config:
    convergence_seconds = 60.772
```

The election measurement starts after `docker compose stop` returns, so 0.156 s is the observed polling time to see the changed leader, not an end-to-end crash-detection SLA. The 60.772 s measurement starts after the rule update was accepted and ends when the changed behavior is observed on both gateways.

Existing proxy requests remained available from cached configuration. The problem is stale configuration after control-plane failover, not a total data-plane outage.

### Expected Behavior

Once an Admin connection closes or is known not to be master, the gateway should promptly re-evaluate the configured Admin endpoints and resynchronize with the new master. The service-level master-check/failover delay should be configurable and covered by integration tests, rather than imposing an unconfigurable 60-second cadence.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Start two Admin nodes sharing MySQL with JDBC cluster mode, matching JWT/event/WebSocket secrets, and two gateways.
2. Configure both Admin WebSocket URLs on each gateway and verify initial configuration synchronization.
3. Create a divide route backed by any reachable HTTP service. Confirm both gateways can call it.
4. Stop the elected Admin master and observe the shared cluster_master record change to the survivor.
5. On the surviving Admin, disable a rule using authenticated `POST /rule/batchEnabled` and confirm the database update.
6. Poll actual route behavior on each gateway every second. In this run both gateways continued using the enabled rule and converged after 60.772 seconds.
7. Re-enable the rule and restore the stopped Admin after the test.

### Environment

- ShenYu `2.7.2-SNAPSHOT`, master `04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac`
- Java 17, ARM64 Linux Docker containers
- Two Admin nodes in JDBC cluster mode, one shared MySQL 8.0 database
- Two bootstrap nodes using WebSocket sync and both Admin URLs

### Code Evidence

- [WebsocketSyncDataService.java, lines 127–174](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-sync-data-center/shenyu-sync-data-websocket/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/plugin/sync/data/websocket/WebsocketSyncDataService.java#L127-L174) schedules masterCheck with a hard-coded `TimeUnit.SECONDS.toMillis(60)`. Cleanup/removal of disconnected or non-master clients occurs in this service-level check.
- [ShenyuWebsocketClient.java, lines 316–334](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-sync-data-center/shenyu-sync-data-websocket/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/plugin/sync/data/websocket/client/ShenyuWebsocketClient.java#L316-L334): onClose calls close and invalidates initial-sync state; it does not notify the owning service to rediscover/reselect the master immediately.
- [healthCheck(), lines 352–377](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-sync-data-center/shenyu-sync-data-websocket/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/plugin/sync/data/websocket/client/ShenyuWebsocketClient.java#L352-L377) reconnects the same client/URL, or sends ping/instance information. Its 10-second timer is not an immediate service-level master-discovery trigger.
- masterCheck only rebuilds clients when its list is empty at method entry. If a pass removes the last client, rebuilding may be deferred to a later pass; the measured ~61 seconds is an observed case, not a guaranteed worst-case bound.

Admin reconciliation.interval is a separate compensation mechanism and does not make this gateway-side master-check interval configurable.

### Suggested Scope / Validation

Evaluate a configurable service-level check interval plus a bounded, serialized rediscovery trigger for close/non-master events. Preserve reconnect backoff and prevent concurrent callbacks from leaking or recreating obsolete clients.

Add an integration test that stops the elected Admin, changes configuration through the new master, and checks application on multiple gateways within the configured failover budget. Cover both a closed connection and a still-open connection whose Admin has become a follower.

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I searched existing open/closed issues.
- #6479 fixed propagation/handling of discovery DELETE events in subscribers. This report is earlier in the chain: the Admin HTTP delete API never publishes a change at all.
- #7791 covers stale targets when the shared cache receives a full non-empty replacement; that is a separate downstream reconciliation problem.

### Current Behavior

`DELETE /discovery-upstream/batch` returns success after deleting database rows, but does not publish the remaining upstream snapshot or notify the gateway. A removed, still-reachable upstream can remain a routing candidate in connected gateways.

The actual path is:

```text
DiscoveryUpstreamController.deleteDiscoveryUpstream
  -> DiscoveryUpstreamServiceImpl.delete(ids)
     -> discoveryUpstreamMapper.deleteByIds(ids)
     -> DELETE_SUCCESS
```

The SQL mapper only deletes rows. The service does not resolve affected discovery handlers, call fetchAll/changeUpstream, or publish a DataChangedEvent.

### Expected Behavior

A successful upstream delete should propagate the complete remaining list for each affected handler, including an empty list when the last upstream is deleted. Connected gateways should stop selecting the removed URL without requiring another unrelated edit or reconnect.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Configure a local Discovery-backed divide selector with one reachable HTTP upstream. Keep a gateway connected through WebSocket sync.
2. Confirm requests are forwarded to that upstream.
3. Obtain the upstream row ID from the selector detail and call authenticated:

```http
DELETE /discovery-upstream/batch
Content-Type: application/json
X-Access-Token: <admin-token>

["<upstream-row-id>"]
```

4. The API returns success and the database row is gone.
5. The delete path emits no DISCOVER_UPSTREAM update/delete; the gateway retains its previous snapshot and may continue forwarding to the removed endpoint while it remains healthy.

Use the final upstream in a selector to isolate this missing-notification bug from the non-empty cache replacement issue in #7791.

### Evidence And Validation Boundary

This finding was independently traced through the controller, service, SQL mapper, event paths and background reconciliation. No live production delete was performed for this report.

- [DiscoveryUpstreamServiceImpl.java:181–184](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/service/impl/DiscoveryUpstreamServiceImpl.java#L181-L184) performs only database deletion.
- [DiscoveryUpstreamController.java:92–94](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/controller/DiscoveryUpstreamController.java#L92-L94) exposes that path directly.
- By contrast, [updateBatch:138–157](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/service/impl/DiscoveryUpstreamServiceImpl.java#L138-L157) invokes fetchAll after commit.
- `DiscoveryUpstreamServiceTest.testDelete()` only checks DELETE_SUCCESS after the mapper call; it does not verify a gateway synchronization event.
- WebsocketDataReconciler's normal loop reconciles PLUGIN, SELECTOR and RULE, so enabling it does not compensate DISCOVER_UPSTREAM deletion.

### Suggested Fix / Regression Coverage

Collect affected handler IDs before deleting rows, perform the deletion transactionally, and publish each handler's remaining list after commit. Cover multiple handler IDs, deleting the final upstream, rollback without publication, and an integration assertion that a connected gateway stops selecting the deleted endpoint. Do not rely solely on the SQL row count.

### Environment

Apache ShenYu `2.7.2-SNAPSHOT`, master `04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac`; Java 17; MySQL; WebSocket sync.

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I searched existing issues for requestMaxSize and chunked request size limits. Reports about codec aggregation returning 413 are different from this rule-level limit not being applied.

### Current Behavior

A positive divide rule `requestMaxSize` is enforced only when the request supplies Content-Length. For a normal chunked/unknown-length request, Spring returns -1 for that header, and the comparison succeeds without examining actual body bytes.

A minimal probe using the built DividePlugin and actual rule/upstream caches produced:

```text
knownLength=true  declaredLength=2  limit=1 forwarded=0 forwardedBytes=0
knownLength=false declaredLength=-1 limit=1 forwarded=1 forwardedBytes=2
```

Both requests contain the same 2-byte body. Only the unknown-length request supplies Transfer-Encoding: chunked instead of Content-Length.

### Expected Behavior

The configured rule-level requestMaxSize should apply to actual request size regardless of HTTP framing. A request exceeding a 1-byte limit should be rejected for both known-length and chunked input.

### Reproduction

1. Populate a divide rule with `requestMaxSize=1`, `retry=0`, and a reachable upstream (or a recording downstream chain).
2. Send a POST with Content-Length: 2 and a 2-byte body. The divide size check prevents downstream execution.
3. Send the same body as a chunked request without Content-Length. The divide plugin executes the downstream chain, which receives 2 bytes despite the 1-byte limit.

The probe invoked the actual DividePlugin.doExecute with Spring MockServerWebExchange, a real DividePluginDataHandler rule cache and UpstreamCacheManager, and a recording downstream chain that consumed/counts/releases the body. It ran in a separate JVM against the current built distribution; it did not modify the running cluster.

### Code Evidence

[DividePlugin.java:89–95](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-plugin/shenyu-plugin-proxy/shenyu-plugin-divide/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/plugin/divide/DividePlugin.java#L89-L95):

```java
if (ruleHandle.getRequestMaxSize() > 0) {
    if (exchange.getRequest().getHeaders().getContentLength() > ruleHandle.getRequestMaxSize()) {
        // reject
    }
}
```

The normal Netty proxy path with retry=0 streams the body and does not apply a corresponding cumulative byte limit. `spring.codec.max-in-memory-size` protects codec aggregation; it does not establish this rule-specific limit for arbitrary proxy streams. A separate ingress limit may bound a particular deployment, but would not implement the divide rule's configured value.

### Suggested Fix / Regression Coverage

Retain the early Content-Length check and also enforce the byte budget while consuming unknown-length bodies. Reject/release excess buffers and cancel forwarding appropriately; avoid unbounded aggregation as a replacement. Test exact-limit, over-limit, unknown-length and cancellation cases, as well as ordinary known-length requests.

### Environment

Apache ShenYu `2.7.2-SNAPSHOT`, master `04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac`; Java 17; Netty HTTP transport; divide retry=0.

[DividePlugin.java:89–95](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-plugin/shenyu-plugin-proxy/shenyu-plugin-divide/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/plugin/divide/DividePlugin.java#L89-L95):

```java
if (ruleHandle.getRequestMaxSize() > 0) {
    if (exchange.getRequest().getHeaders().getContentLength() > ruleHandle.getRequestMaxSize()) {
        // reject
    }
}
```

The normal Netty proxy path with retry=0 streams the body and does not apply a corresponding cumulative byte limit. `spring.codec.max-in-memory-size` protects codec aggregation; it does not establish this rule-specific limit for arbitrary proxy streams. A separate ingress limit may bound a particular deployment, but would not implement the divide rule's configured value.

### Suggested Fix / Regression Coverage

Retain the early Content-Length check and also enforce the byte budget while consuming unknown-length bodies. Reject/release excess buffers and cancel forwarding appropriately; avoid unbounded aggregation as a replacement. Test exact-limit, over-limit, unknown-length and cancellation cases, as well as ordinary known-length requests.

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I searched open and closed issues for headerMaxSize and header-name size accounting; no matching report was found.
- #7816 concerns request BODY size and unknown Content-Length. This report concerns how headerMaxSize accounts for request HEADERS.

### Current Behavior

Divide's `headerMaxSize` sums only header VALUE bytes, omitting names and serialized header-field overhead. A header section can exceed the configured rule limit while its values remain below it, and the request is forwarded.

A standalone probe against the current built DividePlugin, actual rule cache and upstream cache produced:

```text
longName=true  headerLimit=128 valueBytes=9   headerBytes=225 forwarded=1
longName=false headerLimit=128 valueBytes=209 headerBytes=224 forwarded=0
```

The first request contains `Host: 127.0.0.1` and an empty-valued custom header whose name is `X-` followed by 200 ASCII `N` characters. The second uses a short custom header name and a 200-byte value. `headerBytes` counts HTTP/1.1 field names, `: `, values, CRLF and the final CRLF; it does not include the request line. The oversized-name case is permitted solely because the implementation examines values.

### Expected Behavior

The rule-level headerMaxSize should have a documented size definition and enforce the complete intended header size consistently. If it is intended to mean only header values, that limitation needs to be explicit in configuration/API semantics rather than appearing to be a total request-header limit.

### Reproduction

1. Configure a divide rule with `headerMaxSize=128`, no body restriction, and any valid upstream.
2. Invoke it with a GET containing the Host field and the long empty-valued header described above.
3. Observe that the divide chain forwards the request although its header fields exceed 128 bytes.
4. Compare with the same approximate total size using a short name and a long value; this request is rejected by the rule.

The reproduction invoked the actual DividePlugin.doExecute using Spring MockServerWebExchange, a populated DividePluginDataHandler cache, a populated UpstreamCacheManager and a recording downstream chain. It ran outside the deployed gateway process. A complete raw HTTP end-to-end test has not been performed for this report.

### Code Evidence

[DividePlugin.java:77–87](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-plugin/shenyu-plugin-proxy/shenyu-plugin-divide/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/plugin/divide/DividePlugin.java#L77-L87):

```java
long headerSize = exchange.getRequest().getHeaders().values()
        .stream()
        .flatMap(Collection::stream)
        .mapToLong(header -> header.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8).length)
        .sum();
```

Header names are never read by this calculation. An independent parser/ingress upper bound, such as an 8 KiB Netty limit, does not enforce a smaller rule-specific value of 128 bytes; the example header is well below that outer limit.

### Suggested Fix / Coverage

Define the byte-accounting contract and include field names and applicable per-value/header-line overhead. Cover an empty-valued long name, several long names with short values, multi-valued headers, exact-limit and over-limit cases. Keep parser-level protection independent from rule-level policy.

### Environment

## Goal

Evaluate and implement a lightweight HTTP proxy execution path when the effective rule retry count is zero, preserving the existing request, timeout and error semantics.

Performance baseline/tracking: #7650. Reviewed revision: `04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac` (`2.7.2-SNAPSHOT`). This is a source-grounded optimization candidate, not a measured production bottleneck or a promised latency improvement.

## Current work on each request

- [AbstractHttpClientPlugin.java:102–115](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-plugin/shenyu-plugin-httpclient/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/plugin/httpclient/AbstractHttpClientPlugin.java#L102-L115) selects and allocates a RetryStrategy and invokes its execute method even for retry=0.
- [DefaultRetryStrategy.java:68–86](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-plugin/shenyu-plugin-httpclient/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/plugin/httpclient/DefaultRetryStrategy.java#L68-L86) constructs/configures RetryBackoffSpec, computes a retry-sequence timeout and attaches retryWhen/error-mapping operators although no application retry can occur.
- Fixed/exponential strategy paths likewise install retry machinery for a zero retry count.

The original request and timeout/error handling remain necessary. This task concerns avoidable setup/allocation, not removing protection or changing retry eligibility.

## Scope and acceptance criteria

- [ ] Benchmark retry=0 with a controlled local upstream, warm JVM and fixed successful request rate; record allocation bytes/request, CPU/request, throughput and p50/p95/p99.
- [ ] Compare GET, small/large POST and streamed responses. Isolate this change from JVM, pool, logging and matching-cache changes.
- [ ] Add a lightweight no-retry path only if its benefit exceeds run-to-run variation or materially lowers allocation/resource cost.
- [ ] Preserve the current outcomes for each configured backoff type: success, upstream 4xx/5xx, connect/read timeout, generic errors, and cancellation. In particular, default strategy retry exhaustion currently performs status/error mapping even when the retry count is zero; do not blindly return the original publisher and change externally visible status codes.
- [ ] Preserve rule timeout budgets, downstream execution, tracing and cancellation. Assert a single application-level outbound attempt for retry=0 and no body replay-cache initialization.
- [ ] Keep retry>0 current/failover behavior and body-replay limits unchanged, with regression coverage.
- [ ] Retain raw benchmark commands/configuration/results and report observed tradeoffs. Do not add production dependencies for the benchmark.

## Related work

#6413 covers correct replay of retryable request bodies; #7752 covers non-default failover strategy behavior. Neither removes zero-retry setup cost. This task does not duplicate connection reuse/capacity work (#6574, #7644), nor claim to reduce upstream execution time.
