body_text:
## Goal

Evaluate publishing concurrency-safe, read-only upstream-list snapshots so routing requests do not need to copy the entire healthy-upstream list on every lookup.

Performance baseline/tracking: #7650. Reviewed revision: `04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac` (`2.7.2-SNAPSHOT`). Allocation/copy behavior is confirmed in source; an application-level performance gain has not been measured.

## Current request-path cost

[UpstreamCacheManager.findUpstreamListBySelectorId():128–130](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-loadbalancer/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/loadbalancer/cache/UpstreamCacheManager.java#L128-L130) returns `new ArrayList<>(upstreamList)` for each lookup. Divide requests call this before breaker filtering and load balancing; failover can perform additional lookups.

This creates a list and backing-array copy proportional to the selector's upstream count for each request. A single-target, low-rate route will have a much smaller potential benefit than a high-rate selector with many targets.

## Required safety boundary

The copy protects callers from mutable health-check state. #6857 previously addressed exposing a concurrently mutated ArrayList. Simply returning the existing shared list, or wrapping a still-mutated backing list, is not an acceptable optimization.

A candidate design should move structural copying/publication to configuration/health-state updates and expose a coherent read-only snapshot to readers. Upstream elements themselves contain mutable weight/health metadata: structural list immutability alone does not settle element visibility, identity or update semantics.

## Scope and acceptance criteria

- [ ] Establish routing-read and update/health-transition baselines for 1, 10, 100 and larger justified upstream counts; measure allocation/request, CPU, GC and p99 at equal successful throughput.
- [ ] Include concurrent health transitions, weight/metadata changes and configuration churn; measure write-side cost as well as read-side benefit.
- [ ] Define snapshot ownership/publication and ensure no mutable backing list is exposed across threads.
- [ ] Preserve handling of missing/empty lists, target identity, manual offline status, health-check enable/disable, failover and circuit-breaker filtering.
- [ ] Regression-test concurrent readers/writers and ensure removed targets do not remain routing candidates. Coordinate with #7791's existing cache-reconciliation correctness work rather than treating stale targets as acceptable snapshot semantics.
- [ ] Audit consumers that may mutate returned collections and adapt them without allowing shared-state mutation.
- [ ] Compare identical workloads before/after; retain the change only with demonstrated benefit and no unacceptable update-time/p99 regression.

## Related work

#6857 is the prior concurrency bug and explains why the current copy must not be deleted without a replacement publication model. #7791 addresses full configuration replacement correctness; #7815 addresses missing Admin delete notifications. This task is specifically the request-side list-copy cost after correctness is preserved.

## Goal

Reduce repeated circuit-breaker key construction, list allocation and scanning in the HTTP divide request path, while preserving routing and breaker state-transition correctness.

Performance baseline/tracking: #7650. Reviewed revision: `04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac` (`2.7.2-SNAPSHOT`). These are confirmed source-level operations, not yet profiled bottlenecks. No fixed performance gain is claimed.

## Current repeated work

### Description

`GrpcPlugin.doExecute()` deserializes the same `MetaData.rpcExt` JSON into `GrpcExtInfo` for each request, even when the endpoint metadata has not changed. This repeats configuration parsing and allocation on the request path.

Confirmed in Apache ShenYu 2.7.2-SNAPSHOT and upstream `master@7cc1818ace246f60a608e44b5fe985dff46908e7`. The inspected upstream file is identical to the current working copy.

### Code evidence and trigger

[`GrpcPlugin.java:107-115`](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/7cc1818ace246f60a608e44b5fe985dff46908e7/shenyu-plugin/shenyu-plugin-proxy/shenyu-plugin-rpc/shenyu-plugin-grpc/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/plugin/grpc/GrpcPlugin.java#L107-L115):

```java
GrpcExtInfo extInfo = StringUtils.isBlank(metaData.getRpcExt())
        ? new GrpcExtInfo()
        : Optional.ofNullable(GsonUtils.getGson().fromJson(metaData.getRpcExt(), GrpcExtInfo.class))
                .orElseGet(GrpcExtInfo::new);
CallOptions callOptions = CallOptions.DEFAULT.withDeadlineAfter(extInfo.timeout, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);
```

For every valid request to a gRPC endpoint with nonblank `rpcExt`, the same unchanged JSON is parsed again. The parsed values describe endpoint configuration (`timeout` and `methodType`), rather than request-specific arguments.

### Expected behavior / suggested direction

Reuse an immutable parsed representation while the corresponding metadata remains unchanged, or parse it during metadata update handling. Keep cache ownership/invalidation tied to metadata changes and removal, and bound any retained cache entries.

Only the parsed metadata should be reused: `CallOptions.withDeadlineAfter(...)` must still create a fresh request-relative deadline for each call. Preserve blank/null/JSON-null defaults and the existing handling of invalid metadata.

### Task List

- [ ] Avoid repeated JSON deserialization for unchanged gRPC endpoint metadata.
- [ ] Handle metadata updates/removal without stale timeout or method type values or unbounded retention.
- [ ] Preserve null/blank defaults and fresh per-request deadlines.
- [ ] Verify reuse across repeated calls and refreshed values after metadata changes.
- [ ] Benchmark before claiming a latency or throughput gain.

### Related work / validation limits

#6650 addressed null/blank `rpcExt` handling; this task preserves those semantics and concerns repeated configuration parsing instead.

The repeated parse is confirmed by source inspection. No benchmark was run, and this report does not claim a high-severity correctness failure.

body_text:
## Goal and motivation

Reduce the bytes and object-processing work associated with large Admin-to-gateway configuration synchronization by introducing an explicit, compact **gateway wire projection**, starting with Discovery upstream data.

Keep Admin's internal domain/event objects intact. Reuse existing transport envelopes rather than introducing a generic intermediate event framework or duplicating every configuration model immediately.

Reviewed revision: Apache ShenYu `2.7.2-SNAPSHOT`, master `04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac`.

This proposal concerns configuration propagation, initial synchronization and reconnect snapshots. It does not claim that database management fields are on the normal gateway request hot path, or that smaller JSON alone establishes a particular request-latency improvement.

## Current behavior and evidence

The same common DTO families are used across Admin event publication, listener caches, Admin-to-Admin event forwarding and gateway-facing serialization. For example:

- [WebsocketDataChangedListener.sendByNamespace():148–166](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/listener/websocket/WebsocketDataChangedListener.java#L148-L166) groups the existing DTOs by namespace and serializes them directly inside WebsocketData.
- [DiscoveryUpstreamData](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-common/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/common/dto/DiscoveryUpstreamData.java#L25-L78) contains both runtime upstream configuration and persistence/binding fields.
- ClusterDataChangedEventForwarder serializes event.getSource() for the other Admin. That is an internal/control-plane contract, not automatically the right place to trim a gateway payload.
- HTTP polling and registry-backed sync channels have their own serialization/cache/key paths and must be audited explicitly; a WebSocket-only change should not be presented as optimizing every channel.

The existing DTOs are already partly runtime-oriented. Most RuleData/SelectorData matching and plugin fields are meaningful. The proposal is targeted field projection, not the assumption that most configuration data is unused.

## Field-level findings

Repository consumer searches identified the following **candidates for standard gateway wire payloads**, not fields proven removable from every external/custom consumer:

| Object | Candidate fields | Reason / qualification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DiscoverySyncData | discoveryHandlerId | Admin binding identifier; no standard gateway read found |
| DiscoveryUpstreamData | id, dateUpdated, discoveryHandlerId | Persistence/update metadata; no standard gateway read found |
| DiscoveryUpstreamData | per-upstream namespaceId | Repeats namespace information; standard handlers consume the enclosing DiscoverySyncData context. Preserve and validate the outer namespace; audit extensions before removal. |
| SelectorData | beforeConditionList | No current built-in gateway read found; updates may carry a previous condition list. Do not confuse this with the required current conditionList. |
| RuleData | beforeConditionDataList | Same qualification; current conditionDataList remains required. |

The first implementation should focus on Discovery. Treat the old-condition fields as a follow-up after old gateway, cache-invalidation and extension compatibility are verified.

### Fields that must not be dropped indiscriminately

- **dateCreated**: [DivideUpstreamDataHandler:52–63](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-plugin/shenyu-plugin-proxy/shenyu-plugin-divide/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/plugin/divide/handler/DivideUpstreamDataHandler.java#L52-L63) converts it into the runtime upstream timestamp. Load-balancer warmup uses that timestamp. WebSocket/gRPC upstream handlers also consume it. Omission can reset it to the current time and change behavior.
- **protocol, url, status, weight, props**: required upstream configuration. props can contain warmup, health-check, gray and other plugin metadata; do not trim its opaque contents without a plugin-specific schema/contract.
- **DiscoverySyncData.selectorName**: TCP routing and discovery deletion identity use it; it is not merely a UI label.
- **SelectorData.pluginId**: LogCollectConfigUtils.isSampled uses it for global logging-sampler fallback.
- **RuleData.name**: [McpServerPluginDataHandler:149–153](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-plugin/shenyu-plugin-mcp-server/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/plugin/mcp/server/handler/McpServerPluginDataHandler.java#L149-L153) uses it as a default tool name; it is not universally diagnostic-only.
- **Current matching fields, handles and flags**: id/parent identity, pluginName, enabled, sort, matchMode, matchRestful, condition data, continued and plugin handles are used by matching, ordering and plugin handlers.
- **Namespace and snapshot/event semantics**: keep the identity required for isolation, grouping, deletion and authoritative replacement. The existing WebsocketData namespaceId/fullSnapshot fields must retain their meaning.

MetaData and AppAuthData were also inspected; no safe generic field-removal set was established for them. Their apparent extra fields participate in RPC/metadata or authentication behavior.

### Null versus empty

GsonUtils' normal serializer already omits null fields. Null omission is not a new saving to claim. It still serializes empty arrays. SelectorDO/RuleDO snapshot conversion supplies empty before-condition lists in some paths, so omitting a redundant empty field could save repeated names/array syntax, but null/empty/missing semantics and older consumers must first be tested.

## Size experiment: useful evidence, not a production promise

A standalone Java probe used the current built DTOs, GsonUtils and WebsocketData to serialize 10,000 synthetic upstreams in a Discovery snapshot, then removed only the Discovery candidates in the table above. Runtime fields including dateCreated were retained.

Fixture:

- one divide selector and one namespace;
- 10,000 distinct upstream addresses;
- 19-digit row IDs, a repeated handler ID and a 36-character namespace;
- created/updated timestamps, protocol=http://, status=0, weight=100;
- props="{}" to make the fixture reproducible.

Exact generation for i=0..9999: id=`2111700000000000000+i`; handler ID=`2111700000000000000`; namespace=`649330b6-c2d7-4edc-be8e-8a54df9eb385`; dateCreated=`Timestamp(1792300000000+i*1000)`; dateUpdated=`Timestamp(1792301000000+i*1000)`; url=`10.0.(i/250).(i%250+1):8080`. The outer Discovery item used selectorId=`2111700000000000001`, selectorName=`/example`, pluginName=`divide`, and the same handler ID/namespace. The WebsocketData constructor used DISCOVER_UPSTREAM/MYSELF and its existing defaults. Preserve the current GsonUtils timestamp encoding when reproducing the byte counts.

| Representation | Original | Candidate projection |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| UTF-8 JSON bytes | 2,793,466 | 1,203,423 |
| Additional standalone gzip comparison | 129,926 | 59,014 |

The JSON reduction is approximately 57% **for this fixture**. This does not mean all deployments save 57%, that the current sync channel already uses gzip, or that end-to-end latency improves by 57%. Large handles/props and compression can change the distribution substantially. The experiment checked serialized size, not complete mixed-version runtime compatibility.

Minimal fixture/reduction recipe:

```java
// Populate 10,000 DiscoveryUpstreamData entries with all fields described above.
// Wrap them in DiscoverySyncData and WebsocketData("DISCOVER_UPSTREAM", "MYSELF", ...).
String original = GsonUtils.getInstance().toJson(frame);
JsonObject compact = JsonParser.parseString(original).getAsJsonObject();
for (JsonElement item : compact.getAsJsonArray("data")) {
    JsonObject discovery = item.getAsJsonObject();
    discovery.remove("discoveryHandlerId");
    for (JsonElement entry : discovery.getAsJsonArray("upstreamDataList")) {
        JsonObject upstream = entry.getAsJsonObject();
        for (String field : List.of("id", "dateUpdated", "discoveryHandlerId", "namespaceId")) {
            upstream.remove(field);
        }
        // dateCreated and all runtime routing fields remain present.
    }
}
// Compare original.getBytes(UTF_8).length with compact.toString().getBytes(UTF_8).length.
```

JSON-tree removal was only the measurement technique. It is **not** the proposed production implementation.

## Proposed design boundary

```text
Admin entities / existing DataChangedEvent / internal DTOs
                   |
          gateway-sync projection
                   |
compact, explicitly defined gateway payload DTO
                   |
existing transport envelope -> one serialization -> gateway adaptation
```

1. Keep the original Admin event and shared DTO contracts for internal caches, persistence-related operations and Admin-to-Admin forwarding.
2. Introduce a small, explicit payload DTO only where it differs meaningfully, for example DiscoveryUpstreamSyncDTO and its enclosing gateway view. Names/package placement are proposals; use an existing shared contract module rather than adding a new runtime module/dependency by default.
3. Project from typed source objects directly into that DTO at the gateway-facing boundary and serialize once. Avoid production object -> JSON -> delete fields -> JSON round trips.
4. Reuse WebsocketData for WebSocket framing, and preserve the corresponding existing envelope/key contracts on other channels. Do not build a second generic event bus/envelope merely to remove a few fields.
5. Keep plugin-specific handle/props opaque initially. Do not make projection decisions solely from the fact that one test deployment enables only divide.
6. Do not globally mark existing shared fields transient/ignored: this can silently affect other serialization consumers.

### Event-specific payloads

- UPDATE/CREATE need the complete intended runtime item unless a separate patch protocol is explicitly designed; a missing field must not silently mean clear/reset.
- DELETE can be more compact, but the key is group/plugin specific, not universally just id. [DiscoveryUpstreamKey](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-sync-data-center/shenyu-sync-data-api/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/sync/data/api/DiscoveryUpstreamKey.java#L22-L38) already defines pluginName, selectorId and optional selectorName; preserve namespace context and audit deletion handlers.
- MYSELF/REFRESH must preserve full-group/namespace replacement semantics, including authoritative empty arrays. Omitting redundant fields is different from dropping the empty data array that clears configuration.

## Compatibility and rollout

An internal common-DTO getter search does not prove an external plugin, WASM guest, older Bootstrap, or registry consumer ignores a field. Define supported protocol/capability negotiation or a backward-compatible opt-in before enabling compact output in a mixed fleet. Older consumers must retain a supported full-payload path unless compatibility is demonstrated.

Audit WebSocket, HTTP polling, registry-backed sync, initial snapshots, incremental changes, failover/reconnect and plugin-store/WASM consumers separately. Preserve identity/path construction and consider representation-specific serialization, hashes/digests, deduplication and cache keys: changing field presence must not cause cross-version cache confusion or repeated refresh storms.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Publish a field-to-consumer inventory for the first projected group and distinguish unused built-in fields from extension/legacy contract requirements.
- [ ] Retain Admin internal event/cache/cluster-forward behavior; prove the gateway projection does not mutate the shared source objects.
- [ ] Implement the minimal typed projection and keep one production serialization step; preserve each affected transport envelope.
- [ ] Verify old/new Admin and gateway combinations, custom/WASM consumers where supported, and legacy fallback/capability behavior.
- [ ] Test UPDATE/CREATE/DELETE/MYSELF/REFRESH, null/empty/missing fields, authoritative empty snapshots and namespace isolation.
- [ ] Test divide/gRPC warmup timestamps, TCP selector naming, logging sampler fallback, MCP default tool names and relevant plugin handlers before declaring fields removable.
- [ ] Keep deletion/replacement correctness separate and intact, including #7815 and #7791; smaller messages must not retain deleted routes.
- [ ] Compare 1k/10k+ realistic payload shapes, with small and large handles/props. Measure JSON and compressed bytes, serialization/deserialization CPU, allocation/GC, synchronization/apply time and business-request p99 during sync.
- [ ] Record gateway/Admin revisions, JVM/configuration, commands and repeat-run variation. Keep only demonstrated benefits; do not extrapolate the synthetic size ratio into a universal latency claim.

## Related work and scope separation

- #7650: performance baseline/tracker.
- #7645: batching and invalidation while applying received namespace snapshots. This proposal reduces/defines the transmitted representation before application; the two changes should be benchmarked independently.
- #7815 / #7791: synchronization/cache correctness prerequisites, not payload-size optimizations.

No implementation changes have been made for this proposal. Consumer tracing and the standalone serialization-size experiment are the current evidence.

The outer Discovery item used selectorId=`2111700000000000001`, selectorName=`/example`, pluginName=`divide`, and the same handler ID/namespace. The WebsocketData constructor used DISCOVER_UPSTREAM/MYSELF and its existing defaults. Preserve the current GsonUtils timestamp encoding when reproducing the byte counts.

| Representation | Original | Candidate projection |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| UTF-8 JSON bytes | 2,793,466 | 1,203,423 |
| Additional standalone gzip comparison | 129,926 | 59,014 |

The JSON reduction is approximately 57% **for this fixture**. This does not mean all deployments save 57%, that the current sync channel already uses gzip, or that end-to-end latency improves by 57%. Large handles/props and compression can change the distribution substantially. The experiment checked serialized size, not complete mixed-version runtime compatibility.

Minimal fixture/reduction recipe:

```java
// Populate 10,000 DiscoveryUpstreamData entries with all fields described above.
// Wrap them in DiscoverySyncData and WebsocketData("DISCOVER_UPSTREAM", "MYSELF", ...).
String original = GsonUtils.getInstance().toJson(frame);
JsonObject compact = JsonParser.parseString(original).getAsJsonObject();
for (JsonElement item : compact.getAsJsonArray("data")) {
    JsonObject discovery = item.getAsJsonObject();
    discovery.remove("discoveryHandlerId");
    for (JsonElement entry : discovery.getAsJsonArray("upstreamDataList")) {
        JsonObject upstream = entry.getAsJsonObject();
        for (String field : List.of("id", "dateUpdated", "discoveryHandlerId", "namespaceId")) {
            upstream.remove(field);
        }
        // dateCreated and all runtime routing fields remain present.
    }
}
// Compare original.getBytes(UTF_8).length with compact.toString().getBytes(UTF_8).length.
```

JSON-tree removal was only the measurement technique. It is **not** the proposed production implementation.

## Proposed design boundary

```text
Admin entities / existing DataChangedEvent / internal DTOs
                   |
          gateway-sync projection
                   |
compact, explicitly defined gateway payload DTO
                   |
existing transport envelope -> one serialization -> gateway adaptation
```

1. Keep the original Admin event and shared DTO contracts for internal caches, persistence-related operations and Admin-to-Admin forwarding.
2. Introduce a small, explicit payload DTO only where it differs meaningfully, for example DiscoveryUpstreamSyncDTO and its enclosing gateway view. Names/package placement are proposals; use an existing shared contract module rather than adding a new runtime module/dependency by default.
3. Project from typed source objects directly into that DTO at the gateway-facing boundary and serialize once. Avoid production object -> JSON -> delete fields -> JSON round trips.
4. Reuse WebsocketData for WebSocket framing, and preserve the corresponding existing envelope/key contracts on other channels. Do not build a second generic event bus/envelope merely to remove a few fields.
5. Keep plugin-specific handle/props opaque initially. Do not make projection decisions solely from the fact that one test deployment enables only divide.
6. Do not globally mark existing shared fields transient/ignored: this can silently affect other serialization consumers.

### Event-specific payloads

- UPDATE/CREATE need the complete intended runtime item unless a separate patch protocol is explicitly designed; a missing field must not silently mean clear/reset.
- DELETE can be more compact, but the key is group/plugin specific, not universally just id. [DiscoveryUpstreamKey](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-sync-data-center/shenyu-sync-data-api/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/sync/data/api/DiscoveryUpstreamKey.java#L22-L38) already defines pluginName, selectorId and optional selectorName; preserve namespace context and audit deletion handlers.
- MYSELF/REFRESH must preserve full-group/namespace replacement semantics, including authoritative empty arrays. Omitting redundant fields is different from dropping the empty data array that clears configuration.

## Compatibility and rollout

An internal common-DTO getter search does not prove an external plugin, WASM guest, older Bootstrap, or registry consumer ignores a field. Define supported protocol/capability negotiation or a backward-compatible opt-in before enabling compact output in a mixed fleet. Older consumers must retain a supported full-payload path unless compatibility is demonstrated.

Audit WebSocket, HTTP polling, registry-backed sync, initial snapshots, incremental changes, failover/reconnect and plugin-store/WASM consumers separately. Preserve identity/path construction and consider representation-specific serialization, hashes/digests, deduplication and cache keys: changing field presence must not cause cross-version cache confusion or repeated refresh storms.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Publish a field-to-consumer inventory for the first projected group and distinguish unused built-in fields from extension/legacy contract requirements.
- [ ] Retain Admin internal event/cache/cluster-forward behavior; prove the gateway projection does not mutate the shared source objects.
- [ ] Implement the minimal typed projection and keep one production serialization step; preserve each affected transport envelope.
- [ ] Verify old/new Admin and gateway combinations, custom/WASM consumers where supported, and legacy fallback/capability behavior.
- [ ] Test UPDATE/CREATE/DELETE/MYSELF/REFRESH, null/empty/missing fields, authoritative empty snapshots and namespace isolation.
- [ ] Test divide/gRPC warmup timestamps, TCP selector naming, logging sampler fallback, MCP default tool names and relevant plugin handlers before declaring fields removable.
- [ ] Keep deletion/replacement correctness separate and intact, including #7815 and #7791; smaller messages must not retain deleted routes.
- [ ] Compare 1k/10k+ realistic payload shapes, with small and large handles/props. Measure JSON and compressed bytes, serialization/deserialization CPU, allocation/GC, synchronization/apply time and business-request p99 during sync.
- [ ] Record gateway/Admin revisions, JVM/configuration, commands and repeat-run variation. Keep only demonstrated benefits; do not extrapolate the synthetic size ratio into a universal latency claim.

## Related work and scope separation

- #7650: performance baseline/tracker.
- #7645: batching and invalidation while applying received namespace snapshots. This proposal reduces/defines the transmitted representation before application; the two changes should be benchmarked independently.
- #7815 / #7791: synchronization/cache correctness prerequisites, not payload-size optimizations.

No implementation changes have been made for this proposal. Consumer tracing and the standalone serialization-size experiment are the current evidence.

## Goal

Reduce intermediate JSON trees/maps, strings and repeated parsing while receiving large gateway configuration messages. Keep the existing data contract and sync correctness; this is separate from trimming payload fields in #7832.

## Current processing

The receiver currently follows:

```text
frame JSON
 -> raw WebsocketData / generic data objects
 -> data serialized back to JSON
 -> event fingerprint
 -> concrete typed DTO list parsed from JSON
```

- [ShenyuWebsocketClient.handleResult:440–474](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-sync-data-center/shenyu-sync-data-websocket/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/plugin/sync/data/websocket/client/ShenyuWebsocketClient.java#L440-L474) first calls fromJson(result, WebsocketData.class), then toJson(websocketData.getData()).
- [AbstractDataHandler.handle:84–102](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-sync-data-center/shenyu-sync-data-websocket/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/plugin/sync/data/websocket/handler/AbstractDataHandler.java#L84-L102) converts that JSON into the group-specific list.
- [WebsocketDataHandler:82–93](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-sync-data-center/shenyu-sync-data-websocket/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/plugin/sync/data/websocket/handler/WebsocketDataHandler.java#L82-L93) also constructs an eventType+JSON fingerprint input and hashes the complete payload.
- handleResult computes result.getBytes(UTF_8).length solely for its INFO size diagnostic, allocating a complete byte array even when the INFO call is disabled.

## Scope and acceptance

- [ ] Parse the envelope once and adapt its data directly to the group's typed representation, e.g. via an existing JSON element/type adapter; avoid a generic-object -> JSON-string -> typed-object round trip.
- [ ] Preserve group/event validation, namespace isolation, fullSnapshot and authoritative empty arrays, legacy MYSELF handling, initial-sync completion/failure state, and exception/reconnect behavior.
- [ ] Keep duplicate suppression correct across event types. If fingerprint input representation changes, specify equivalence and test field order, whitespace, numeric/string values, UPDATE/DELETE/MYSELF, snapshots and reconnect. Do not simply remove deduplication or hash only a subset of the identity.
- [ ] Avoid full-size byte-array allocation solely for disabled diagnostics; retain honest UTF-8 byte-size semantics if the log still says bytes. String.length() is not an equivalent byte count.
- [ ] Cover malformed input, all supported groups, timestamp/number fidelity and plugin handler callbacks with round-trip/regression tests.
- [ ] Compare 1k/10k+ configuration messages, unchanged repeats, incremental events and realistic large handles; measure deserialize/dispatch time, allocation and peak heap independently of #7832's field projection.

## Related work

#7832 changes which fields are transmitted; this task changes how the received representation is processed. #7645 owns batching while applying DTOs to caches. Neither requires this repeated JSON conversion.

## Baseline and validation boundary

Reviewed Apache ShenYu `2.7.2-SNAPSHOT`, master `04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac`. Source inspection confirms the processing described here; no before/after load benchmark has been run and no fixed performance gain is claimed. Use #7650's reproducible benchmark contract: warm JVM, identical configuration/resources, controlled payload shapes, repeated runs, CPU/allocation/GC, synchronization convergence and business-request p99 during sync. No new production dependency is required for this proposal.

body_text:
## Goal

Remove avoidable complete-message JSON processing and log volume from Admin's WebSocket send path, including when its INFO logging is disabled. Preserve useful operational diagnostics and existing message delivery.

## Current processing

[WebsocketCollector.send(namespaceId,...):336](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/listener/websocket/WebsocketCollector.java#L326-L357) passes maskSensitive(message) as an INFO argument. Java evaluates this method before the logger checks its level.

[maskSensitive():428–460](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/listener/websocket/WebsocketCollector.java#L428-L460) parses the entire message into maps/lists, recursively traverses it and serializes another complete JSON string. It is also called before the send path discovers that no matching sessions are present. Async logging does not remove this caller-side work.

## Scope and acceptance

- [ ] Log event metadata (namespace, group/type, item count, measured size and appropriate bounded diagnostics) for normal delivery rather than an entire payload. Reuse metadata available to the publisher instead of reparsing a large JSON solely to recover it.
- [ ] Any opt-in detailed diagnostic path must remain safely redacted and lazy/level-guarded. Do not optimize by logging the unredacted message.
- [ ] Verify that disabled INFO/detailed diagnostics do not invoke full-payload parsing/redaction/serialization. Preserve validation and delivery behavior even when logs are disabled.
- [ ] Exercise ordinary sends, initial synchronization, empty data, absent sessions and malformed diagnostic input. Keep request/sequence handling and send failure handling unchanged.
- [ ] Measure caller-thread CPU/allocation, log bytes/sec, queue pressure and sync/business p99 at equal traffic and log destinations for 1k/10k+ payloads.

## Related work

#7643 (closed) covered routine match-success diagnostics and the gateway receiver's full-payload logging. The current Admin collector still performs the explicit whole-message redaction/INFO operation above; this is the residual producer-side processing path, not a request to re-add an async appender or redo the already-fixed receiver log. #7832 owns compact wire DTOs; logging should not undo their gains by creating more complete message copies.

## Baseline and validation boundary

Reviewed Apache ShenYu `2.7.2-SNAPSHOT`, master `04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac`. Source inspection confirms the processing described here; no before/after load benchmark has been run and no fixed performance gain is claimed. Use #7650's reproducible benchmark contract: warm JVM, identical configuration/resources, controlled payload shapes, repeated runs, CPU/allocation/GC, synchronization convergence and business-request p99 during sync. No new production dependency is required for this proposal.

body_text:
## Goal

Evaluate a compatibility-safe structured payload representation for two envelopes that currently embed an already serialized JSON message as a string. Avoid another escaping/unescaping layer for large configuration data.

## Current representation

1. [WebsocketSyncFrame.payload:35](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-common/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/common/dto/WebsocketSyncFrame.java#L20-L46) is String. [WebsocketCollector:391–397](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/listener/websocket/WebsocketCollector.java#L391-L397) serializes a frame containing the complete configuration message string during opt-in initial sync.
2. [ClusterDataChangedEventPayload.source:40–43](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/model/dto/ClusterDataChangedEventPayload.java#L30-L48) is String. ClusterDataChangedEventForwarder serializes event.getSource() before RestTemplate serializes the envelope.

JSON syntax and existing escaped handle/config strings therefore pass through an additional string-escaping layer. This is a representation/performance task, not a claim that these valid JSON envelopes are currently malformed.

## Scope and acceptance

- [ ] Measure raw/compressed bytes and encode/decode allocation/CPU for current versus structured envelopes with realistic nested handle/props content. Do not assume a universal reduction ratio.
- [ ] Define a version/capability-compatible structured payload representation appropriate to each transport's serializer. Do not assume Gson and Jackson tree types are interchangeable without explicit adapters/tests.
- [ ] Keep INITIAL_SYNC_V1 and mixed-version Admin/gateway/cluster compatibility or provide an explicit negotiated replacement and tested legacy fallback. Do not silently change a String field into an object for existing consumers.
- [ ] Preserve requestId, sequence validation, connection ownership, ordered delivery and retry/failure handling. Initial-sync payload=null is a completion marker and must remain distinct from an empty configuration snapshot.
- [ ] Preserve group, event and namespace context, cluster authentication and after-commit dispatch. No change to the internal DataChangedEvent source is required by this task.
- [ ] Implement only after compatibility and benchmark results justify it; keep existing envelopes conceptually rather than introducing another generic event bus. Test WebSocket framing and Admin forwarding independently.

## Related work

#7716 concerns inconsistent encoding of instance-info reports; these are configuration/committed-event envelopes, not that reporting field. #7832 reduces gateway payload fields; this task removes redundant enclosing string encoding. Keep their benchmarks and rollout decisions separate.

## Baseline and validation boundary

Reviewed Apache ShenYu `2.7.2-SNAPSHOT`, master `04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac`. Source inspection confirms the processing described here; no before/after load benchmark has been run and no fixed performance gain is claimed. Use #7650's reproducible benchmark contract: warm JVM, identical configuration/resources, controlled payload shapes, repeated runs, CPU/allocation/GC, synchronization convergence and business-request p99 during sync. No new production dependency is required for this proposal.

[WebsocketSyncFrame.payload:35](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-common/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/common/dto/WebsocketSyncFrame.java#L20-L46) is String. [WebsocketCollector:391–397](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/listener/websocket/WebsocketCollector.java#L391-L397) serializes a frame containing the complete configuration message string during opt-in initial sync.
2. [ClusterDataChangedEventPayload.source:40–43](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/model/dto/ClusterDataChangedEventPayload.java#L30-L48) is String. ClusterDataChangedEventForwarder serializes event.getSource() before RestTemplate serializes the envelope.

JSON syntax and existing escaped handle/config strings therefore pass through an additional string-escaping layer. This is a representation/performance task, not a claim that these valid JSON envelopes are currently malformed.

## Scope and acceptance

- [ ] Measure raw/compressed bytes and encode/decode allocation/CPU for current versus structured envelopes with realistic nested handle/props content. Do not assume a universal reduction ratio.
- [ ] Define a version/capability-compatible structured payload representation appropriate to each transport's serializer. Do not assume Gson and Jackson tree types are interchangeable without explicit adapters/tests.
- [ ] Keep INITIAL_SYNC_V1 and mixed-version Admin/gateway/cluster compatibility or provide an explicit negotiated replacement and tested legacy fallback. Do not silently change a String field into an object for existing consumers.
- [ ] Preserve requestId, sequence validation, connection ownership, ordered delivery and retry/failure handling. Initial-sync payload=null is a completion marker and must remain distinct from an empty configuration snapshot.
- [ ] Preserve group, event and namespace context, cluster authentication and after-commit dispatch. No change to the internal DataChangedEvent source is required by this task.
- [ ] Implement only after compatibility and benchmark results justify it; keep existing envelopes conceptually rather than introducing another generic event bus. Test WebSocket framing and Admin forwarding independently.

## Related work

## Goal

Evaluate reducing repeated full-group cache regeneration during bursts of independent, committed configuration events in HTTP long-polling deployments. Preserve bounded notification latency, transaction visibility and event semantics.

## Current remaining work

[AbstractDataChangedListener.onRuleChanged():220–227](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/listener/AbstractDataChangedListener.java#L220-L227) groups one event by namespace and calls updateRuleCache. [updateRuleCache():392–393](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/listener/AbstractDataChangedListener.java#L385-L394) reloads all rules for that namespace. [updateCache():340–351](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/listener/AbstractDataChangedListener.java#L340-L351) serializes/hashes the complete list before it can skip an unchanged MD5. Selector and other group cache paths use the same pattern.

An already-batched event performs one rebuild per namespace; that behavior is correct and should remain. A burst of separate configuration requests/events can still perform repeated complete reloads even when only the final published cache state matters to long-poll readers.

## Important distinction from fixed work

#6576 was closed by PR #7181, which batches selector import data-sync events. Do not report a current 1,000-row selector import as producing 1,000 data-sync rebuilds without evidence: that path was fixed. This follow-up specifically evaluates multiple independent committed events, such as rapid edits by API clients, rather than undoing or duplicating import batching.

#6569 addressed the older global-lock/namespace refresh problem; this task is not a blanket increase of scheduler threads or reintroduction of global refresh. It applies to the HTTP/cache-listener path, not a claim that the WebSocket gateway itself queries the database per business request.

## Scope and acceptance

- [ ] Benchmark sustained and burst independent updates for one group/namespace, multiple groups and multiple namespaces; record DB queries, full serialization/hash counts, allocations, convergence and request p99.
- [ ] Evaluate a bounded dirty-key/rebuild generation mechanism or a measured short coalescing window at the cache/notification layer. Define the maximum added notification latency and overload behavior.
- [ ] Keep every business/audit/domain event and required plugin callback. Coalescing cache rebuild work must not blindly drop DELETE/UPDATE ordering or after-commit boundaries.
- [ ] Handle writes arriving during a rebuild: a generation/dirty state must ensure that the newest committed configuration is eventually published. Do not lose wakeups by clearing a pending marker too early.
- [ ] Preserve MD5/version comparison, long-poll wakeups, authoritative empty groups, rollback behavior and isolation between namespaces.
- [ ] Retain #7181's import batching and its tests; add concurrent independent-event and rollback tests. Keep current behavior where coalescing is disabled or not beneficial.
- [ ] Retain only measured benefit under an explicit convergence budget; publish commands and results.

## Related work

#7645 batches application of a received gateway snapshot. This task is producer-side HTTP cache rebuild work. #7832 trims transport fields, not database read/rebuild frequency.

## Baseline and validation boundary

Reviewed Apache ShenYu `2.7.2-SNAPSHOT`, master `04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac`. Source inspection confirms the processing described here; no before/after load benchmark has been run and no fixed performance gain is claimed. Use #7650's reproducible benchmark contract: warm JVM, identical configuration/resources, controlled payload shapes, repeated runs, CPU/allocation/GC, synchronization convergence and business-request p99 during sync. No new production dependency is required for this proposal.

## Goal

Reduce repeated whole-snapshot serialization, concatenation and reparsing during an enabled WebSocket reconciliation cycle, while preserving deterministic change detection and authoritative replacement.

## Current processing

[WebsocketDataReconciler.reconcileGroup():204–224](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/listener/websocket/WebsocketDataReconciler.java#L204-L224) currently performs:

```text
load DTOs
 -> serialize every row to String
 -> sort row JSON strings
 -> concatenate all rows into another String for MD5
 -> if changed, parse every row back into JsonElement
 -> serialize the complete WebsocketData again
```

Unchanged cycles still pay the load, per-row serialization, sort and large concatenated digest-input cost. Changed cycles add reparsing and final serialization. Reconciliation is opt-in; this task does not claim the disabled default performs this work. The existing active-namespace and master-only restrictions are useful and should be retained.

## Scope and acceptance

- [ ] Profile unchanged and changed cycles for realistic 1k/10k+ PLUGIN/SELECTOR/RULE groups with small and large handles; measure CPU, allocation, peak heap, DB reads, tick duration and business p99 disturbance.
- [ ] Evaluate reusing a canonical row/tree representation for digest and outgoing payload instead of serializing then reparsing each row. Avoid retaining more intermediate forms than the current approach.
- [ ] Evaluate incremental/streaming MessageDigest updates to avoid String.join of the entire snapshot. Preserve delimiter/order semantics or explicitly test/document a compatible digest migration.
- [ ] Preserve deterministic ordering and detection of row additions, deletions and field changes; do not replace the digest with an unsafe shortcut such as max(dateUpdated) that misses deletions or out-of-band changes.
- [ ] Preserve namespace/master gating, fullSnapshot metadata, authoritative empty data, failure retry and advancing the digest cursor only after the applicable publication outcome.
- [ ] Preserve reconciliation as a recovery mechanism for missed events/shared-DB changes. A cached last-seen event version alone is not an equivalent authoritative check.
- [ ] Run unchanged-order/changed-order equivalence, empty snapshot, serialization failure and publication failure regressions. Retain only a measured improvement with correct final gateway state.

## Related work

#7356 introduced shared-database convergence work. #7645 owns how gateways apply snapshots, #7832 owns field projection, and the receive-side JSON round-trip optimization is a separate stage. Benchmark these independently so a smaller payload does not hide redundant reconciliation processing.

## Baseline and validation boundary

Reviewed Apache ShenYu `2.7.2-SNAPSHOT`, master `04f7c2e8b7d282f14510157a9ab0bfaab538ecac`. Source inspection confirms the processing described here; no before/after load benchmark has been run and no fixed performance gain is claimed. Use #7650's reproducible benchmark contract: warm JVM, identical configuration/resources, controlled payload shapes, repeated runs, CPU/allocation/GC, synchronization convergence and business-request p99 during sync. No new production dependency is required for this proposal.

### Description

The existing MapUtilsTest in my base checkout covers transStringMap but does not cover computeIfAbsent.

I would like to add two unit tests:

- When the key already has a non-null value, return the existing value without invoking the mapping function.
- When the key is absent, invoke the mapping function, return its result, and store that result in the map.

This is a test-only change. No production code is modified.

I have prepared the tests on my fork and validated them with:

`.\mvnw.cmd -pl shenyu-common -am test "-Dtest=MapUtilsTest" "-Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false"`

Result: MapUtilsTest ran 3 tests with 0 failures, 0 errors and 0 skipped tests. The build passed.

body_text:
### Bug description

Automatic Swagger/OpenAPI document loading in Admin loses the upstream HTTP scheme. On current master (`9f57e930169404dd2d2e50b838bd651a18833924`), a discovery upstream with `protocol=https://` and `url=example.com:8443` produces a request to `http://example.com:8443/<context>/v3/api-docs`. Without an explicit port it also defaults to 80 instead of 443.

This affects both the initial scan (`loadApiDocument`) and discovery CREATE/UPDATE callbacks (`loadDocOnUpstreamChanged`). An HTTPS-only backend therefore fails automatic document loading even when its discovery configuration is correct.

### Reproduction and evidence

1. Enable the Admin API document loading dictionary flag.
2. Configure a divide upstream with `protocol=https://`, `url=example.com:8443` and selector name `/project`.
3. Trigger the initial scan or an upstream UPDATE event.
4. Observe an HTTP request to `http://example.com:8443/project/v3/api-docs`, rather than HTTPS.

A local regression test invokes the public loader entry points, runs the real PullSwaggerDocServiceImpl and HttpUtils request-building path, and records the outgoing OkHttp request with an application interceptor. Both entry points currently send HTTP for HTTPS inputs. The HTTP/default-protocol control cases pass. No external endpoint is contacted by this test.

### Cause and proposed scope

- Both upstream conversion paths in `LoadServiceDocEntryImpl` split the address on `:` and default missing ports to 80, discarding `DiscoveryUpstreamData.protocol`.
- `UpstreamInstance` has no scheme field.
- `PullSwaggerDocServiceImpl.getSwaggerRequestUrl` hard-codes `http`.

Preserve the upstream scheme through the internal instance object, retain HTTP as the default for existing callers, select 443 for HTTPS without an explicit port, and use the preserved scheme to construct the document request. Carry the same scheme into generated API document metadata so debug requests do not revert to HTTP. Use URI parsing locally for the document-loader conversion.

### Related work / boundaries

This is the automatic upstream-document loading path. It is distinct from manual Swagger URL import and its port/DNS policy (#7595, PR #7868), and is not established as the cause of #6362. PR #6456 also touches address parsing in LoadServiceDocEntryImpl for general IPv6 support; the document-loader URI parsing will need reconciliation if both changes land. This issue does not propose changes to gateway routing, TLS certificate validation or general discovery address normalization.

I am preparing a focused fix and regression coverage.

Automatic Swagger/OpenAPI document loading in Admin loses the upstream HTTP scheme. On current master (`9f57e930169404dd2d2e50b838bd651a18833924`), a discovery upstream with `protocol=https://` and `url=example.com:8443` produces a request to `http://example.com:8443/<context>/v3/api-docs`. Without an explicit port it also defaults to 80 instead of 443.

This affects both the initial scan (`loadApiDocument`) and discovery CREATE/UPDATE callbacks (`loadDocOnUpstreamChanged`). An HTTPS-only backend therefore fails automatic document loading even when its discovery configuration is correct.

### Reproduction and evidence

1. Enable the Admin API document loading dictionary flag.
2. Configure a divide upstream with `protocol=https://`, `url=example.com:8443` and selector name `/project`.
3. Trigger the initial scan or an upstream UPDATE event.
4. Observe an HTTP request to `http://example.com:8443/project/v3/api-docs`, rather than HTTPS.

A local regression test invokes the public loader entry points, runs the real PullSwaggerDocServiceImpl and HttpUtils request-building path, and records the outgoing OkHttp request with an application interceptor. Both entry points currently send HTTP for HTTPS inputs. The HTTP/default-protocol control cases pass. No external endpoint is contacted by this test.

### Cause and proposed scope

- Both upstream conversion paths in `LoadServiceDocEntryImpl` split the address on `:` and default missing ports to 80, discarding `DiscoveryUpstreamData.protocol`.
- `UpstreamInstance` has no scheme field.
- `PullSwaggerDocServiceImpl.getSwaggerRequestUrl` hard-codes `http`.

Preserve the upstream scheme through the internal instance object, retain HTTP as the default for existing callers, select 443 for HTTPS without an explicit port, and use the preserved scheme to construct the document request. Carry the same scheme into generated API document metadata so debug requests do not revert to HTTP. Use URI parsing locally for the document-loader conversion.

### Related work / boundaries

This is the automatic upstream-document loading path. It is distinct from manual Swagger URL import and its port/DNS policy (#7595, PR #7868), and is not established as the cause of #6362. PR #6456 also touches address parsing in LoadServiceDocEntryImpl for general IPv6 support; the document-loader URI parsing will need reconciliation if both changes land. This issue does not propose changes to gateway routing, TLS certificate validation or general discovery address normalization.

I am preparing a focused fix and regression coverage.

## Goal

Provide a read-only explanation of how a hypothetical request matches a selected gateway's current configuration. Operators should be able to answer why a request matched or missed a selector/rule without sending it to an upstream or inferring the decision from verbose logs.

Example: enter GET /orders/42 with headers/query values. Show the considered plugins, selector/rule conditions, priority decisions, default-rule behavior and final matching result, together with the configuration snapshot used for the explanation.

## First deliverable

- A diagnostic API and report model; an Admin UI can consume the same result in a coordinated follow-up.
- Input: URI, method, relevant headers/query/cookies and explicitly supported routing context.
- Select a gateway instance and identify its namespace, configuration source and available group revision/digest. Distinguish node-local configuration from Admin's desired configuration.
- Explain plugin enablement/order, selectors considered, each condition result, matching specificity/sort, chosen rule, default-rule behavior, and no-match cases.
- Report unsupported or unavailable context explicitly. Do not guess outcomes for arbitrary custom predicates, body-dependent logic, authentication decisions or remote calls.
- Show eligible upstream candidates and the configured load-balancing policy where available. Do not claim a hypothetical exact selection by advancing stateful round-robin counters or consuming circuit-breaker recovery probes.

## Execution boundaries

Reuse the production matching semantics, including compound conditions and RESTful matching; avoid a separately implemented approximation that drifts from the gateway. The diagnostic path must not execute normal plugin side effects, forward HTTP/RPC requests, change configuration, populate request-match caches, advance load-balancer counters, reserve breaker probes, or debit request/token budgets. Redact sensitive input values in stored/shared reports and bound input/report sizes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Match results agree with normal gateway matching for supported conditions on the same configuration snapshot.
- [ ] Cover exact/prefix/regex/pathPattern, mixed header/query conditions, AND/OR, enabled/disabled entries, specificity/sort, RESTful parameters and default rules.
- [ ] Explain both matched and unmatched cases, including which earlier candidate won and why.
- [ ] Same path with different headers/query values produces independently correct reports.
- [ ] Clearly label stale/unknown/unsupported context and config changes during an inspection; never present mixed snapshots as one atomic revision.
- [ ] Prove no outbound call and no mutation of matching/load-balancing/breaker/budget state.
- [ ] Namespace and selected-node isolation, bounded work and access control are tested.

## Existing implementation / boundaries

Reviewed against master `87c22dde7`. Matching currently lives in [AbstractShenyuPlugin](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/87c22dde7/shenyu-plugin/shenyu-plugin-base/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/plugin/base/AbstractShenyuPlugin.java); execution ordering lives in [ShenyuWebHandler](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/87c22dde7/shenyu-web/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/web/handler/ShenyuWebHandler.java).

This is an explanation/simulation feature, separate from sending a real debug request through SandboxService, from request tracing, and from #6081's matching-engine refactoring. Existing matching fixes should remain independent prerequisites rather than being duplicated here. No runtime implementation or performance gain is claimed by this proposal.

## Goal

Reduce manual configuration of Agent Gateway HTTP tools by generating supported tool plans from an OpenAPI definition and explicitly selected existing ShenYu HTTP routes. Import should produce a reviewable plan and explain unsupported operations before any configuration is published.

## Existing capability and distinction

Master `87c22dde7` already contains:

- [SwaggerImportServiceImpl.importMcpConfig](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/87c22dde7/shenyu-admin/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/admin/service/impl/SwaggerImportServiceImpl.java), which imports tool registrations for the existing MCP-server flow.
- [AgentGatewayHttpToolConfig](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/87c22dde7/shenyu-common/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/common/dto/AgentGatewayHttpToolConfig.java), which accepts explicitly named, bounded GET/POST HTTP tool plans.
- The Agent Gateway HTTP dispatch/registry path introduced by #7572.

This proposal targets generation of **Agent Gateway httpTools plans** and their rule permission bindings, not a second copy of the existing MCP-server Swagger importer or a new HTTP dispatch engine.

## MVP scope

1. Accept a supplied OpenAPI JSON document, reusing the existing parsing infrastructure where practical. Remote URL import, if included, must reuse the established import-fetch policy.
2. Select a namespace, existing gateway routes and operations; require an explicit method/path mapping. Do not infer backend-only paths as gateway routes.
3. Generate stable suggested tool names/descriptions, the currently supported inputSchema subset, requestTemplate and argsPosition; reconcile these names with the rule's allowedTools.
4. Start with literal GET/POST routes and supported flat scalar query/JSON-body arguments. Produce a per-operation unsupported report for path templates, arrays/nested schemas, unsupported constraints/media types, header/cookie parameters, ambiguous names and other unrepresentable mappings. Do not silently flatten, discard constraints or invent a weaker contract.
5. Preview additions/updates/removals and name collisions against startup-local, remote and configured HTTP tool namespaces. Publish only explicitly selected valid plans through existing Admin configuration APIs.
6. Make repeated import of the same source/mapping idempotent. Preserve explicitly managed/manual configuration, and require a visible deletion plan for operations removed from the source.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Generated plans pass both the Admin rule validator and gateway AgentGatewayHttpToolConfig parser.
- [ ] Supported OpenAPI versions and schema subset are documented and tested; unsupported operations cannot silently become enabled tools.
- [ ] Required/optional scalar parameters, GET query values, POST query/body values, reserved characters and UTF-8 are preserved end to end.
- [ ] Query/body name collisions, duplicate operation IDs, invalid tool names and existing-provider collisions have actionable diagnostics.
- [ ] Preview/generation does not publish configuration or expose every imported operation automatically.
- [ ] Re-import, manual edits, source removals and namespace isolation have defined behavior.
- [ ] Tests verify generated tools through the ordinary gateway routing chain, including final upstream URI and JSON result handling.

The current HTTP tool path restrictions and private-header/session semantics remain authoritative. Extending that execution contract is a separate decision, not something the importer should bypass. Coordinate relevant integration fixes such as #7909 rather than reproducing their implementation in the generator.

## Goal

Support multiple developers running instances of the same service without maintaining a complete duplicate set of selectors/rules for each developer.

Example: a request carrying an operator-defined developer identity should prefer developer A's user-service instance when A overrides that service, while order-service continues through the configured shared/default pool. The behavior for an absent or unhealthy personal instance must be explicit and observable.

## Reuse and boundaries

- The user scenario is described in #6238; that issue is a question rather than an implementation/acceptance tracker.
- Master `87c22dde7` propagates discovered upstream labels (#7847); reuse this model and the existing load-balancing/discovery path.
- PR #6317 already implements generic Divide gray routing. Coordinate/reuse that engine rather than creating a competing gray load balancer or duplicating its configuration fields.

The new deliverable is a developer-profile workflow and a clearly defined per-service isolation/fallback policy on top of these capabilities.

## MVP scope

- Define one profile convention: an operator-controlled request identity source, a discovery label key and the services a profile overrides. The request may select only configured profiles/registered upstreams, not an arbitrary upstream address.
- Configure the policy once per service/namespace. Developers should not copy every selector and rule merely to add their own instance.
- For overridden services, select healthy matching upstreams and retain the configured balancing policy within that subset.
- Define fallback explicitly: shared/default pool versus strict no-match failure. Specify whether other developer-labelled instances are eligible; do not silently cross profiles.
- Services not overridden by the profile retain ordinary configured routing.
- Expose a diagnostic reason for profile match, shared fallback and strict miss. Keep diagnostics bounded and avoid unbounded per-developer metric labels.
- Start with documented REST/configuration operations and a runnable example. Coordinate an optional Dashboard flow using the same contract.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A/B/shared user-service instances coexist; requests for A and B reach their intended instances.
- [ ] An unrelated service follows the normal shared routing policy without a per-developer duplicate configuration.
- [ ] Missing, unhealthy, removed and restarted personal instances follow the declared fallback/strict policy.

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I searched open/closed issues and PRs for gRPC backpressure, streaming, buffering and flow control; I did not find an equivalent report.

### Current Behavior

`ShenyuGrpcClient.invoke()` sends CLIENT_STREAMING and BIDI_STREAMING requests by traversing the entire request list:

```java
requestObserver = asyncClientStreamingCall(createCall(callParams), compositeObserver);
requestList.forEach(requestObserver::onNext);
requestObserver.onCompleted();
```

The bidi branch uses the same loop. Neither branch observes `ClientCallStreamObserver.isReady()` or resumes sending through an `onReadyHandler`.

grpc-java still provides HTTP/2 transport flow control. However, `StreamObserver.onNext()` can enqueue a message before the peer can consume it; ignoring readiness can create additional outbound buffering when the backend reads slowly. This is a missing application-level sending policy, not evidence that HTTP/2 flow control is absent or that an OOM has occurred.

The request JSON is already materialized as a list before this loop. A readiness-aware drain would bound additional sending work; it would not by itself bound the original HTTP request body/list.

### Expected Behavior

Drain pending client/bidi requests according to gRPC outbound readiness, preserving message order, termination and existing RPC semantics.

### Evidence

- [Request materialization](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/87c22dde7be14c1c3755440a4d8b082a86d10a87/shenyu-plugin/shenyu-plugin-proxy/shenyu-plugin-rpc/shenyu-plugin-grpc/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/plugin/grpc/client/ShenyuGrpcClient.java#L80-L84).
- [CLIENT_STREAMING/BIDI_STREAMING send loops](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/87c22dde7be14c1c3755440a4d8b082a86d10a87/shenyu-plugin/shenyu-plugin-proxy/shenyu-plugin-rpc/shenyu-plugin-grpc/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/plugin/grpc/client/ShenyuGrpcClient.java#L148-L157).
- grpc-java 1.65.1's [`CallStreamObserver.isReady()` contract](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-java/blob/v1.65.1/stub/src/main/java/io/grpc/stub/CallStreamObserver.java) explains that ignoring readiness can cause excessive internal buffering.

### Suggested Verification and Acceptance

- [ ] Capture the actual client call observer through the supported client-observer lifecycle; use `isReady`/`onReady` or an equivalent bounded mechanism.
- [ ] When readiness is false, pause the drain; resume after readiness becomes true, checking readiness again during the callback.
- [ ] Preserve order and exactly-once delivery to `onNext`; invoke `onCompleted` only after pending messages have been submitted.
- [ ] Stop pending sends on termination/cancellation, and serialize drain work to prevent duplicate sends from reentrant/concurrent readiness callbacks.
- [ ] Add deterministic tests that alternate ready/not-ready states, including termination while requests remain. Keep unary/server-streaming behavior unchanged.
- [ ] Exercise a slow-reading backend with a large finite request list; record pending work, memory and convergence. Do not replace the loop with an unbounded executor/queue.

### Environment and Validation Boundary

Reviewed ShenYu `2.7.2-SNAPSHOT`, master `87c22dde7be14c1c3755440a4d8b082a86d10a87`, grpc-java `1.65.1`. This report is based on source inspection and the installed official grpc-java source. The slow-backend scenario above is proposed validation; no load benchmark or production failure was reproduced.

The [separate response-aggregation issue](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/issues/7928) concerns received results and the HTTP response contract. WebSocket forwarding uses a separate reactive `receive -> send` bridge and is outside this report.

body_text:
## Goal
Allow an operator to drain a running gateway instance for maintenance or rollout, observe remaining work, and resume admission without restarting the process.

## Existing capabilities and boundary
Build on the existing Spring/Netty shutdown lifecycle. This proposal does not claim ShenYu has no graceful shutdown. #7718 covers readiness/liveness and optional draining **reporting**; this issue owns the runtime admission and draining behavior behind that reported state. Admin presence or a successful command send must not imply that a gateway has finished draining.

## Initial scope
- Define an opt-in, instance-scoped serving -> draining -> drained lifecycle, plus explicit resume and a deadline. A drain operation has an identity and observable progress.
- Mark readiness unavailable and stop admitting new business requests while allowing health/management traffic needed to operate the instance. Account for load-balancer propagation delay: readiness alone does not prevent requests on existing keep-alive connections.
- Track admitted HTTP requests and long-lived SSE/WebSocket sessions until completion or cancellation. Define upgrade races and the policy for closing remaining sessions at the deadline.
- Reuse lifecycle hooks for process shutdown where appropriate. Document integration with the ingress/load balancer rather than promising immediate external deregistration.
- Start with an authenticated gateway management operation; any Admin trigger must identify namespace, instance and boot generation, authorize the action and obtain a gateway acknowledgement.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An opt-in fixture drains one of two gateways under HTTP, SSE and WebSocket traffic; existing work follows the documented policy and new business requests receive a documented response.
- [ ] Races between admission, upgrade, drain, cancellation and resume cannot leak counters or admit work after the defined boundary.
- [ ] Repeated commands are idempotent; stale commands from a previous boot do not affect a replacement instance. Restart behavior is explicit.
- [ ] The deadline bounds waiting and releases resources; interrupted clients and non-terminating streams are covered.
- [ ] Management remains reachable, progress distinguishes requested/active/completed/expired, and resume restores readiness only when other readiness checks pass.
- [ ] Disabled mode preserves existing request behavior. Document retry implications for rejected non-idempotent requests.

Related: #7718 (reporting), #7719 (acknowledgement semantics). This is a feature proposal, not a measured availability improvement.

## Goal
Protect an upstream from rising concurrency when its latency degrades, and recover capacity gradually when it becomes healthy. Connection-pool sizing alone is not a feedback-based admission policy.

## Existing capabilities and boundary
#7644 and PR #7684 concern connection-pool/pending-acquisition capacity. Reuse those limits and the existing fault-tolerance/metrics extension points; this feature should not introduce a second connection pool or replace static rate limiting. A latency controller is a proposal to evaluate, not an assertion of measured throughput gains.

## MVP
- Offer an opt-in per-upstream-group controller with configured minimum/maximum concurrency, initial limit, sampling interval, minimum sample count and conservative recovery behavior.
- Begin with observation mode: compute a recommended limit and expose decisions without rejecting traffic. Document the chosen feedback algorithm before enabling enforcement.
- In enforcement mode, admit only within the current limit with a documented overload response. Prefer immediate rejection initially; any queue must have a finite size and deadline.
- Define the measured interval, treatment of retries, timeouts, errors and cancellations, and exclusion of local admission/queue delay from upstream latency samples.
- Start with non-streaming HTTP and a per-gateway limit. Explicitly document aggregate exposure across replicas; SSE/WebSocket/AI stream occupancy needs a separate policy before support.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Controlled healthy, slow, failing and recovering upstream scenarios demonstrate bounded in-flight work and stable convergence without sustained oscillation.
- [ ] Sparse traffic, insufficient samples and controller cold starts retain a documented safe limit; changes stay within configured bounds.
- [ ] Completion, error and cancellation release permits exactly once. Rule removal/configuration changes do not strand permits or grow controller state indefinitely.
- [ ] Observe-only and disabled modes preserve routing behavior; enforcement reports bounded decision/rejection metrics and does not block event-loop threads.
- [ ] Compare against static concurrency and existing bounded pools using #7650: successful throughput, upstream latency, gateway p99, rejection rate, CPU and memory. Report regressions as well as gains.
- [ ] Document interactions with retries, circuit breakers and horizontally scaled gateways; do not claim a cluster-wide hard limit.

Related: #7644, PR #7684 and #7650.

## Goal
Give a request one gateway-owned time budget so queueing, plugin external calls, retries and upstream attempts cannot each independently consume a full timeout after earlier work has used the available time.

## Existing capabilities and boundary
HTTP/AI calls already have timeout and retry settings. #7560 addresses WASM execution deadlines and memory limits. This proposal coordinates remaining time across the request chain; it does not replace those component limits or claim that reactive cancellation can forcibly stop arbitrary synchronous code.

## MVP
- Create a request-scoped monotonic deadline from explicit gateway configuration. Start at admission and make remaining time available through a small shared runtime contract.
- For each supported queue/external call/retry, use the smaller of its existing configured limit and the remaining request budget; do not begin a new attempt after expiry.
- Start with the standard non-streaming HTTP forwarding path and enumerate supported plugin integrations. Report unsupported boundaries honestly rather than claiming universal enforcement.
- Specify optional inbound/outbound deadline propagation separately. Untrusted client headers cannot extend the configured maximum; wall-clock timestamps must not become the local elapsed-time clock.
- Define expiry before/after response commitment, cancellation cleanup and fallback behavior. Streaming must explicitly distinguish time-to-first-response, idle timeout and maximum session lifetime; avoid applying a short buffered-response deadline to SSE/WebSocket by accident.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A fixture with queue delay, a plugin call and retried upstream attempts shares one finite budget; timeout settings cannot multiply the elapsed allowance.
- [ ] Retry/backoff uses remaining time and stops on expiry or downstream cancellation. Connection acquisition and in-flight resource cleanup are verified on the actual supported clients.
- [ ] Expiry before headers produces a documented result; expiry after commitment terminates according to the protocol without attempting to rewrite committed headers.
- [ ] Monotonic timing, zero/invalid budgets, nested calls and unavailable propagation metadata have defined tests.
- [ ] Metrics distinguish budget exhaustion from component timeout without request-ID/path label explosion.
- [ ] Disabled mode remains compatible; document unsupported synchronous execution and stream semantics.

Related: #7560 (WASM-specific enforcement), #7644 (bounded connection acquisition), #7650 (validation).

body_text:
## Goal
Validate a candidate upstream against live request shapes by sending an opt-in sample to a shadow destination and comparing outcomes while the primary response remains authoritative.

## Existing capabilities and boundary
#6108 and PR #6393 cover HTTP recording/replay. Reuse their bounded capture and request representation where suitable; this proposal adds online shadow execution, pairing and response differences rather than another recording platform.

## MVP
- Begin with explicitly allowlisted, replay-safe non-streaming HTTP requests. Read-only methods are a useful default, not proof that a target has no side effects. Writes require explicit route/target authorization and a documented safety strategy.
- Configure an independent shadow target, credentials, sample rate, concurrency, queue, body-size and time limits. Handle target selection through established upstream restrictions and do not automatically forward production secrets.
- Keep dispatch and comparison outside the primary response dependency. A slow or failing shadow cannot delay or replace the primary response; overload drops shadow work with a reason.
- Compare status, an allowlisted set of headers, bounded JSON/body representations and separately measured latency. Support explicit normalization/ignored fields for timestamps and nondeterministic IDs.
- Export bounded summaries and representative redacted differences through existing observability facilities. No unbounded body retention or new general-purpose analytics store.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Primary status/headers/body are unchanged with a healthy, slow, failing or unavailable shadow. Measure primary-path overhead under #7650.
- [ ] Tests cover sampling, queue overflow, body-size limits, cancellation, binary/non-JSON responses, decompression limits and malformed shadow responses.
- [ ] Streaming/SSE/WebSocket and non-replayable bodies are skipped with a clear reason in the first version.
- [ ] Request/response correlation remains correct under concurrency; comparison expiry and shutdown release buffers and queued work.
- [ ] Auth/tenant boundaries and redaction are enforced before export. Destination credentials and production cookies/tokens cannot leak through default copying.
- [ ] Difference summaries distinguish mismatch, normalization, truncation, skipped comparison and shadow failure.

Related: #6108, PR #6393 and #7650. This proposal does not promise identical responses from inherently nondeterministic services.

## Goal
Allow operators to explain AI usage and estimated cost by tenant/application, provider and actual model, then reconcile those records with provider reports.

## Existing capabilities and boundary
#7702 and PR #7848 own token-budget reservations and settlement. #7911 addresses missing Responses-protocol usage accounting. Reuse normalized usage and settlement observations; do not implement a second admission counter or present reserved estimates as actual billed usage.

## MVP
- Define a versioned usage event: namespace/authorized tenant/application, provider, requested/resolved model where known, operation/attempt identity, timestamps, protocol, final outcome and available token categories.
- Distinguish provider-reported usage, estimated usage, reported zero and unavailable usage. Record attempted upstream work separately from the final logical request so retries/fallback costs are attributable without double counting.
- Attach a versioned operator-supplied price schedule with effective dates, currency and supported categories (for example input, output and cached tokens). Preserve the price version and raw normalized quantities needed to recompute an estimate.
- Add bounded asynchronous delivery to a pluggable ledger sink and basic aggregation/export. Define delivery guarantees, idempotency keys, retention and failure visibility; do not block gateway traffic on a remote billing database.
- Begin with one documented provider/protocol and fixed token pricing. Reconciliation against provider exports can be a follow-up; negotiated discounts, taxes and unsupported pricing must remain explicit unknowns.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Buffered and streaming success, failure, cancellation, missing usage, retry and fallback cases create correctly scoped records with no false exact cost.
- [ ] Duplicate delivery is idempotent within a documented retention window; queue overflow/crash loss is observable and the delivery guarantee is stated honestly.
- [ ] Historical estimates retain their original price version; revaluation produces a separate auditable result rather than silently rewriting history.
- [ ] Tenant authorization applies to queries/exports. Prompts, responses and credentials are excluded by default; event volume, cardinality and retention are bounded.
- [ ] Usage extraction is shared with existing accounting and tested across supported formats, including #7911's protocol distinction.
- [ ] A small fixture reconciles ledger totals, attempts and price calculations against known inputs; unavailable pricing is never displayed as zero cost.

Related: #7702, PR #7848 and #7911. Cost values are estimates unless a provider reconciliation establishes otherwise.
