body_text:
## Goal
Make MCP tool schema changes reviewable and allow clients/operators to select a known contract before a changing remote tool breaks an agent workflow.

## Existing capabilities and boundary
Agent Gateway already has remote catalog refresh, schema validation and generation fencing. Extend those capabilities with immutable contract snapshots and evolution workflows; do not replace catalog refresh or confuse a refresh generation with an externally stable contract version. #6365 concerns client-admin registration protocols, not MCP tool contracts.

## MVP
- Snapshot each tool's identity and the input/output schema and capability metadata actually exposed by the supported MCP implementation. Use a stable digest/canonical representation and retain source/generation provenance.
- Show structural differences and classify a conservative subset: removed tool, newly required input, removed accepted input/enum value or incompatible type. Treat unknown JSON Schema constructs as requiring review rather than claiming a complete compatibility theorem.
- Allow an operator to approve and pin an exposed tool contract/version. Define tool listing/call behavior when the source changes or a pinned contract becomes unavailable.
- Store bounded, redacted regression examples for schema validation. Actual tool execution is opt-in and needs a safe test target; a matching schema is not proof of unchanged semantics.
- Integrate with existing catalog publication and generation fencing so lists, validators and invocations observe a coherent approved generation.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Tests cover additive/required/type/enum/removal changes and unsupported schema features, with explicit backward-compatibility direction.
- [ ] Canonically equivalent schemas do not generate spurious versions; snapshot history and per-tool/example sizes have retention limits.
- [ ] Concurrent refresh/pin/unpin does not mix tool metadata and validators from different generations.
- [ ] A pinned snapshot does not pretend to restore an old remote implementation. If the provider cannot serve the pinned contract, calls fail with a documented compatibility/unavailability result or an explicitly configured adapter.
- [ ] Tenant/namespace permissions apply to history, pinning and examples; credentials and private source metadata are redacted.
- [ ] Existing unpinned behavior remains compatible; legacy tools without output schemas are represented accurately.

Related: #7923 (OpenAPI-derived HTTP tool plan preview), #6365 (separate registration protocol work). This is contract governance, not general remote-service version control.

## Description

Track the remaining Agent Gateway/MCP capabilities needed to complete the current delivery roadmap. The preceding protocol, identity, request/terminal-context and interop work is development-complete. This does not assert that every related PR has merged: #7860, #7864 and #7921 were still open when checked. Reuse their accepted contracts and coordinate the integration baseline rather than rebuilding those features or silently depending on unpublished changes.

## Remaining task list

### Governance and reliability (P1-06 to P1-10)

- [ ] P1-06 Unified invocation auditing: #7950 - one correlated, privacy-preserving decision/terminal audit record per logical invocation. Requires the completed identity and request/terminal-context contracts.
- [ ] P1-07 Resource admission: #7951 - local, global and per-server in-flight limits with bounded queues. Requires the request/terminal-context and runtime-observability contracts.
- [ ] P1-08 Catalog recovery: #7952 - managed catalog freshness, bounded refresh, recovery and credential re-resolution. Requires #7951; coordinate with #7935 without implementing contract pinning here.
- [ ] P1-09 HTTPS connectivity: #7953 - controlled DNS/service-discovery targets and credential rotation/revocation. Requires #7951 and the completed protocol/identity boundaries.
- [ ] P1-10 Session recovery: #7954 - remote session expiry/404 recovery and verified legacy session-level gaps. Requires #7951 and #7952.

### Metering, policy and quotas (P1-11 to P1-14)

- [ ] P1-11 Usage metering: #7955 - shared per-attempt, protocol-aware LLM usage collection. Requires #7950 and the completed request/terminal-context contracts; coordinate with #7911 and PR #7937.
- [ ] P1-11 Cost acceptance (reuse): #7934 - existing versioned pricing, usage ledger and estimated cost attribution. Together with #7955, this completes the metering/cost capability. Do not create a second ledger.
- [ ] P1-12 Decision contract: #7956 - shared shadow/enforce, reason-code, audit and metric semantics. Requires #7950; execution integration ships with #7957 and #7958.
- [ ] P1-13 MCP quotas: #7957 - distributed tenant/subject invocation and concurrency admission. Requires #7951 and #7956; reuse #7950 audit vocabulary.
- [ ] P1-14 Token/cost budgets: #7958 - identity-scoped multidimensional token/cost budgets beyond the existing reservation foundation. Requires accepted #7955 and #7934, #7956 and the #7702 / PR #7848 foundation. Reuse #7957 atomic-admission lessons without creating another settlement store.

### Lower-priority capability (P2/P3)

- [ ] P2-16 Prompts aggregation: #7959 - authorized local and remote prompts list/get with bounded aggregation. Requires #7951 and #7952; SDK migration is a prerequisite only when its trigger is demonstrated.

The checkboxes track accepted delivery, not issue creation. Shared prerequisites may be designed in parallel, but feature publication must state unmerged dependencies. Each child issue includes background, reuse boundaries, implementation scope, non-goals, acceptance criteria, tests and dependencies.

## Existing ownership and reuse

- #7934 owns the usage ledger, versioned pricing and estimated cost attribution. #7911 and PR #7937 own the OpenAI Responses usage bug. Additional work must be limited to shared protocol-aware per-attempt metering and integration gaps.
- #7702 and PR #7848 own opt-in token reservations and reconciliation. Reuse that foundation; only identity-scoped, multidimensional token/cost policy and shadow/enforce integration belong to the follow-up.
- Catalog freshness/recovery is separate from #7935 contract diffs, approval and pinning. A refresh generation is not a stable tool-contract version.
- Existing resources PR #7669 is independent earlier work and is not a newly scheduled implementation.

## Conditional and deferred work

- P2-15 SDK migration: no implementation task until a selected protocol/client compatibility requirement or dependency-maintenance requirement is demonstrated. Assess MCP BOM, Spring AI and Java/Spring compatibility and public replacements for private reflection; an upgrade alone does not prove compatibility or remove reflection. Reprioritize before a dependent feature only when triggered.
- P3-17 Additional resources capability: defer new resources work until a concrete file/knowledge-base use case identifies a gap beyond existing resources work. Do not recreate #7669 or assume its existence completes every future resources requirement.

## Tracking rules

One coherent feature per implementation PR; explicit dependencies; no assignees set by this tracker. Keep authentication, authorization and base resource protection independent of shadow mode. Extend the existing interop regression matrix rather than creating a competing harness. No checkbox is completed merely because code is proposed or an issue is linked.

Repository evidence baseline: master `87c22dde7be14c1c3755440a4d8b082a86d10a87`; open PRs are proposals until merged and verified. Spring AI is a reuse instruction where applicable, not a reason to replace the current native AI Proxy paths.

## Repository metadata follow-up

Only existing labels were requested: `type: enhancement` for this tracker and its children; `mcp` for the tracker and MCP/governance children; `plugin:ai` for #7955 and #7958. Creation succeeded but GitHub did not retain the labels. A direct labels request returned HTTP 403, so a maintainer must apply them; no new labels or assignees were created.

The native sub-issue attachment endpoint returned HTTP 404. The Markdown checklist, child-to-parent links and explicit dependency links above are the active tracking structure; native parent-child metadata is not claimed.

## Design gates retained for implementation

- #7953 must establish the concrete approved hostname/discovery and revocation policy before expanding network access.
- #7955 and #7934 must agree the shared usage event and actual provider/protocol acceptance matrix; choose an operator-owned price source, currency and versioning policy for cost acceptance. Unsupported routes are not assumed implemented.
- #7957 and #7958 must document quota dimensions, Redis-outage behavior and soft-budget exposure before enforcement. Existing contributors retain ownership of #7911/#7937 and #7702/#7848.
- SDK migration needs an evidenced protocol/client or maintenance trigger; additional resources work needs a concrete unmet resource-reading use case. Neither has an implementation issue scheduled here.

body_text:
## Background

Parent #7949. This task belongs to the unified governance layer. Metrics and traces do not replace a correlated, privacy-preserving decision and terminal audit record, especially for requests rejected before execution.

## Existing capabilities and reuse

Reuse the logging SPI/collectors, trusted identity, immutable request context and terminal observations from the completed identity, context and observability work (#7811, #7827, #7860, #7921). Reuse existing queue/drop instrumentation (#7687), not another logging delivery subsystem. At the research baseline those later context/observability PRs remained open; integrate against their final merged contracts.

## Implementation scope

- Define a versioned audit record containing trusted tenant/subject, internal API-key identifier when available, target/model/tool, configuration and policy versions, decision, bounded reason code, terminal status and correlation identifiers.
- Emit one terminal record per logical invocation, including authentication, authorization and admission rejection before upstream execution. Correlate separate upstream-attempt records without counting them as additional logical calls.
- Use bounded nonblocking delivery through existing logging extension points. Specify queue capacity, overflow and drop visibility, sink-error handling, shutdown behavior and the actual delivery guarantee.
- Omit prompts, arguments, response bodies and credentials by default. Do not use W3C trace IDs as identity or raw API keys as identifiers.

## Non-goals

A new authorization server, a billing or usage ledger (owned by #7934), guaranteed lossless remote delivery, body logging, or replacing existing metrics and tracing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Success, failure, timeout, cancellation and pre-execution rejection have correctly correlated, tenant-isolated records with one logical terminal event.
- [ ] Retry and fallback attempts retain separate identities; late or duplicate terminal callbacks do not duplicate logical completion.
- [ ] Queue saturation and sink failures are observable and never block gateway event loops or leak sensitive data.
- [ ] Record schema, retention and delivery limitations, configuration and reason-code semantics are documented.

## Tests

Unit tests for record mapping, redaction and terminal idempotence; concurrent Reactor-context isolation tests; a real logging-sink fixture covering slow or failing sinks, queue overflow and shutdown; regression tests confirming unchanged response status/body and existing logging metrics.

## Dependencies

Completed identity, context and observability contracts; #7860 and #7921 integration availability. #7955 and #7956 consume this record and decision vocabulary; they must not introduce competing audit records.

body_text:
## Background

Parent #7949. This task belongs to resource isolation and predictable admission. Per-request byte and deadline bounds and an individual transport cap do not bound total work across local providers and remote servers.

## Existing capabilities and reuse

At master `87c22dde7`, `RequestScopedMcpClient` has `MAX_IN_FLIGHT=64` and bounded requests; `RemoteCatalogLifecycle` already supports bounded parallel discovery. Retain existing deadline and response-byte protection and the legacy server response-capture guard. Reuse existing resource and fault-tolerance facilities where their semantics fit; do not replace transport pools.

## Implementation scope

- Add local-provider, gateway-wide and per-remote-server in-flight admission limits with bounded, deadline-aware queueing and explicit overload outcomes.
- Make only necessary fixed limits configurable through trusted configuration, validating defaults, hard maxima and invalid updates in Admin and runtime.
- Release permits exactly once on every terminal path; bound queued work, concurrent discovery and connection exposure and aggregate retained response memory. Define isolation so one failing or slow server cannot consume all capacity.
- Keep `tools/call` non-replaying by default. Reuse circuit breaking only with an explicit side-effect-safe contract; HTTP GET retries do not authorize tool retries.

## Non-goals

Distributed business quotas (tracked by #7957), a new connection pool, automatic tool replay, or latency-adaptive concurrency (separately tracked by #7930). This task owns deterministic resource caps and bounded queues, not that adaptive controller.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Local and remote load cannot exceed configured global or per-server in-flight and queue limits; queue deadlines include time already spent waiting.
- [ ] Error, cancellation, timeout, configuration removal and shutdown release permits and queued references without double release.
- [ ] Invalid configuration is rejected consistently; runtime updates cannot bypass hard bounds.
- [ ] Slow, failing-server and parallel-refresh fixtures demonstrate bounded connections and memory and unaffected independent targets within documented shared-capacity limits.
- [ ] Rejections and in-flight state use bounded runtime metrics, with operational defaults and sizing guidance.

## Tests

Deterministic concurrent admission, cancellation and update tests; actual HTTP MCP fixtures for slow, large and failing upstreams; multi-request memory and connection measurements with stated limits rather than unsupported performance claims; legacy response-bound and no-replay regressions.

## Dependencies

Completed request/terminal-context and runtime-observability contracts (#7860 and #7921 integration baseline). #7952, #7953, #7954 and #7957 build on these bounds. Coordinate with #7930 without duplicating its algorithm or rollout.

## Background

Parent #7949. This task belongs to managed catalog operability. Configuration-triggered publication alone does not provide a bounded production freshness and recovery policy.

## Existing capabilities and reuse

At master `87c22dde7`, `RemoteCatalogLifecycle` supports ordered parallel refresh with concurrency 1-8; `ManagedRemoteMcpCatalog` constructs the default serial lifecycle and already has a bounded control queue, revision fencing, credential resolution and failure diagnostics. ## Background

Parent #7949. This task belongs to production outbound connectivity. Production MCP services may require controlled HTTPS hostnames and operational credential rotation, beyond fixed-IP targets.

## Existing capabilities and reuse

At master `87c22dde7`, `RemoteTransportPolicy` explicitly rejects DNS-based targets and uses direct connections; `RemoteServerBinding` and credential resolvers bind service credentials to trusted endpoints. Reuse these boundaries and configuration synchronization. Do not forward caller credentials or diagnostic subjects to remote servers. Related #6471 concerns separate AI Proxy client credential-cache isolation, not this MCP transport extension.

## Implementation scope

- Support approved HTTPS DNS and service-discovery targets with one coherent policy for resolution, allowed addresses, actual connection destination, TLS hostname/SNI and certificate validation. Enforce the policy at connection time, not merely URL parsing.
- Bound DNS resolution and re-resolution, connection attempts and discovery results; defend against DNS rebinding and unauthorized address changes, including pooled-connection behavior.
- Preserve independent target-bound credentials; define versioned rotation and emergency revocation semantics for new and in-flight requests, cached bindings and pooled clients. Never publish secrets in configuration diagnostics or metrics.
- Keep fixed-IP compatibility and redirects disabled. Document trusted configuration, rejection semantics and deployment requirements.

## Non-goals

Arbitrary URL fetching, permissive TLS or trust-all, delegated OAuth, unrestricted enterprise proxies, IPv6 expansion without an actual requirement, or a new service-discovery platform.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] DNS allowlist, connected address and TLS/SNI validation agree; rejected or changed destinations cannot bypass policy through retries or connection reuse.
- [ ] Invalid or untrusted certificates and hostname mismatches fail closed.
- [ ] Rotation and revocation have documented, tested new and in-flight semantics without cross-target secret reuse.
- [ ] Fixed-IP paths remain compatible; unauthorized configuration is rejected in Admin and runtime.

## Tests

Controlled DNS and rebinding fixtures with real TLS MCP endpoints; SAN, hostname and certificate failures; pool reuse and address-change races; credential rotation and revocation with concurrent calls; cancellation, timeouts and secret-redaction regression. Use test CA configuration only in fixtures, never weaken production validation.

## Dependencies

Completed protocol and trusted-identity contracts, plus #7951; coordinate credential refresh with #7952. Resolve the concrete approved domain and discovery deployment policy during design before broadening outbound access.

## Background

Parent #7949. This task belongs to outbound session lifecycle management. Remote session lifetime is different from request cleanup. Agent Gateway ingress remains stateless.

## Existing capabilities and reuse

At master `87c22dde7`, `RequestScopedMcpClient` retains an optional upstream `MCP-Session-Id`, cancels tracked requests and performs session deletion on close, but non-2xx responses (including 404) follow the generic upstream-error path. Reuse request isolation and the legacy pending-request, duplicate-ID and disconnect fixes (#7638); those are not new work in this issue.

## Implementation scope

- Detect protocol-defined remote session expiry and 404; invalidate only the affected binding and safely reinitialize for subsequent eligible work, with bounded or coalesced recovery and catalog generation checks.
- Never replay an already-issued `tools/call` during recovery. Return an explicit outcome for that invocation and avoid claiming the remote side effect did not occur.
- Define idle reclamation, close deadlines and failure isolation so one failed cleanup cannot block other targets or leak all generations.
- For supported deployments using the legacy MCP Server, first inventory existing session-level caps and TTL/idle behavior; fill only verified gaps and document maximum sessions and multi-replica routing constraints.

## Non-goals

Stateful Agent Gateway ingress, exactly-once remote execution, automatic tool retries, rebuilding fixed pending-request isolation, or gateway-wide runtime draining (#7929).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Expired sessions cannot serve new work; concurrent expiry yields bounded reinitialization without resurrecting removed targets or credentials.
- [ ] A dispatched `tools/call` is observed at most once by the test upstream even when it returns session-expiry or disconnects.
- [ ] Idle and close-failure cases release local resources within bounds and preserve unrelated servers.
- [ ] Stateless upstreams remain supported without invented session IDs.
- [ ] Legacy session-level findings and supported multi-replica routing are documented; any required cap or TTL gaps have executable coverage.

## Tests

Real MCP HTTP fixture with 404 and expiry, concurrent calls, reconnect, late responses, hanging or failed DELETE and idle expiry; assert side-effect counts and resource cleanup. Extend legacy-server lifecycle tests only for missing session-level behavior; retain request-ID isolation regressions.

## Dependencies

Completed protocol contract, #7951 and #7952. Coordinate with #7953 credential revocation. #7929 may reuse close hooks later but is not implemented here.

## Background

Parent #7949. This task owns the shared metering integration for LLM usage. A shared per-attempt usage contract is needed for auditing, the existing cost-ledger proposal and subsequent budgets. This issue does not own a second cost ledger.

## Existing ownership and reuse

- #7934 owns the usage ledger, versioned prices and currency, effective time, historical estimated costs and export. Reuse its event contract; do not duplicate storage, pricing or export here.
- #7911 and open PR #7937 own the concrete OpenAI Responses output-token bug. Consume that fix rather than implementing it again.
- #7702 and open PR #7848 own reservation and reconciliation; metering must not introduce another debit or settlement chain.
- Reuse AI Proxy protocol adapters, bounded response observers and parsers and terminal events. Master `87c22dde7` still reads `completion_tokens` in `AiTokenLimiterPlugin`. Coordinate client-versus-target protocol attribution with #7871; retain existing native AI Proxy and applicable Spring AI paths, not a new provider stack.

Reimplementing #7911, a second ledger or pricing engine, new AI providers or retry/fallback policy, or treating estimates as provider invoices. Cost acceptance remains jointly tracked through #7934.

Reuse the existing parser regression suite.

## Dependencies

## Background

Parent #7949. This task defines the shared policy decision contract. MCP quotas and LLM budgets need the same explainable shadow and enforce decision semantics, rather than incompatible local switches.

## Existing capabilities and reuse

Reuse trusted request context, bounded runtime metrics and audit records from #7950. Reuse existing Redis and limiter primitives in the later execution integrations. #7933 is HTTP shadow traffic replay and comparison and is unrelated to this non-executing policy evaluation mode.

## Implementation scope

- Define a versioned decision contract with policy and configuration version, mode, allow or would-deny or deny result, bounded reason codes, correlation and effective time.
- Shadow mode must not reject otherwise permitted requests or debit real quotas. Use an isolated bounded shadow ledger and counters for continuous evaluation, while recording actual observed usage normally.
- Enforce mode acts at the real admission and settlement points in #7957 and #7958. Define mode transitions, in-flight reservations, expiry and comparison semantics without moving or double-debiting state between ledgers.
- Authentication, authorization and fundamental resource protection always remain enforced independently of policy shadow mode.

## Non-goals

Duplicating audit or metrics implementations, bypassing security in shadow mode, traffic mirroring, or claiming a contract-only implementation completes #7957 or #7958 integration.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A common decision schema and reason vocabulary is consumed by metrics and audit; bounded labels exclude tenant and trace IDs as unbounded dimensions.
- [ ] Shadow evaluation preserves normal routing and production quota state, yet evaluates repeated calls against evolving isolated state.
- [ ] Mode changes and in-flight work have deterministic, documented semantics without double accounting or lost reservations.
- [ ] Security and resource rejections remain effective in both modes.
- [ ] Executable contract tests are supplied for both MCP quota and LLM budget consumers; real execution integrations are tracked by their respective issues.

## Tests

Contract and state-transition tests; concurrent shadow and enforce isolation; configuration updates and stale policy versions; audit and metric correlation tests; failure, expiry and cancellation cases and tests proving authentication, authorization and resource limits cannot be bypassed.

## Dependencies

Completed request/terminal-context and runtime-observability contracts, plus #7950. Define this contract before #7957 and #7958; those tasks must ship actual shadow and enforce integration with their first release.

body_text:
## Background

Parent #7949. This task owns distributed MCP business-quota admission. Per-process resource admission is not a distributed tenant or subject business quota across gateway replicas.

## Existing capabilities and reuse

Reuse trusted identity and deny-first tools authorization, Redis and existing rate-limiter infrastructure, current deadlines, #7951 resource bounds, #7956 decisions and existing audit and metrics. Review #7702 and PR #7848 atomic and idempotent accounting patterns where applicable, but MCP invocation counts are not LLM tokens.

## Implementation scope

- Implement tenant and subject invocation-count windows first; explicitly scoped tool and server dimensions and multilevel concurrency are added only where required by the chosen policy, without allowing cross-tenant keys.
- Provide atomic distributed admission, deterministic window expiry and separate count-debit and concurrency-release semantics.
- Use unique bounded concurrency leases, renewal where necessary, crash expiry and idempotent release. Define failed admissions, cancellation, retry and unknown upstream outcome accounting.
- Validate trusted configuration; define Redis failure behavior explicitly and preserve underlying authentication, authorization and resource limits.
- Ship shadow and enforce modes using #7956, isolated shadow state, audit decisions and bounded metrics in the initial feature.

## Non-goals

A second rate-limiter platform, elapsed-time billing or quota, LLM token and cost budgets (#7958), or replaying side-effecting tools. Existing deadlines remain the execution-time boundary.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two or more gateways cannot admit beyond the configured shared count or concurrency policy through races.
- [ ] Count consumption and permit release are independently correct; duplicate completion cannot refund counts or release another request's lease.
- [ ] Crashed holders and expired windows recover within documented bounds; renewal cannot resurrect removed policies or released leases.
- [ ] Redis outage, configuration updates and cancellation have explicit outcomes; state and key cardinality and shadow retention are bounded.
- [ ] Shadow does not debit production counters; enforce rejects at the actual execution boundary with matching audit and metrics.

## Tests

Real Redis multi-instance concurrent admission, window boundaries, renewal and release races, process-loss and expiry and Redis outage and recovery; authenticated tenant isolation, configuration invalidation, shadow and enforce transitions and actual MCP side-effect counts. Avoid timing-only assertions where controllable clocks or barriers are possible.

## Dependencies

Completed identity and request/terminal-context contracts, #7951 and #7956; #7950 audit vocabulary. Reliable atomic admission lessons should be reused by #7958, not a hard requirement to create another accounting store.

body_text:
## Background

Parent #7949. This task owns the remaining multidimensional token and cost budget policy. Identity-scoped budgets must build on trustworthy per-attempt metering and existing reservations, not a competing settlement implementation.

## Existing ownership and reuse

#7702 and open PR #7848 own opt-in estimated completion-token reservation and reconciliation, Redis-time fixed windows, idempotent settlement, cancellation and unknown-usage handling and validation and metrics. Do not duplicate that implementation or open another overshoot bug. As of 2026-10-21, #7848 was open, not a merged baseline.

#7934 owns the usage ledger and versioned estimated cost; #7911 and PR #7937 own Responses usage repair. #7955 completes shared metering coverage. Preserve the existing token-limiter compatibility policy unless explicitly configured otherwise.

## Implementation scope: gaps beyond #7848

- Extend the accepted reservation foundation to trusted tenant, subject, internal API-key ID and model dimensions and token or cost policy based on accepted #7955 measurements and #7934 price provenance.
- Define atomic reserve, settle and compensate across applicable dimensions: all-or-nothing admission or reliable compensation, one authoritative settlement chain, and idempotent attempt and logical correlation.
- Cover retry and fallback attempts without creating a new retry policy or double charging. Specify failure, cancellation, missing usage, process crash, expired reservations and price or policy changes.
- Ship #7956 shadow and enforce integration with isolated shadow accounting, audited decisions and bounded metrics. Reuse #7957 atomic-admission lessons.
- State soft-budget exposure whenever maximum consumption or trustworthy final usage cannot be bounded. Reserved estimates and estimated monetary costs are not provider invoices or hard actual-spend guarantees.

## Non-goals

## Background

Parent #7949. This task is a lower-priority MCP capability and can proceed independently after its catalog and security dependencies. MCP prompts provide client-facing templates and need their own list and get authorization and bounded aggregation contract.

## Existing capabilities and reuse

Reuse Agent Gateway tools catalog snapshots, remote connection and credential lifecycle, trusted identity and list and execution authorization patterns. Existing tools-only behavior remains compatible. Existing resources PR #7669 is separate prior work, not a prerequisite or a replacement for prompts.

## Implementation scope

- Add local and remote `prompts/list` and `prompts/get` with deterministic naming and conflict handling, correct routing and argument validation. Document naming before implementation; do not silently change existing tools names.
- Enforce consistent list visibility and get authorization with deny precedence and tenant isolation; use trusted capability grants rather than treating tool access as prompt access.
- Implement capability advertisement, pagination and directory-change handling only as required by the selected supported protocol; preserve coherent snapshots under refresh and removal.
- Bound discovery and result sizes, concurrency and cancellation; reuse target-bound credentials and #7952 recovery rather than new transport infrastructure.

## Non-goals

Automatic prompt-injection protection, implicit authorization to execute tools described by a prompt, full MCP protocol completion, resources subscriptions or templates, or unconditional SDK migration.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A documented real MCP client can list and get both local and remote prompts through the gateway with deterministic routing.
- [ ] Unauthorized prompts are neither listed nor retrievable; removed or revoked definitions cannot reappear through stale snapshots.
- [ ] Argument errors, pagination, naming conflicts, unsupported capabilities, bounded responses, timeout and cancellation have explicit protocol-consistent behavior.
- [ ] Existing tools and legacy MCP Server paths remain compatible and credentials or content do not leak into logs.

## Tests

Parser, handler, catalog and provider tests; actual client-to-gateway-to-MCP-server list and get fixtures; multiple servers with name collisions, pagination and changing definitions; tenant and grant isolation and revoke or refresh races; error, cancel, oversize and tools-coexistence regressions.

## Dependencies

Completed protocol and trusted-identity contracts, #7951 and #7952. SDK migration becomes a prerequisite only if this selected protocol or client path demonstrates a genuine compatibility or maintenance trigger; otherwise reuse the current stack. Additional resources capability is not a prerequisite.

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Current Behavior

Rule match results are stored under plugin name and request path, without selector ID. After selecting a selector, AbstractShenyuPlugin accepts the cached rule without checking its selectorId. Therefore, two selectors selected by different request headers can execute each other's rules.

### Expected Behavior

A cached rule must belong to the currently selected selector. Isolate entries by selector and path, and ensure negative entries have the same isolation.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Enable a test plugin using AbstractShenyuPlugin, with default match caches enabled.
2. Add custom-flow selector A: AND `header X-Tenant = a`; add selector B: AND `header X-Tenant = b`. Set both enabled and continued=true.
3. Under A add enabled rule RA: `uri = /x`. Under B add enabled rule RB: `uri = /x`.
4. Execute GET /x with X-Tenant=a. Observed doExecute receives A and RA.
5. Execute GET /x with X-Tenant=b. Observed doExecute receives **B and RA**, instead of B and RB.

The header-based selectors are not positively cached, but their URI-only rules are. Thus selector selection is correct while rule selection crosses the selector boundary. This can apply the wrong route, transformation or policy handle, depending on the plugin.

### Anything else?

- Rule lookup: https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/862f5e37e894bd8cef85ef540a8629f313e9ecdf/shenyu-plugin/shenyu-plugin-base/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/plugin/base/AbstractShenyuPlugin.java#L120-L132
- Cache key: https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/862f5e37e894bd8cef85ef540a8629f313e9ecdf/shenyu-plugin/shenyu-plugin-base/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/plugin/base/cache/MatchDataCache.java#L175-L178

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Current Behavior

A URI-only selector can be cached by plugin/path when it is the only selector matching the current request, even though another selector depends on dynamic request attributes and could win on a subsequent request with the same path.

`cacheSelectorData` checks only the winning selector's conditions. It does not establish that the winner remains correct across the entire candidate set for all requests sharing the cache key. A positive cache hit then bypasses candidate evaluation.

Consequently, warming the cache with an ordinary request changes the routing result of an otherwise identical VIP request. This is a correctness defect, not only a cache hit-rate concern.

### Expected Behavior

With configuration unchanged, enabling or warming a match cache must not change the selected selector/rule for a given request. A path-only result must be reused only if the relevant candidate set cannot produce a different winner due to omitted request attributes.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Enable a concrete AbstractShenyuPlugin test plugin and default match caches.
2. Configure two enabled CUSTOM_FLOW selectors with AND matching:
   - Generic: `uri = /x`.
   - VIP: `uri = /x` AND `header X-Tenant = a`.
3. Set continued=false for both so the test isolates selector matching and uses the default rule.
4. Execute GET /x with X-Tenant=b. Generic is the only match and is cached.
5. Execute GET /x with X-Tenant=a. Observed: Generic executes again.
6. Clear only the selector match cache and repeat step 5. Observed: VIP executes, as required by its larger AND-condition count.

Executed via a recording AbstractShenyuPlugin subclass, real BaseDataCache/MatchDataCache, Spring MockServerWebExchange and execute(...).block():

```text
ordinary request warms cache: generic:default_rule
VIP request after warmup:     generic:default_rule
same VIP request after clear: special:default_rule
```

### Environment

ShenYu master, 2.7.2-SNAPSHOT, commit `862f5e37e894bd8cef85ef540a8629f313e9ecdf`, Java 17. This is an executed in-process reproduction, not a deployed HTTP integration test.

### Anything else?

- [Positive selector cache eligibility](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/862f5e37e894bd8cef85ef540a8629f313e9ecdf/shenyu-plugin/shenyu-plugin-base/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/plugin/base/AbstractShenyuPlugin.java#L157-L177)
- [Cached selector accepted before matching](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/blob/862f5e37e894bd8cef85ef540a8629f313e9ecdf/shenyu-plugin/shenyu-plugin-base/src/main/java/org/apache/shenyu/plugin/base/AbstractShenyuPlugin.java#L93-L104)
- The analogous positive rule-cache eligibility should also be covered by regression tests; the executed reproduction above isolates selectors.
- #7977 concerns caching a miss. This issue concerns caching a successful generic match that later shadows a more specific dynamic candidate.
- #7976 concerns rule-cache isolation across selectors, a separate issue.

Adding a single header to the key is not a general fix: competing candidates can depend on method, query, cookies, domain or other inputs. Conservative candidate-set cache eligibility or dependency-aware cache keys should preserve matching semantics.

## Summary (executable leaf)

Merge the local multi-group Measure query's per-group results as batches, instead of through the row merger `logical_measure.MergeGroupMIterators`. Follow-up to #14066 (closed) under #13998.

Checked against BanyanDB `origin/main` @ 15635181b. The blocker is merged, and the row stack has exactly **one** production caller left:

- `banyand/query/processor.go` `dispatchMeasure` (multi-group branch, around lines 643-667) calls `vecplan.Dispatch` once per group. Each call returns an `executor.MIterator`, i.e. rows. It then merges them with `MergeGroupMIterators` (`pkg/query/logical/measure/cross_group_merge.go`), which wraps each iterator in `sortableDataPoints` → `sort.NewItemIter` → `sortedMIterator`.
- The liaison already has a batch k-way merger for multi-group rows: `mergeDistributedRowsMulti` / `runDistributedRowMerge` in `pkg/query/vectorized/measure/plan/distributed_rows.go`. It null-fills columns a group lacks into a merged schema, sorts by the requested key, and dedups `(sid, ts)` inside each equal-sort window keeping the highest version. It runs on decoded frames only.

## Required change

1. Add a batch-returning dispatch, e.g. `vecplan.DispatchBatches`, that runs the same per-group plan as `Dispatch` but hands back the plan's `RecordBatch` output and schema instead of an `MIterator`.
2. In the multi-group branch of `dispatchMeasure`, collect each group's batches, align them to the merged schema (the same null-fill rules as `decodeMultiGroupSources`), and merge them through the existing `runDistributedRowMerge` loop. Generalize its source from "decoded frame" to "in-memory batch"; do not write a third merger.
3. Convert to an `MIterator` once, after the merge, and strip hidden criteria tags at that point (today `hiddenTagsMIterator` does this per group).
4. Delete `MergeGroupMIterators`, `sortableDataPoints` and `sortedMIterator` (`cross_group_merge.go`, `sortable_data_points.go`, `sorted_miterator.go`) and their tests. Keep `ResolveCrossGroupMergeOrder`, or move it next to the new caller if nothing else needs it.

Single-group dispatch, aggregation (`GroupBy`/`Agg`/`Top`, including `emitPartial`), and wire formats are unchanged.

## Concrete oracle

Two groups, measure schema `ts, SID, version, value`. Duplicate versions are split across batches and groups:

```text
group A batch 1: (ts=10, SID=7, version=1, value=100)
group B batch 1: (ts=10, SID=7, version=3, value=300)
group A batch 2: (ts=20, SID=8, version=1, value=200)
```

- Ascending by time: `(10,7,3,300)`, `(20,8,1,200)`.
- Descending: `(20,8,1,200)`, `(10,7,3,300)`.
- Ascending with offset 1 and limit 1: only `(20,8,1,200)`.
- Index order on a tag both groups define gives the same version-dedup result.
- A tag that only group B defines comes back null on group A rows (schema alignment).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test through `dispatchMeasure`'s multi-group branch (not the helper alone) asserts the exact oracle above, with each group's rows split across at least two batches.
- [ ] The row stack is gone: `MergeGroupMIterators`, `sortableDataPoints` and `sortedMIterator` no longer exist, so restoring row merging means re-adding code a reviewer will see. The returned plan string names the batch merge (e.g. `vec-multi-measure-batch[...]`), and the test asserts it.
- [ ] Hidden criteria tags (a criteria tag not in the projection) don't appear in the output.
- [ ] Error and cancellation: if one group's dispatch or batch read fails, every batch already obtained is released and the error is returned. Assert this with a failing fake group.
- [ ] Existing tests pass:

```sh
go test ./banyand/query ./pkg/query/logical/measure ./pkg/query/vectorized/measure/...
go test ./test/integration/standalone/query/...
```

## Out of scope

- The liaison distributed path (already batch-native), and aggregation partial reduction (#14069).
- Top or GroupBy semantics, the internal TopN pre-aggregation RPC, and wire formats.
- New memory-bound claims. A benchmark that reports allocations before and after is welcome but not required.

<details><summary>Original description (tracking parent)</summary>

## Summary

Merge vectorized Measure results without first converting them into individual `InternalDataPoint` objects. Follow-up to #14066 under #13998.

## Size audit and dependencies

Classification: **tracking parent**, not an executable leaf or automated implementation task.
Boundary: the production multi-group Measure caller of `MergeGroupMIterators` and its `sortableDataPoints` / `sortedMIterator` stack.
This spans batch consumption, caller/egress migration, schema alignment, ordering/version deduplication, and resource ownership. Decompose after the legacy removal merges.
Blocked by: #14066 via BanyanDB PR apache/skywalking-banyandb#1326.

## Requirements

R1. Consume and merge per-group batches directly; do not reconstruct the row merger internally.
R2. Preserve requested ordering, version-based deduplication, schema alignment, and pagination.
R3. Materialize protobuf only where the response boundary requires it; preserve tracing and response compatibility.
R4. Release consumed batches correctly on completion, cancellation, and errors.

## Concrete oracle

Two groups supply these records, with duplicate versions split across batches:

```text
timestamp=10, SID=7, version=1, value=100
timestamp=10, SID=7, version=3, value=300
timestamp=20, SID=8, version=1, value=200
```

Ascending output is `(10,7,3,300)` followed by `(20,8,1,200)`. Descending reverses that order. Ascending with offset 1 and limit 1 returns only `(20,8,1,200)`.

## Completion criteria and RED-test direction

- [ ] The real processor multi-group caller consumes the batch-native merger.
- [ ] Tests assert the exact oracle across batch boundaries, plus index ordering and supported schema alignment.
- [ ] A path-sensitive production-caller regression fails if row iteration/materialization is restored. Output assertions alone are insufficient: the existing merger already produces these answers.
- [ ] Each executable child identifies its public boundary and failing test before implementation; no helper-only foundation PR counts as completion.
- [ ] Cancellation/error tests verify resource release; benchmark comparisons report allocations without claiming a new resource bound that has not been proved.

Packages: `banyand/query`, `pkg/query/logical/measure`, `pkg/query/vectorized/measure`.

```sh
go test ./banyand/query ./pkg/query/logical/measure ./pkg/query/vectorized/measure/...
go test ./test/integration/standalone/query/... ./test/integration/distributed/query/...
```

## Out of scope

Changing ordinary Top or GroupBy semantics; the internal TopN pre-aggregation RPC; schema-evolved aggregate partial reduction (separate workstream).

Parent: #13998.

## Compatibility and review policy

- Preserve existing on-disk and wire formats and mixed-version compatibility. Any necessary protocol change requires a separately reviewed compatibility contract.
- Use explicit, hand-calculated expected results; do not depend on the removed row engine as the test oracle.
- Human review enforces the no-new-row-path policy. A row-call-site lint guard is not required.

</details>

## Summary

Make a valid multi-group Measure aggregate query succeed when the participating groups have different projected tag schemas (schema evolution). Follow-up to #14066 under #13998.

## Size audit and dependencies

Classification: **executable leaf**.
Boundary: the multi-group aggregate path of `DistributedPlan.Execute` → `executeAgg` → `ReduceRawFrames` → `ReducePartialBatches` (`pkg/query/vectorized/measure/plan/distributed.go`, `pkg/query/vectorized/measure/reduce.go`).
Blocked by: nothing — #14066 merged via apache/skywalking-banyandb#1326.

## Current behavior (rechecked on apache/skywalking-banyandb `main` @ 15635181b)

1. For a multi-group query, `DistributedPlan.Execute` broadcasts one request per group and narrows its tag projection to that group's own schema with `intersectTagProjection` (distributed.go): tags the group does not define are dropped, so each group's data nodes return frames with **only their own columns**.
2. With an aggregation, all groups' frames are flattened and passed to `executeAgg` → `ReduceRawFrames` → `ReducePartialBatches`.
3. `ReducePartialBatches` takes the first non-empty partial's schema as the reference and calls `schemaCompatible` on every other partial, which requires the same column count, names, roles and types. A group missing a projected tag fails with `ReducePartialBatches: partial N schema mismatch: column count mismatch …`, and the whole query fails.

No existing test covers aggregation over schema-evolved groups.

## Change

Normalize missing **projected, non-grouping tags** to null before partial reduction, so partials from groups with different tag schemas reduce together. Do not simply disable structural schema validation: genuinely incompatible partials (same column name with a different type, or a missing grouping tag / aggregate column) must still be rejected with a clear error.

## Concrete oracle

- Group `g_old`, schema `svc,value`; rows `(old,2)` and `(old,3)`.
- Group `g_new`, schema `svc,zone,value`; rows `(new,west,7)` and `(new,west,11)`.
- Query across both groups: `GROUP BY svc`, `SUM(value)`, project `svc,zone`.

Expected unordered output:

```text
old, NULL, 5
new, west, 18
```

Different service keys deliberately avoid ambiguity over representative values of non-grouping tags. Today the query fails with `partial … schema mismatch`.

## Completion criteria and RED-test direction

- [ ] A regression test drives the oracle through the **distributed production caller** (`DistributedPlan.Execute` / `executeAgg` with per-group frames), not only `ReducePartialBatches`; it fails on current `main` with the schema-mismatch error and passes after the change.
- [ ] Normalization preserves aggregate-state columns, including the count sidecar used by `MEAN`; add a `MEAN` case across the same two groups.
- [ ] Genuinely incompatible partials are still rejected with a clear error (a projected tag present in both groups with different types).
- [ ] Existing single-group and same-schema multi-group aggregation results are unchanged.

```sh
go test ./pkg/query/vectorized/measure/...
go test ./test/integration/distributed/query/...
```

## Out of scope (separate issue)

Replica deduplication that preserves storage-group provenance — e.g. contributions 5 and 18 for service `api` from two different storage groups must total **23** even when both groups use shard 0, while duplicate replicas of either contribution must not increase the sum. That is an independent change with its own test and will be filed as its own issue under #13998.

## Summary (executable leaf)

Merge the **local multi-group** Stream query's per-group batches with the existing batch pipeline, instead of turning every group into `[]*streamv1.Element` and merging rows with `MergeGroupElements`. Follow-up to #14066 and #14067 (both closed; #14067 landed in BanyanDB PR apache/skywalking-banyandb#1400) under #13998.

Checked against BanyanDB `origin/main` @ 15635181b:

- `banyand/query/processor.go` `tryVecMergeDispatch` (around lines 334-359) already gets each group's result as batches (`group.Scan.ExecuteVectorized` → `stageStreamBatches`). It then calls `vstream.BuildElementsFromBatch` for **each group**, merges the Elements with `logical_stream.MergeGroupElements` (`pkg/query/logical/stream/stream_plan_merge.go:127`), and slices offset/limit with `sliceStreamElements`.
- A batch merge pipeline already exists and is used by the local single-scan path: `vstream.BuildStreamMergePipeline` (`pkg/query/vectorized/stream/pipeline.go`), i.e. `SortedMerge` (time or `OrderKey`, asc/desc, stable ties) → `Distinct` (first-seen by ElementID) → `Limit(offset, limit)`.
- `MergeGroupElements` has no other production caller.

## Required change

1. In `tryVecMergeDispatch`, feed every group's staged batches into one `SortedMerge` → `Distinct` → `Limit(merge.Offset, merge.Limit)` pipeline (reuse `BuildStreamMergePipeline`, or its operators, with a multi-source input).
2. Groups may project different tags (schema-evolved groups). Align their batches to one merged schema first: null-fill tags a group lacks, the same rule the row path follows today when one group's Elements lack a tag.
3. Build Elements once, from the pipeline's output only.
4. Delete `MergeGroupElements` and its tests. `newComparableElement` and `sortableElements` stay, because the distributed coordinator still uses them (see Out of scope).

## Concrete oracle

```text
Group 1: A(key=1), B(key=3)
Group 2: A(key=1), C(key=2)
```

The two copies of A are identical (same ElementID).

- Ascending by `key` with offset 1 and limit 2: **C, B**.
- Descending with offset 0 and limit 2: **B, C**.
- The same results when each group's rows are split across two batches, and when ordering is by timestamp (A=1, C=2, B=3).
- When the order tag isn't in the client's projection, the order still holds and the tag doesn't appear in the output.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test drives `tryVecMergeDispatch` (or the processor entry above it) with two groups and asserts the oracle, including the cross-batch and unprojected-sort-tag cases.
- [ ] `MergeGroupElements` no longer exists, and no per-group `BuildElementsFromBatch` call remains in `tryVecMergeDispatch`. Restoring row merging means re-adding code a reviewer will see.
- [ ] A test with schema-evolved groups: a tag only one group defines is present on that group's elements and absent from the other group's. Record main's output for this fixture first and assert the exact elements.
- [ ] Failure: if one group's scan or staging fails, batches from groups already executed are released and the existing error message is returned.
- [ ] Existing tests pass:

```sh
go test ./banyand/query ./pkg/query/logical/stream ./pkg/query/vectorized/stream/...
go test ./test/integration/standalone/query/...
```

## Out of scope (follow-up slices of the original R1-R4)

- The **distributed coordinator** (`pkg/query/logical/stream/stream_plan_distributed.go` `distributedPlan.Execute` / `decodeNodeElements`), which still decodes frame replies into Elements before merging. It needs a proto→batch conversion at the compatibility boundary for mixed frame/proto replies, so it is a separate leaf.
- Filter-first semantics, timestamp under-fill, wire formats, and new memory-bound claims.

<details><summary>Original description (tracking parent)</summary>

## Summary

Remove intermediate `Element` materialization from Stream result merging and deduplication. Follow-up to #14066 under #13998.

## Size audit and dependencies

Classification: **tracking parent**, not an executable leaf or automated implementation task.
Boundaries: local multi-group dispatch using `MergeGroupElements`, and the distributed coordinator that currently decodes frames into Elements before merging.
These are separate production cutovers and must become separate executable tasks.
Blocked by: #14066 via BanyanDB PR apache/skywalking-banyandb#1326.
Related dependency: #14067. Coordinate with that workstream for full filtered/hidden-tag coverage; basic frame-input coordinator merging can be sliced independently. Do not start a child whose required projection boundary is not yet merged.

## Requirements

R1. Merge and deduplicate batches directly for both local multi-group and distributed callers.
R2. Preserve ordering, selected duplicate values, and global offset/limit behavior. Retain internal sort keys even when clients do not project ordering tags.
R3. Accept frame and protobuf node responses for tracing and mixed-version compatibility. Convert protobuf input at the compatibility boundary, rather than forcing frame inputs back into Elements.
R4. Materialize final Elements only where the client output requires them; release batch resources on completion, cancellation, and malformed responses.

## Concrete oracle

```text
Source 1: A(key=1), B(key=3)
Source 2: A(key=1), C(key=2)
```

The two copies of A are identical. Ascending order with offset 1 and limit 2 returns **C, B**. Exercise the same oracle across batches, across local groups, and across data-node replies. Specify duplicate-version and equal-key fixtures separately when defining each executable child; do not invent a new tie rule as a side effect of the cutover.

## Completion criteria and RED-test direction

- [ ] Real local and distributed callers use batch merge/deduplication, including cross-batch duplicates and pagination.
- [ ] Mixed frame/protobuf replies preserve the oracle and tracing information.
- [ ] Path-sensitive tests fail if frame inputs are materialized into Elements before merging. Output assertions alone are not RED because the current row merge can return the same answers.
- [ ] Cancellation, malformed replies, and batch release are covered in each caller cutover.
- [ ] Benchmark comparisons quantify allocation changes; no new wire format or unproved bounded-memory guarantee is required.

Relevant code: `banyand/query/processor.go`, `pkg/query/logical/stream/stream_plan_merge.go`, `pkg/query/logical/stream/stream_plan_distributed.go`, and `pkg/query/vectorized/stream`.

```sh
go test ./banyand/query ./pkg/query/logical/stream ./pkg/query/vectorized/stream/...
go test ./test/integration/standalone/query/... ./test/integration/distributed/query/...
```

## Out of scope

Changing filter-first semantics, timestamp under-fill behavior, or wire formats; implementing Stream filtering/projection itself (separate workstream).

Parent: #13998.

## Compatibility and review policy

- Preserve existing on-disk and wire formats and mixed-version compatibility. Any necessary protocol change requires a separately reviewed compatibility contract.
- Use explicit, hand-calculated expected results; do not depend on the removed row engine as the test oracle.
- Human review enforces the no-new-row-path policy. A row-call-site lint guard is not required.

</details>

Part 5 of 5 of the [tag aggregation and time bucketing design](https://github.com/apache/skywalking-banyandb/blob/main/docs/design/0.12.0/tag-aggregation/README.md), shipped in apache/skywalking-banyandb#1360.

**Design references:** [§7.7 The local scan: entity and indexed tags never touch the data file](https://github.com/apache/skywalking-banyandb/blob/main/docs/design/0.12.0/tag-aggregation/README.md#77-the-local-scan-entity-and-indexed-tags-never-touch-the-data-file) · [§12 Delivery order](https://github.com/apache/skywalking-banyandb/blob/main/docs/design/0.12.0/tag-aggregation/README.md#12-delivery-order) (stages 8a–9, both marked *optional* in the design)

**Depends on:** #14089 (time-bucket grouping) and #14090 (COUNT_DISTINCT) — this optimizes both. Not required for either to ship; the design explicitly defers this and asks that the payoff be measured before it's built.

## Scope

**Phase A — run-folding** (design's "intermediate step," no new execution path)
- Fold each maximal `(series, bucket)` span once instead of per row, using a plan-time flag marking which key columns are index-resolved — derived from `searchSeriesList`'s existing three-way projection split, never inferred at runtime by sampling column values.
- Applies whenever an index-resolved tag is a group key: `COUNT_DISTINCT` collapses `n − 1` redundant set inserts per span into one; `COUNT` becomes `count += spanLength`.

**Phase B — metadata-only scan** (after Phase A lands)
- Bypass block decode entirely when *every* tag the query touches (group keys, aggregation target, any tag a residual predicate touches) resolves from the series index — gated by the range-containment guard (a block whose `[min,max]` isn't fully inside the query range must still read `timestamps.bin`) and the no-residual-predicate guard.
- `index_mode` measures are the structural first case: they hold no part-resident tags at all, so an index-mode aggregation is index-only by construction.

## Out of scope
- Anything that changes correctness or the query surface — this issue is pure performance, gated by differential tests against the existing (already-correct) path.

## Test / Definition of done
- Phase A: differential test against the unoptimized per-row path on the same fixture (identical results, fewer group-map probes); a magnitude assertion (an 8192-row block at hour buckets collapses to ~137 spans, not 8192 key computations).
- Phase B: differential test against the decoding path across both index-mode and part-backed fixtures (identical results); the range-containment fixture — a block with rows at 09:00 and 09:59 (one hourly bucket) queried over 09:30–09:31 must yield no bucket row, while the same block fully inside the query range takes the shortcut.

## Summary

Handle node-local schema absence gracefully in distributed stream queries. If the liaison knows the requested schema but a queried data node does not yet know it, that node must not fail the entire query. Return the results available from the other nodes.

This replaces the proposed schema-sync change in #14103. Schema convergence through incremental updates and periodic full reconciliation is intended behavior; this issue does not change its timing or consistency model.

## Boundary and behavior

The production boundary is the data-node stream query response and its handling by the liaison's distributed stream query execution path.

- When a participating data node specifically lacks the requested stream schema, treat that node's contribution for that stream/group as empty and merge the remaining results normally.
- Preserve the normal schema-not-found error when the liaison itself cannot resolve the requested schema. Do not turn invalid queries into successful empty results.
- Preserve existing handling of unrelated failures, including timeouts, unavailable nodes, authorization failures, and query execution errors. Do not match arbitrary error-message text or suppress generic errors.
- For multi-group queries, missing schema for one group must not discard valid contributions for other requested groups on the same node. If all queried data nodes lack a schema that the liaison knows, the result for that schema is empty.

This intentionally permits results based on the currently available schema view during convergence. It does not promise a globally complete snapshot: node-local schema absence is not proof that the node has no persisted data.

## Example and acceptance criteria

Use a controlled fixture, independent of native logging and reconciliation timers:

1. The liaison and data nodes A/B know stream S. A contains an identifiable row A1; B contains B1. Queried node C lacks S.
2. Query S through the public stream API on the liaison. It succeeds and returns exactly A1 and B1, respecting the requested ordering and limit, instead of failing because C lacks S.
3. Verify the all-data-nodes-missing case, liaison-local schema absence, and a multi-group case where C can still contribute to a different requested group.
4. Inject an unrelated node error and verify that the new schema-absence handling does not swallow it.

Add a focused regression test before implementation and demonstrate RED -> GREEN. Add the real distributed query scenario to the existing in-process integration suite; do not require external server binaries or a 150-second wait.

## Scope and implementation pointers

Inspect the current main branch before implementation:

- `banyand/query/processor.go`: data-node stream execution-context lookup currently wraps lookup failures in a generic `common.Error`.
- `banyand/stream/svc_standalone.go`: `ErrStreamNotExist` identifies stream absence.
- `banyand/dquery/stream.go` and the distributed execution/response aggregation path: distinguish liaison-local validation from remote node failures.
- Existing fixtures: `test/cases/stream` and `test/integration/distributed/query`.

Preserve an unambiguous schema-absence distinction through the actual query transport, or normalize it at the node boundary without affecting liaison-local validation. Verify mixed-version behavior: old generic failures must not accidentally become ignorable. No persisted-format change is intended, and no unbounded retries or new buffering are needed.

Out of scope: revision watermarks, replay/full-reconciliation scheduling, storage durability, flush-on-close, and measure/trace query semantics. No dependency on the native-log implementation in apache/skywalking-banyandb#1368.

## Readiness and verification

Bounded implementation leaf: one distributed stream-query behavior, with the data-node response consumed by the existing liaison query path. Relevant callers and fixtures have been inspected, but no new regression test has been authored or run for this issue; establish the failing test on current main before implementation or automation queueing.

Focused checks (after adding the tests):

- `go test ./banyand/query ./banyand/dquery`
- `go test ./test/integration/distributed/query` with the suite's normal prerequisites.

## Summary (executable leaf)

The liaison's distributed Stream coordinator should merge data-node frame replies as columnar batches, instead of decoding each frame into `[]*streamv1.Element` and merging rows. This is the distributed-coordinator half of #14070's original scope. #14070 was narrowed to the local multi-group path (apache/skywalking-banyandb#1426), and this half has no issue. Under #13998.

Checked against BanyanDB `origin/main` @ 450c73a3:

- `pkg/query/logical/stream/stream_plan_distributed.go` `distributedPlan.Execute` (around lines 140–199) broadcasts the query. For each reply, `decodeNodeElements` (around 212–234) decodes a frame with `streamframe.Decode` and immediately calls `vstream.BuildElementsFromBatch`, turning the whole batch into Elements. The replies are then k-way merged as rows (`newSortableElements` → `sort.NewItemIter`, around 184–187), deduplicated by `ElementId` with a `seen` map, and sliced by `distributedLimit` (offset/limit, around 339–355).
- Data nodes reply with a frame whenever the query is not traced. `banyand/query/processor.go:366` `streamVecEmitAsFrame` returns `distributed && wireModeRaw && !traced`, and both `svc_liaison.go:165` and `svc_standalone.go:262` set the raw wire mode. So in a normal distributed query every reply is a frame, and the coordinator materializes all of them as rows.
- The batch operators this needs already exist: `pkg/query/vectorized/stream` `SortedMerge` (time or `OrderKey`, asc/desc, stable ties) → `Distinct` (first-seen by element id) → `Limit(offset, limit)`, composed by `BuildStreamMergePipeline`. apache/skywalking-banyandb#1426 adds a multi-source `BatchSource` and union-schema alignment for the local path, and this work should reuse them.

## Required change

1. In `distributedPlan.Execute`, decode each frame reply into a batch and feed every node's batches into one merge pipeline (reuse `BuildStreamMergePipeline` and #1426's `BatchSource` / schema alignment; no third merger). Replies with differing projected tags are aligned to one merged schema the same way #1426 aligns groups.
2. Apply the request's offset/limit in the pipeline's `Limit`, and build Elements once, from the pipeline output, for the client response. `distributedLimit` then slices nothing for this path (keep it for the traced path below, or fold it in).
3. Keep the per-node cap (`queryRequest.Limit = maxElementSize`) and the span tags (`response_count`, `element_id_count`) as today.
4. **Traced queries stay on the current path.** When any reply is a `*streamv1.QueryResponse` (a traced query), keep today's Element merge for that broadcast, including `span.AddSubTrace`. Converting protobuf replies to batches is out of scope.

## Concrete oracle

Two data nodes, frame replies, ordered by `key` ascending:

```text
Node 1: A(key=1), B(key=3)
Node 2: A(key=1), C(key=2)
```

The two copies of A are the same element (same ElementID, a replica).

- Ascending, offset 1, limit 2: **C, B**.
- Descending, offset 0, limit 2: **B, C**.
- Ordered by timestamp instead (A=1, C=2, B=3): the same results.
- The ordering tag isn't in the client projection: same order, and the tag is absent from the response (it travels in the frame's `OrderKey` column).
- Each node's rows split across two frames or batches: same results.
- A node that returns an error: the merged result of the other nodes plus the error, as today (`multierr`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test through `distributedPlan.Execute` with a fake broadcast of frame replies asserts every case of the oracle.
- [ ] Path-sensitive: for frame replies, no Element is built before the merge. `decodeNodeElements` no longer calls `BuildElementsFromBatch` on the frame path, and a test fails if per-reply Element materialization is restored, e.g. by asserting Elements are built once from the merged output. Asserting the answers alone is insufficient, because the current row merge returns the same answers.
- [ ] A traced query (protobuf replies) returns the same elements as before and still attaches every node's sub-trace.
- [ ] Batches from every reply are released on completion, on a decode error, and on context cancellation; covered by tests.
- [ ] Existing tests pass:

```sh
go test ./pkg/query/logical/stream/... ./pkg/query/vectorized/stream/... ./banyand/query
go test -tags=querymetrics ./test/integration/distributed/query/...
```

## Dependencies

Builds on apache/skywalking-banyandb#1426 (`BatchSource`, schema alignment). Start after it merges, or base the branch on it.

## Out of scope

- Converting traced (protobuf) replies to batches; the Element path stays for them. That's a follow-up, after which `newSortableElements` and `comparableElement` can be deleted.
- The Trace query merges (`pkg/query/logical/trace`), which apache/skywalking-banyandb#1423 is reworking.
- Wire format, per-node cap semantics, filter-first semantics, and new memory-bound claims.

## Compatibility and review policy

- Preserve existing on-disk and wire formats.
- Use explicit, hand-calculated expected results; do not use the removed row engine as the test oracle.

## Summary

`writeCallback.Rev` (`banyand/stream/write_standalone.go`) logs each failed event and continues, and always returns an empty response. The caller gets `STATUS_SUCCEED` for elements that were not stored.

For example, for a missing group, `handle` fails in `prepareElementsInGroup` (`cannot load tsdb for group`). `Rev` logs `cannot handle write event` and returns no error.

## Observed

With native self-stored logs (apache/skywalking-banyandb#1419) on a standalone node, a forced delete of `_monitoring_log` lost 3 events. `native_log_written_total` rose for them, and every `native_log_dropped_total` reason stayed 0.

## Notes for a fix

- The error reply path already exists: `localBatchPublisher.Close` (`banyand/queue/local.go`) and the data-node sub server (`banyand/queue/sub/helpers.go`) forward a `*common.Error`, as `CheckHealth` does for disk-full.
- The liaison applies one status to every message it sent to a node in a batch (`banyand/liaison/grpc/stream.go`). Reporting an error on a partial failure would mark stored elements as failed, and a retrying client would store them twice. Report an error only when nothing in the batch was stored, or report per element.
- Index-write failures happen after the elements are stored, so they should stay logged only.
- `banyand/measure` and `banyand/trace` use the same pattern.

## Effect on #1419

#1419 does not change this callback. Until it is fixed, events lost while the log destination is missing are counted as written, so a test cannot observe that loss.

# Summary

I'm wondering why `argo-cd` is not using `-s` and `-w` ldflags and `-trimpath` to reduce final binary size. I understand adding `-s` or `-w` will cause problems with debugging, but maybe for production build it will be fine? Also `-trimpath` seems as no-brainer, because as far as I know there is no real advantage of not using it.

# Motivation

Command: `make argocd-all`

Option                    | `argocd` binary size (bytes) | Difference between nothing (bytes)
--------------------------|------------------------------|-----------------------------------
nothing                   | 211893899                    | 0
`-trimpath`               | 211617969                    | 275930 (0.26 Mebibytes)
`-w` + `-trimpath`        | 171784687                    | 40109212 (38.25 Mebibytes)
`-s` + `-w` + `-trimpath` | 148361400                    | 63532499 (60.59 Mebibytes)

# Proposal

Add `-s -w` to ldflags and `-trimpath` to `go build`. I'm not saying it should be added, but wondering why it wasn't. I couldn't find information about it.

In my environment some services are not reachable by intention because deployed to fargate.

**Expected behavior**

When service is not available or not reachable - the only impact - is a feature that is handled by that specific service.

<!-- If you are trying to resolve an environment-specific issue or have a one-off question about the edge case that does not require a feature then please consider asking a question in argocd slack [channel](https://argoproj.github.io/community/join-slack). -->

Checklist:

- [x] I've searched in the docs and FAQ for my answer: https://bit.ly/argocd-faq.
- [x] I've included steps to reproduce the bug.
- [x] I've pasted the output of `argocd version`.

**Describe the bug**

When syncing a **multi-source ArgoCD Application** where:
- **Source 1:** Git repository containing Helm values files
- **Source 2:** Helm chart from a Helm repository

The Application syncs with **new values from Git** but uses **old/cached Helm chart templates**. This results in the new values being applied to outdated templates, causing configuration mismatches.

**Example scenario:**
- Helm chart version is bumped from `1.0.0` to `1.1.0`
- Chart `1.1.0` contains a **new template** (e.g., new ConfigMap entry or new resource)
- Values in Git are updated to include values for the new template
- After sync: Git values are correctly pulled (new values present), but the **chart templates are still from version `1.0.0`**
- Result: New values exist but the with old template being used

**Key observations:**
- Git source (values) syncs correctly - new values are present
- Helm chart source does NOT sync to new version - old templates are used
- The **entire Application** uses old chart templates with new Git values (not a partial sync)
- This behavior is **intermittent** but becomes **more reproducible** with Applications containing ~100+ resources
- Hard refresh before sync does not consistently resolve the issue


**Expected behavior**

When syncing a multi-source Application:
1. Git source should pull the latest values ✓ (this works)
2. Helm chart source should pull the latest chart version/templates ✗ (this fails)
3. The rendered manifests should use **new chart templates** + **new values**

## Actual Behavior

When syncing a multi-source Application:
1. Git source correctly pulls the latest values ✓
2. Helm chart source uses **cached/old chart templates** ✗
3. The rendered manifests use **old chart templates** + **new values**

This causes:
- New values referencing new template structures fail to render correctly
- New ConfigMap entries defined in chart `1.1.0` are missing (template doesn't exist in cached `1.0.0`)
- Application deploys with inconsistent state

Also - after push to git and after bad sync with wrong values there is another sync right after the first one with new chart but it cannot be completed since application is in failed state with diff.


**To Reproduce**

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a multi-source ArgoCD Application:
   ```yaml
   apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
   kind: Application
   metadata:
     name: my-app
   spec:
     sources:
       - repoURL: https://git.example.com/my-org/helm-values.git
         targetRevision: main
         ref: values
       - repoURL: https://helm.example.com/charts
         chart: my-chart
         targetRevision: 1.0.0
         helm:
           valueFiles:
             - $values/environments/prod/values.yaml
     destination:
       server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
       namespace: my-namespace
   ```

2. Deploy chart version `1.0.0` - works correctly

3. Update Helm chart to version `1.1.0` with new template:
   ```yaml
   # New ConfigMap entry in templates/configmap.yaml
   data:
     EXISTING_VAR: {{ .Values.existingVar }}
     NEW_VAR: {{ .Values.newVar }}  # New entry in chart 1.1.0
   ```

4. Update Git values to include the new variable:
   ```yaml
   # environments/prod/values.yaml
   existingVar: "value1"
   newVar: "value2"  # New value for new template entry
   ```

5. Update Application to use chart version `1.1.0`:
   ```yaml
   targetRevision: 1.1.0
   ```

6. Application syncs automatically (or manual sync)

7. **Observe:**
   - Git values are updated (contains `newVar: "value2"`) ✓
   - Chart templates are **NOT updated** - still using `1.0.0` templates ✗

**Example scenario:**
- Helm chart version is bumped from `1.0.0` to `1.1.0`

- Hard refresh before sync does not consistently resolve the issue

When syncing a multi-source Application:
1. Git source should pull the latest values ✓ (this works)
2. Helm chart source should pull the latest chart version/templates ✗ (this fails)

**Describe the bug**

When using Azure Workload Identity in a multi-tenant environment, ArgoCD fails to switch between tenants for different OCI/Helm repositories. Despite configuring different azureTenantId values in the Repository Secrets, the argocd-repo-server consistently uses the Tenant ID injected into the Pod's environment variables by the Azure Workload Identity mutating webhook.

**To Reproduce**

1. Deploy ArgoCD with Workload Identity enabled for the argocd-repo-server.
2. The Azure Webhook injects AZURE_TENANT_ID (Tenant A) and AZURE_CLIENT_ID into the pod.
3. Configure a Repository Secret for an ACR in a different tenant (Tenant B), setting:
```
useAzureWorkloadIdentity: "true"
azureTenantId: <Tenant-B-ID>  # this is where the ACR lives
clientId: <Identity-ID-from-Tenant-A> (Cross-tenant trust established via Federated Credentials - App Registration in Tenant A + Enterprise App in Tenant B).
```
Attempt to connect to the repository.

**Expected behavior**

ArgoCD should prioritize the azureTenantId and clientId specified in the Repository Secret over the global Pod environment variables to allow cross-tenant repository access within a single repo-server instance.

**Actual behavior**

ArgoCD fails with a 401 Unauthorized error. Logs indicate: failed to get Azure access token after challenge: failed to get refresh token: 401 Unauthorized.

Investigation via curl inside the pod confirms that manual token requests to Tenant B using the ServiceAccount token (OIDC) work perfectly when the Tenant B endpoint is targeted. However, ArgoCD appears to ignore the azureTenantId from the secret because the Azure SDK for Go prioritizes the AZURE_TENANT_ID environment variable over programmatically provided values.

body_text:
# Summary

With Argo CD introducing OCI as a first-class supported repository type in its 3.1 release, it should also support Workload Identity in the same way that other first‑class repo types such as Git and Helm do.

# Motivation

Workload Identity provides a secure way for workloads running in an AKS (Azure Kubernetes Service) cluster to authenticate to other Azure resources.
A common scenario is that Argo CD components are deployed in AKS and use an ACR (Azure Container Registry) registry as the OCI backend for storing artifacts. Using a username and password for authentication is error‑prone and insecure. To improve security, Argo CD should support Workload Identity for OCI registries, closing this current gap.

# Proposal

The proposed implementation follows a similar pattern to the earlier Workload Identity PR: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/pull/21118/changes

Introduce an abstract credential interface:
```go
type Creds interface {
	GetUsername() string
	GetPassword() (string, error)
	GetCAPath() string
	GetCertData() []byte
	GetKeyData() []byte
	GetInsecureSkipVerify() bool
}
```
Then provide two implementations:

1.  OCICreds: Standard OCI Credentials

```go
type OCICreds struct {
	Username           string
	Password           string
	CAPath             string
	CertData           []byte
	KeyData            []byte
	InsecureSkipVerify bool
}
```

2. AzureWorkloadIdentityCreds: Workload Identity for Azure

```go
type AzureWorkloadIdentityCreds struct {
	repoUrl            string
	CAPath             string
	CertData           []byte
	KeyData            []byte
	InsecureSkipVerify bool
	tokenProvider      workloadidentity.TokenProvider
}
```
