### Description of the bug:


[StarlarkAttrTransitionProviderTest#.testTransitionOnBuildSetting_noSuchTarget](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/31c4c24667be57195b01548952409d891576c877/src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/analysis/starlark/StarlarkAttrTransitionProviderTest.java#L2725) is a simple test that transitioning on a non-existent flag returns a "no such target" error.

Comment out these lines:

https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/31c4c24667be57195b01548952409d891576c877/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/analysis/producers/TransitionApplier.java#L120-L124

then run:

```
$ USE_BAZEL_VERSION=9.0.1rc1 bazelisk test   //src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/analysis/starlark:StarlarkAttrTransitionProviderTest --test_filter=.testTransitionOnBuildSetting_noSuchTarget --test_output=errors
```

It now fails with:

```
java.lang.IllegalStateException: Unexpected analysis error: ConfiguredTargetKey{label=//test/starlark:test, config=BuildConfigurationKey[1d3999f38bc198a7ca1cbe23f490a4a0ab9d8b194fcd3960c0c8e6b62206a781]} -> ErrorInfo{exception=com.google.devtools.build.lib.analysis.starlark.StarlarkTransition$TransitionException: com.google.devtools.build.lib.packages.NoSuchTargetException: no such target '//test/starlark:the-answer': target 'the-answer' not declared in package 'test/starlark' defined by /workspace/test/starlark
```

### Analysis:

The test target `//test/starlark:test` has an explicit exec dependency on `$function_transition_allowlist`.

The test intentionally triggers an error on a *different* Skyframe evaluation: the one that tries to load `//test/starlark:the-answer`, which doesn't exist.

Before the suggested change, https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/31c4c24667be57195b01548952409d891576c877/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/analysis/producers/TransitionApplier.java#L123

runs and completes before the failing thread runs. Since `applyStarlarkTransition` runs the Starlark thread that evaluates the exec transition, that means the exec transition completes successfully before Skyframe finds errors in other evaluations.

After the suggested change, this now runs: https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/31c4c24667be57195b01548952409d891576c877/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/analysis/producers/TransitionApplier.java#L129

I'm pretty sure  that means Skyframe's currently running `Driver` completes, which gives the failing evaluation time to schedule and fail, then a new `Driver` evaluation runs on `applyStarlarkTransition`, which means the exec transition is evaluated after Skyiframe already knows there's a problem elsewhere.

That means that `StarlarkThread` calls:

https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/31c4c24667be57195b01548952409d891576c877/src/main/java/net/starlark/java/eval/StarlarkThread.java#L123-L125

which `DependencyResolver` catches [here](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/31c4c24667be57195b01548952409d891576c877/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/skyframe/DependencyResolver.java#L749) as an exceptional case, which triggers the failure.

I experimentally verified that sequencing. i..e I *know* the `StarlarkThread` interrupt triggers only after this change, and before this change the whole evaluation completes before the "no such target" evaluation fails.  I'm not quite as confident what the principled answer is, although a simple catching of the `InterruptedException` [here](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/31c4c24667be57195b01548952409d891576c877/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/analysis/producers/TransitionApplier.java#L158) should practically resolve it.


### Which category does this issue belong to?

Configurability


### Which operating system are you running Bazel on?


Linux

### Description of the feature request:


@thesayyn has been studying the new https://developer.apple.com/documentation/FSKit API introduced in recent versions of MacOS. We believe this could allow a sandbox implementation that's both fast and isolated, in the sense that it avoids common sandbox escaping by following symlinks.

Background:
- Current implementation is substantially slower than `local` spawn: https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/8230 from 2019
- NodeJS tooling *always* follows symlinks, even when implemented in Go or Rust. Thus the new Go implementation of the TypeScript type-checker can't run in a Bazel sandbox, along with ESbuild, SWC, OXC, and so on. https://github.com/aspect-build/rules_js/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aopen%20sandbox lists some of the issues
- The `docker` strategy gives a stronger isolation but is impractical since it doesn't re-use containers.
- Sahin has some experiments at https://github.com/thesayyn/sandboxfs

Alternatives:
- Replace eager symlink creation with an on-demand userland filesystem
- If cross-device hardlinks were permitted, it might help. The kernel security system might need changes.
- MacFUSE has a FSkit implementation now, but you have to reduce secure boot.
- bb-clientd uses an NFS approach but it's brittle (@jsharpe)

{"repository": "bazelbuild/bazel", "task_candidate_id": 2245, "repository_id": 44, "issue_number": 29165, "github_issue_id": 4180874311, "html_url": "https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/29165", "created_at": "2026-03-31T17:07:43+00:00", "author_association": "CONTRIBUTOR", "title": "Stronger MacOS Sandbox with FSKit", "body_text": "### Description of the feature request:


@thesayyn has been studying the new https://developer.apple.com/documentation/FSKit API introduced in recent versions of MacOS. We believe this could allow a sandbox implementation that's both fast and isolated, in the sense that it avoids common sandbox escaping by following symlinks.

Background:
- Current implementation is substantially slower than `local` spawn: https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/8230 from 2019
- NodeJS tooling *always* follows symlinks, even when implemented in Go or Rust. Thus the new Go implementation of the TypeScript type-checker can't run in a Bazel sandbox, along with ESbuild, SWC, OXC, and so on. https://github.com/aspect-build/rules_js/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aopen%20sandbox lists some of the issues
- The `docker` strategy gives a stronger isolation but is impractical since it doesn't re-use containers.
- Sahin has some experiments at https://github.com/thesayyn/sandboxfs

Alternatives:
- Replace eager symlink creation with an on-demand userland filesystem
- If cross-device hardlinks were permitted, it might help. The kernel security system might need changes.
- MacFUSE has a FSkit implementation now, but you have to reduce secure boot.
- bb-clientd uses an NFS approach but it's brittle (@jsharpe)

body_text: ### Description of the bug: When trying running bazel7.4.1 on risc-v platform, Illegal instruction happends. GDB it we figured that is because the abseil module: Missing separate debuginfos, use: dnf debuginfo-install glibc-2.38-34.eos30.riscv64 [Thread debugging using libthread_db enabled] Using host libthread_db library "/usr/lib64/libthread_db.so.1". [New Thread 0x7ffff73ff0a0 (LWP 285921)] [New Thread 0x7fffee9ff0a0 (LWP 285922)] [New Thread 0x7ffff6bfe0a0 (LWP 285923)] Thread 2 "default-executo" received signal SIGILL, Illegal instruction. [Switching to Thread 0x7ffff73ff0a0 (LWP 285921)] 0x0000555555863180 in absl::lts_20230125::base_internal::UnscaledCycleClock::Now() () Missing separate debuginfos, use: dnf debuginfo-install libgcc-12.3.1-33.eos30.riscv64 And this is because "starting with Linux 6.6 [1], RDCYCLE is a privileged instruction on RISC-V and can't be used directly from userland. There is a sysctl option to change that as a transition period, but it will eventually disappear. The RDTIME instruction is another less accurate alternative, however its frequency varies from board to board, and there is currently now way to get its frequency from userland" more detail could be found in https://github.com/abseil/abseil-cpp/pull/1644 Which refers that this is actually a fixed bug. But When I try to fix it, I can't find absl/base/internal/unscaledcycleclock.cc Could you help me？ ### Which category does this issue belong to? _No response_ ### What's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? ### Description of the feature request:


Skip an incompatible target only if there exists some configuration under which it can be built; otherwise fail the build as there is a target that is unbuildable by any configuration.

### Which category does this issue belong to?

Configurability

### What underlying problem are you trying to solve with this feature?


When a user runs `bazel build --platforms=//platforms:linux_x86_64 //...`, they expect to build everything in that closure that can be built for linux x86_64. This is useful as some targets have dependencies that are only compatible with certain platforms e.g. freebsd_arm64, and skipping makes sense here. However, this behavior can hide an unbuildable target introduced by a new dependency.

Consider the following example:

```
# BUILD.bazel

linux_image(
    name = "linux_image",
    efi = "//:efi_image", # transitions to uefi
)

efi_image(
    name = "efi_image",
    deps = [
       ...
       "//:lib",
    ]
)

cc_library(
    name = "lib",
    srcs = [...],
    deps = [
        "...",
        "//:new_lib", # new dependency gets added
    ], 
)

# incompatible with uefi
cc_library(
    name = "new_lib",
    srcs = [...],
    target_compatible_with = ["@platforms//os:linux"], 
)
```

//:linux_image should be compatible with the requested platform, but it is skipped because a transitive dependency (//:new_lib) is incompatible in the uefi configuration introduced by the efi transition. Since that transition happens regardless of the top-level platform, no configuration can build //:linux_image. Skipping in this case hides an unconditionally broken dependency graph, so it should fail loudly.

### Which operating system are you running Bazel on?


Linux

### What is the output of `bazel info release`?


release 8.5.1

### Description of the feature request:


Allow the module override functions (git_override, archive_override, local_path_override) to get their key value (e.g. commit) from an environment variable. This is to allow easily customizing module overrides without having
to modify MODULE.bazel.

So one would do e.g.

```
git_override(
  name = "rules_foo",
  branch = "${RULES_FOO_COMMIT:-deadbeef}",
)
```

For repo rules, this is mostly already possible by creating custom repo rules. There isn't a equivalent for module overrides, though.

### Which category does this issue belong to?

_No response_

### What underlying problem are you trying to solve with this feature?


The general problem to solve is when you want to follow the bleeding edge version of code. For example, say you want to use the latest (or near latest) code from a project using git_override.


Using branch=master somewhat works, but has two downsides:
1. You have near-zero control over what commit is used
2. You have very little visibility into what commit was used
3. Subsequent invocations may use a different commit, depending on the bazel cache state, exacerbating non-determinism.

While an automated system could modify MODULE.bazel, that imposes a large engineering cost in various ways. Operating such a system is a decent amount of overhead. More importantly, if one wanted to track the bleeding edge of multiple dependencies, it means the commit rate of changes to MODULE.bazel is the sum of all those dependencies.

Comparatively, it is trivial to, for example, have a GHA job runs some shell to compute a commit (e.g. latest commit mod hour), persist that somewhere, then run a second job with that commit in an environment variable. This then yields relatively stable and deterministic behavior while still tracking near head.

### Which operating system are you running Bazel on?


linux

### Description of the bug:


When a C++20 module interface is supplied through `cc_library.module_interfaces`, Bazel's LLVM coverage report does not include that source file. Ordinary C++ sources in `srcs` are reported as expected.

This reproduces with Bazel 9.2.0, the default `rules_cc`, Clang, and LLVM native coverage.


### Which category does this issue belong to?

C++ Rules

### What's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.


https://github.com/PikachuHyA/bazel_cxx20_modules_demo/tree/main/hello_module_coverage

https://github.com/PikachuHyA/bazel_cxx20_modules_demo/actions/runs/34828654074/job/103926525923 shows the different coverage dat file

```starlark
load("@rules_cc//cc:defs.bzl", "cc_library", "cc_test")

cc_library(
    name = "lib2",
    module_interfaces = ["lib.cppm"],
    features = ["cpp_modules"],
)

cc_test(
    name = "test_with_module",
    srcs = ["test.cc"],
    copts = ["-DUSE_MODULE"],
    deps = [":lib2"],
    features = ["cpp_modules"],
)
```

`test.cc` imports `lib` and executes a function implemented in `lib.cppm`.

Coverage configuration:

```text
coverage --instrument_test_targets
coverage --experimental_use_llvm_covmap
coverage --experimental_generate_llvm_lcov
coverage --repo_env=BAZEL_USE_LLVM_NATIVE_COVERAGE=1
coverage --repo_env=BAZEL_LLVM_COV=llvm-cov
coverage --repo_env=BAZEL_LLVM_PROFDATA=llvm-profdata
```

Run:

```bash
bazel coverage :test_with_module --nocache_test_results
cat bazel-out/_coverage/_coverage_report.dat
```




### Which operating system are you running Bazel on?


ubuntu 24.04

### What is the output of `bazel info release`?


release 9.2.0

### If `bazel info release` returns `development version` or `(@non-git)`, tell us how you built Bazel.


_No response_

### What's the output of `git remote get-url origin; git rev-parse HEAD` ?


```text

```

### If this is a regression, please try to identify the Bazel commit where the bug was introduced with bazelisk --bisect.


_No response_

### Have you found anything relevant by searching the web?

_No response_

### Any other information, logs, or outputs that you want to share?


## Proposed direction

Add an optional `unfiltered_source_attributes` parameter to `coverage_common.instrumented_files_info`. `InstrumentedFilesCollector` should collect artifacts from these attributes without applying the source-extension filter, while still applying Bazel's instrumentation filter.

Then `rules_cc` could use:

```starlark
coverage_common.instrumented_files_info(
    ctx = ctx,
    source_attributes = ["srcs", "hdrs"],
    unfiltered_source_attributes = ["module_interfaces"],
    extensions = source_extensions,
)
```

### Description of the feature request:


Introduce the concept of aspect "reducers", which would run once per aspect, over all derivations of that aspect.

This would allow an aspect to accumulate and process the results of all aspect applications in an invocation, for example (using CLI as the demo case, but the same principles apply to any aspect application) `bazel test --aspects=//aspect.bzl:my_reducer --output_groups +my_reduced_results //a //b //c` could  return a single output, which is the result of `my_reducer((reduced_aspect(//a), //a), (reduced_aspect(//b), //b), (reduced_aspect(//c), //c))`.

This could come in the form of either an additional 'reduction' step for an aspects, or a special form of aspect that only functions in the reduction case and can require other aspects.

A few further ideas:
- It may be sensible to support 'sharding' reducers, if the reducer is known to be commutative it would make sense to for example allow applying the reducer on a per-package (or some other stable method of subdivision) basis for improved caching at the cost of additional actions. 
  If done per-package I have a suspicion that fact will be relied on, so worth keeping in mind.
  ```mermaid
  graph TD;
      R[R //...] --> R'(R' //pkg1);
      R' --> A(//pkg1:target1);
      R' --> B(//pkg1:target2);
      R --> R''(R'' //pkg2);
      R --> C(//:target1);
      R'' --> D(//pkg2:target1);
      R'' --> R'''(R''' //pkg2/pkg3);
      R''' --> E(//pkg2/pkg3:target1);
  ```
  (Note: this graph is from the POV of a reduction over //..., the general result of the sharding process would differ by perspective.)


@fmeum seems to have further ideas as to the details of this functionality.

### Which category does this issue belong to?

_No response_

### What underlying problem are you trying to solve with this feature?


I am attempting to address several issues at once with our company build setup:
- Provide a way to accumulate an SBOM for an entire repository, by computing the sum of SBOMs across all deployable targets. 
  This involves reducing the output of our SBOM aspects into one unified report and is currently achievable through our bazel frontend, but is not cached as part of the build as a result despite how aggressively cache-friendly it is.
- Provide a way to accumulate test reports specific to our internal tooling.

### Description of the bug:

With `--collect_code_coverage` and `--experimental_worker_multiplex_sandboxing` enabled together, **every** Java compile fails:

```
ERROR: BUILD.bazel:14:13: Building liblib.jar (2 source files) failed: (Exit 1):
  java failed: error executing Javac command (from target //:lib) ...
java.io.FileNotFoundException:
  <output_base>/bazel-workers/Javac-multiplex-worker-1-workdir/_main/
  bazel-out/darwin_arm64-fastbuild/bin/liblib-paths-for-coverage.txt (No such file or directory)
```

Both flags are required, and the toolchain must set `javac_supports_worker_multiplex_sandboxing = True`. `rules_java`'s stock toolchains leave it at `False`, which makes `--experimental_worker_multiplex_sandboxing` a no-op for Javac, so the bug is invisible with a default setup.

| `--collect_code_coverage` | `--experimental_worker_multiplex_sandboxing` | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| yes | yes | **FileNotFoundException** |
| yes | no | ok |
| no | yes | ok |
| no | no | ok |

**Cause.** `<target>-paths-for-coverage.txt` is a declared input of the Javac action and *is* staged correctly, into the per-request sandbox directory:

```
.../Javac-multiplex-worker-1-workdir/_main/__sandbox/1/_main/bazel-out/.../liblib-paths-for-coverage.txt   ← staged here
.../Javac-multiplex-worker-1-workdir/_main/bazel-out/.../liblib-paths-for-coverage.txt                     ← opened here
```

A sandboxed multiplex worker's process working directory is the multiplexer's, while each request's inputs live under the `__sandbox/<id>/` subdir named by `WorkRequest.sandbox_dir`. JavaBuilder resolves execroot-relative paths against that per-request dir (`JavaLibraryBuildRequest.asPath`), but the `--post_processor jacoco <file>` argument never went through it — [`JacocoInstrumentationProcessor.java`](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/master/src/java_tools/buildjar/java/com/google/devtools/build/buildjar/instrumentation/JacocoInstrumentationProcessor.java) does:

```java
jar.addEntry(coverageInformation, Path.of(coverageInformation));
```

`Path.of` on a relative path resolves against the process working directory, so the lookup lands one level of `__sandbox/<id>/` too high. It only surfaces with both flags because the argument only exists under `--collect_code_coverage`, and the working directory only diverges from the request dir under multiplex sandboxing.

**Why it matters.** Path mapping skips persistent-worker actions unless the worker is sandboxed, so a repository that wants Java actions to participate in `--experimental_output_paths=strip` is pushed toward `--experimental_worker_multiplex_sandboxing` (as suggested in #22658). Doing that makes `bazel coverage` unusable. The only workarounds are giving up multiplex workers for Javac (`--strategy=Javac=sandboxed`) or leaving Java out of path mapping.

This is *not* a path-mapping bug on its own — it reproduces with `--experimental_output_paths=off`, at the unstripped path. With `--experimental_output_paths=strip` the same failure is reported at the stripped path, which makes it easy to misattribute.

### Which category does this issue belong to?

Java Rules, Local Execution

### What's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.

```sh
bazel clean
bazel build --collect_code_coverage --experimental_worker_multiplex_sandboxing //:lib
```

`bazel clean` matters: neither flag is part of the action key, so a cached result from a previous invocation masks the failure.

`BUILD.bazel`:

```starlark
load("@rules_java//toolchains:default_java_toolchain.bzl", "default_java_toolchain")
load("@rules_java//java:defs.bzl", "java_library")

# The only non-default ingredient.
default_java_toolchain(
    name = "java_toolchain_sandboxed_mux",
    javac_supports_worker_multiplex_sandboxing = True,
    source_version = "17",
    target_version = "17",
)

java_library(
    name = "lib",
    srcs = ["src/main/java/com/example/A.java"],
)
```

`.bazelrc`:

```
build --extra_toolchains=//:java_toolchain_sandboxed_mux_definition
build --java_language_version=17
build --java_runtime_version=remotejdk_17
```

with `MODULE.bazel` depending on `rules_java` 9.3.0 and any trivial `A.java`.

### Which operating system are you running Bazel on?

macOS 26.6.2, arm64

### What is the output of `bazel info release`?

`release 9.2.0`

I verified the failure directly on 9.2.0 and 8.6.0. It is also reported on 8.7.0 and 8.8.0, which I did not run myself.

### If this is a regression, please try to identify the Bazel commit where the bug was introduced with bazelisk --bisect.

Not a regression as far as I can tell — it appears to have been broken since sandboxed multiplex worker support was added for JavaBuilder. I did not bisect.

### Have you found anything relevant by searching the web?

No existing issue found. #22658 is the discussion that recommends enabling `javac_supports_worker_multiplex_sandboxing`, which is what puts a repository into the broken configuration.

### Any other information, logs, or outputs that you want to share?

Fix proposed in #31151: resolve the coverage-paths file against the request's working directory, like every other path in `JavaLibraryBuildRequest`. The jar *entry* name stays execroot-relative — `JacocoCoverageRunner` matches it by its `-paths-for-coverage.txt` suffix only, so the rewritten name that path mapping produces is harmless.

### Description of the bug:


In **Bazel 9**, configuring `--flag_alias` with a negated Starlark flag (e.g. `build --flag_alias=nobool=no@bazel_skylib//lib:bool` or `no//pkg:flag`) passes the initial prefix check in `FlagAliasConverter`, but fails option parsing / analysis with an unhandled `LabelSyntaxException: invalid package name 'no@...': package names may not contain '//' path separators`.

### Which category does this issue belong to?

CLI, Configurability, Core

### What's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.


- pkg/BUILD.bazel

```python
load("@bazel_skylib//rules:common_settings.bzl", "bool_flag")

bool_flag(
    name = "my_feature",
    build_setting_default = True,
)
```

- .bazelrc
```bash
build --flag_alias=nomy_feature=no@demo//pkg:my_feature
```
- MODULE.bazel
```python
module(name = "demo")
bazel_dep(name = "bazel_skylib", version = "1.8.2")
```

CLI:
```bash
$ export USE_BAZEL_VERSION=9.2.0
$ gbazelisk build //pkg:my_feature --nobuild
```

### Which operating system are you running Bazel on?


x86_64 GNU/Linux

### What is the output of `bazel info release`?


release 9.2.0

### If `bazel info release` returns `development version` or `(@non-git)`, tell us how you built Bazel.


N/A

### What's the output of `git remote get-url origin; git rev-parse HEAD` ?


```text

```

### If this is a regression, please try to identify the Bazel commit where the bug was introduced with bazelisk --bisect.


Ran bazelisk bisect
```
$ bazelisk --bisect=9.0.0..9.2.0 build //pkg:my_feature --nobuild
...
--- Bisect Result

first bad commit is https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/commit/897af1683dd5fe69c0be60975f6a96c5a0e4b8dc
```

### Have you found anything relevant by searching the web?

From LLM:

#### Root Cause in Bazel codebase: In CoreOptionConverters.java:

1. `FlagAliasConverter `validates the RHS of `--flag_alias` using `STARLARK_SKIPPED_PREFIXES` (`["--//", "--no//", "--@", "--no@"]`), which explicitly allows `--no@` and `--no//`.
1. It then calls `convertOptionsLabel(longForm, conversionContext)`, which expects a standard Label string.
1. Because `no@...` does not start with `@` or `/`, `convertOptionsLabel` prepends `//`, producing `//no@demo//pkg:my_feature`.
1. `Label.parseWithRepoContext()` attempts to parse `no@demo//pkg:my_feature` as a package name, throwing LabelSyntaxException: package names may not contain '//' path separators.


### Any other information, logs, or outputs that you want to share?

Observed error:

```
ERROR: While parsing option --flag_alias=nobool=no@bazel_skylib//lib:bool: invalid package name 'no@bazel_skylib//lib': package names may not contain '//' path separators

### Description of the feature request:


Bazel should provide an experimental build mode that completes loading and analysis, then evaluates only an eligible subset of Bazel-owned actions that are known not to start a process. The initial set could include deterministic file writes, template expansion, manifests, direct symlinks, and runfiles/symlink-tree creation.

Eligibility should be fail-closed and attached to audited action implementations, rather than inferred from mnemonic, rule kind, or language. An eligible action should run only when all of its generated inputs are produced by other eligible actions. Spawns, workers, tests, input-discovering actions, and unknown implementations should remain unevaluated.

Selected actions should use Bazel's normal action executor, validation, action cache, and Skyframe values. Deferred actions should receive no successful value, cache entry, placeholder metadata, or error node. The analyzed graph and successful selected-action values should remain available to the next command in the same Bazel server. The command should report selected, materialized, deferred, and unresolved counts through BEP.

### Which category does this issue belong to?

Core

### What underlying problem are you trying to solve with this feature?


A long-lived Bazel server can prepare a repository before a real build arrives. `--nobuild` preserves analysis but does not materialize deterministic metadata created during analysis. A normal build also runs arbitrary user commands.

Forcing spawns through an unreachable executor happens to let some Bazel-owned in-process actions finish, but it represents the intended stopping point as a build failure and leaves failed Skyframe nodes. Fabricating action-cache or REv2 results would instead claim that deferred outputs exist. Neither is a sound boundary.

We have a prototype on Bazel 9.2.0rc1. In a mixed-language repository it visited 1,393 actions, materialized 506 audited in-process actions, deferred 887, and started no subprocesses. A following build in the same server reused the analysis graph and selected action values. Output comparison found 34,238 matching entries and no mismatches.

### Which operating system are you running Bazel on?


Linux ARM64 for the snapshot workload; development and tests also run on macOS ARM64.

### What is the output of `bazel info release`?


release 9.2.0rc1 (`313773c665866583223f6f59148d373d405edc82`)

### If `bazel info release` returns `development version` or `(@non-git)`, tell us how you built Bazel.


_No response_

### What's the output of `git remote get-url origin; git rev-parse HEAD` ?


```text

```

### Have you found anything relevant by searching the web?

- #11194 proposes serializing the analysis cache. That could eventually make analysis portable across servers, but would not materialize these metadata outputs.
- #14179 concerns retaining multiple analyses in one server.
- #30877 tracks materialization in existing completion values and appears compatible with this proposal.
- #24921 and #26045 make file writes and symlinks lazy. This mode would need explicit eager semantics for selected actions.
- #30635 proposes metadata-only remote-cache results. This proposal stays within local Skyframe evaluation and does not change REv2 or represent deferred actions as successful.

### Any other information, logs, or outputs that you want to share?

The prototype is implemented and tested, but has not yet been ported to `master`. Before preparing a PR, feedback would be useful on:

1. where the internal process-free capability should live;
2. which built-in actions should be admitted initially; and
3. whether the result belongs in a dedicated BEP event or existing execution metrics.

body_text:
### Description of the feature request:


With `--experimental_remote_repo_contents_cache`, a cache-hit repo is injected into the in-memory `RemoteExternalFileSystem` and only `.bzl` / `REPO.bazel` files are written under `<output_base>/external/<repo>` (`RemoteExternalOverlayFileSystem#shouldPrefetch`). Bazel itself and local actions read the rest lazily, but a tool running *outside* the Bazel server has no supported way to learn the contents of those files: they are not on disk, and no query output exposes them.

I'd like one (ideally the first) of the following:

1. **Source-file digests in query output.** An opt-in flag, e.g. `--proto:source_file_digests`, that adds `digest` (and `is_executable`) to the `SourceFile` message for `query`/`cquery --output=proto|streamed_proto|jsonproto`. For in-memory repos Bazel already holds the digest from the cached `Directory` tree (`RemoteExternalOverlayFileSystem#getDigest`), so this costs no downloads. For on-disk files it could use `getFastDigest` and fall back to hashing. Restricting it to external repos would be fine if main-repo cost is a concern.
2. **A supported way to materialize specific repos.** e.g. `bazel fetch --repo=@@foo --materialize` (name is a strawman), wired to the existing `LazyMaterializer#ensureMaterialized`. Today `bazel fetch --remote_download_all` does not materialize; the only thing that works is building each source file as a top-level target (`bazel build --remote_download_all @@repo//:path/to/file`), which doesn't scale to tens of thousands of files.
3. **A per-repo tree digest.** Expose the root `Directory` digest of an injected repo (e.g. in `bazel mod show_repo --output=streamed_proto`, or a file next to the marker file). A tool with remote cache access could then walk the CAS itself. This is the least convenient for tools but the smallest change.

Independently of which option is chosen, a way to **detect** the situation would help: currently an external tool cannot distinguish "file is remote-backed and only in memory" from "file does not exist".

### Which category does this issue belong to?

External Dependency

### What underlying problem are you trying to solve with this feature?


I maintain [bazel-diff](https://github.com/Tinder/bazel-diff), which computes a hash per target at two commits and diffs them to find the affected targets. The pattern (shared with target-determinator and similar tools) is:

1. `bazel query`/`cquery --output=streamed_proto` to get the target graph.
2. For every `SourceFile` target, read the file from disk and hash its contents. For labels in external repos the path is `$(bazel info output_base)/external/<canonical repo>/<pkg>/<file>`.
3. Combine rule attribute hashes with the hashes of transitive inputs.

Step 2 silently breaks under the remote repo contents cache. The files aren't on disk, so they hash as "missing", and the result depends on which repos happened to be materialized on that machine. A user reported this in Tinder/bazel-diff#506 (Bazel 9.2.0, RBE, `--remote_download_minimal`): same commit, identical target graph (200,599 targets), but 51,917 file-not-found warnings with the cache enabled vs. 85 without, and 3,884 target hashes changed with no source change. That turns into a large set of false-positive "affected" targets in CI.

We can (and will) make bazel-diff fail loudly instead of silently, but we cannot make it *correct* without help from Bazel:

- Turning the flag off for the bazel-diff invocation isn't practical. It's a startup option, so toggling it restarts the server and discards the analysis cache, and it forces the full repo downloads the flag exists to avoid.
- Building every external source file as a top-level target to force materialization is O(files) targets on the command line and downloads everything.
- Reading the repo's cached tree from the remote cache ourselves would mean reimplementing Bazel's repo cache key computation, which is internal and unstable.

Option 1 is the best fit: the tool never needs the bytes, only a stable content identity, and Bazel already has it in memory. It would also let these tools stop re-hashing external files that Bazel has already digested, even when the repo contents cache is off.

### Which operating system are you running Bazel on?


Linux amd64 (reported); the behaviour is platform-independent

### What is the output of `bazel info release`?


release 9.2.0

### If `bazel info release` returns `development version` or `(@non-git)`, tell us how you built Bazel.


_No response_

### What's the output of `git remote get-url origin; git rev-parse HEAD` ?


```text

```

### Have you found anything relevant by searching the web?

- Tinder/bazel-diff#506: the downstream report with the numbers above.
- #27509: the feature discussion; tooling outside Bazel reading repo contents isn't covered.
- #31005: the opposite direction (repos being materialized too eagerly by `readFile` in module extensions). A fix there makes fewer files reach disk, so external tools will see this more often, not less.
- #29656, #30217: local actions needing materialization. Those were fixed inside Bazel via the prefetcher / `ensureMaterializedBelow`; external tools have no equivalent hook.

### Any other information, logs, or outputs that you want to share?

How bazel-diff would consume each option:

| Option | bazel-diff change | Bytes downloaded | Hashes identical with flag on/off |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. digests in query proto | Pass the flag on the query we already run; mix `SourceFile.digest` + exec bit into the target hash instead of reading the file | none | yes, if digests are emitted for on-disk repos too |
| 2. materialize command | Run it for the repos the user asked us to hash file-by-file, then read from `output_base/external` as today | full repo | yes |
| 3. per-repo tree digest | Hash the tree digest per repo; per-file granularity would need our own CAS client | none | only at whole-repo granularity |

Notes on option 1:

- The digest function (`--digest_function`) only needs to be stable for a given configuration; consumers mix the bytes in opaquely. Including the function name in the output would let tools detect a mismatch between two runs.
- Symlinks: reporting the digest of the resolved target (what an action would see) is what consumers want.
- Source directories could be left without a digest in a first version.

There are a few changes that didn't land in 8.8.0 such as RepMaxCDC and we'd like to see the clonefile support backported to the 8.x series so this is a request for a 8.9.0 release with these changes backported.

As 8.x is the last release to still support WORKSPACE, I think this holds some value for users that have constraints that slow their migration to bzlmod and hence the 9.x series or newer.

### Description of the feature request:

I'd like a `%bazelrc_dir%` placeholder that expands to the directory of the rc file it is written in. It would work in option values and in `import` / `try-import` paths:

```
# /opt/tools/corp-bazel/corp.bazelrc, loaded with BAZELRC=/opt/tools/corp-bazel/corp.bazelrc
startup --host_jvm_args=-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore=%bazelrc_dir%/cacerts.p12
common --downloader_config=%bazelrc_dir%/downloader.cfg
```

The client would replace it while parsing the rc file in `RcFile::ParseFile`. The parser already knows the canonical path of each file, so this is a small change and it works the same for startup and command options.

### Which category does this issue belong to?

Core

### What underlying problem are you trying to solve with this feature?

We ship company wide Bazel settings to developers and CI machines: a trust store for our corporate CA and a downloader config that points to our internal mirror. They are installed by a package manager into a directory that is different on every machine and for every version, and we load them with `BAZELRC`.

The rc file can't point to the files that sit next to it:

* Relative paths in option values are resolved against the workspace, and relative `import` paths against the current working directory.
* `%workspace%` points into the repository, but these files are not part of any repository.
* There is no way to use environment variables in rc files (#10904). The client also ignores `JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS`, `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` and `_JAVA_OPTIONS`, so we can't pass the trust store that way either.

Right now the only options are to generate the rc file on every machine or to wrap the `bazel` binary so it adds absolute paths. Both are fragile.

#3050 asked for relative `import` paths and was closed because `%workspace%` is clearer than a relative path, where it isn't obvious what the path is relative to. This proposal has the same clarity. The placeholder always means the directory of the file it appears in. `%workspace%` stays the right tool for config inside the repository, and `%bazelrc_dir%` would cover config that lives outside of it.

### Which operating system are you running Bazel on?

Linux, macOS, Windows

### What is the output of `bazel info release`?

release 9.2.0

### If `bazel info release` returns `development version` or `(@non-git)`, tell us how you built Bazel.

_No response_

### What's the output of `git remote get-url origin; git rev-parse HEAD` ?

_No response_

### Have you found anything relevant by searching the web?

* #3050: relative `import` paths, closed in favour of `%workspace%`
* #10904: environment variables in `.bazelrc`
* #28725: `%workspace%` in `--downloader_config`
* #27447 and #27675: version conditional imports, where substitution and a dedicated syntax were discussed

### Any other information, logs, or outputs that you want to share?

An existing rc file that contains the literal text `%bazelrc_dir%` would now be expanded. I doubt anyone relies on that. Older Bazel versions keep the placeholder as plain text, so an rc file that is shared across versions can wrap it in `try-import-if-bazel-version`.

I have a working implementation with tests and docs and would be happy to open a PR if the idea and the name work for you.

We ship company wide Bazel settings to developers and CI machines: a trust store for our corporate CA and a downloader config that points to our internal mirror. They are installed by a package manager into a directory that is different on every machine and for every version, and we load them with `BAZELRC`.

The rc file can't point to the files that sit next to it:

* Relative paths in option values are resolved against the workspace, and relative `import` paths against the current working directory.
* `%workspace%` points into the repository, but these files are not part of any repository.
* There is no way to use environment variables in rc files (#10904). The client also ignores `JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS`, `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` and `_JAVA_OPTIONS`, so we can't pass the trust store that way either.

Right now the only options are to generate the rc file on every machine or to wrap the `bazel` binary so it adds absolute paths. Both are fragile.

#3050 asked for relative `import` paths and was closed because `%workspace%` is clearer than a relative path, where it isn't obvious what the path is relative to. This proposal has the same clarity. The placeholder always means the directory of the file it appears in. `%workspace%` stays the right tool for config inside the repository, and `%bazelrc_dir%` would cover config that lives outside of it.

### Which operating system are you running Bazel on?

Linux, macOS, Windows

### What is the output of `bazel info release`?

release 9.2.0

### If `bazel info release` returns `development version` or `(@non-git)`, tell us how you built Bazel.

_No response_

### What's the output of `git remote get-url origin; git rev-parse HEAD` ?

_No response_

### Have you found anything relevant by searching the web?

* #3050: relative `import` paths, closed in favour of `%workspace%`
* #10904: environment variables in `.bazelrc`
* #28725: `%workspace%` in `--downloader_config`
* #27447 and #27675: version conditional imports, where substitution and a dedicated syntax were discussed

### Any other information, logs, or outputs that you want to share?

An existing rc file that contains the literal text `%bazelrc_dir%` would now be expanded. I doubt anyone relies on that. Older Bazel versions keep the placeholder as plain text, so an rc file that is shared across versions can wrap it in `try-import-if-bazel-version`.

I have a working implementation with tests and docs and would be happy to open a PR if the idea and the name work for you.

`docs/run/build.mdx`, at 7a5be08 and on bazel.build on 2026-09-24, says: "Bazel will print a warning if your system does not support sandboxing to alert you to the fact that builds are not guaranteed to be hermetic and might affect the host system in unknown ways. To disable this warning you can pass the `--ignore_unsupported_sandboxing` flag to Bazel."

The warning was removed in 0c613be in April 2017. The flag lived on as a no-op until e887cfbfd641 removed it from master in November 2025, "Delete a no-op flag (`--ignore_unsupported_sandboxing`) and documentation referencing it", cherry-picked to 9.0.0 as #27747. `build.mdx` was not part of that change. The paragraph is also in the 9.0.0 and 9.1.0 versioned docs.

Bazel 9.2.0 rejects the flag before building anything:

```
ERROR: --ignore_unsupported_sandboxing :: Unrecognized option: --ignore_unsupported_sandboxing
```

On Linux (Debian 13, kernel 6.12), with user namespaces unavailable to Bazel because I ran it inside `bwrap --unshare-user --disable-userns`, 9.2.0 fell back to processwrapper-sandbox and printed no warning in the console. The process summary named `processwrapper-sandbox` instead of `linux-sandbox`, and the server's `java.log` had one warning-level line. The fallback itself is tracked in #13995. This is only about the paragraph. I didn't run macOS.

`sandboxing.mdx` already describes the fallback and how to get an error instead, so `build.mdx` could point there.

body_text:
I read Bazel's pages on sandboxing at 7a5be08, and on bazel.build on 2026-09-24. They disagree about what the sandbox does.

`docs/docs/sandboxing.mdx` says: "Sandboxing doesn't hide the host environment in any way. Processes can freely access all files on the file system." It says network access can optionally be prevented. By default it isn't: `--sandbox_default_allow_network` defaults to true.

Other pages say the opposite. `docs/run/build.mdx` says "Bazel uses sandboxes to guarantee that actions run hermetically and correctly", and a few lines later defines hermeticity as an action using only its declared input files. In `docs/basics/artifact-based-builds.mdx`, actions "are unable to read any files they don’t declare", and "Bazel also uses sandboxes to restrict actions from communicating via the network."

I ran Bazel 9.2.0 on Linux only, Debian 13 with kernel 6.12, under the default linux-sandbox. A genrule read a file outside the workspace that it had not declared. Another opened a TCP connection to 1.1.1.1:443. With `--sandbox_block_path` on that file the read got `Permission denied`, and with `tags = ["block-network"]` the connection failed with `Network is unreachable`. So `sandboxing.mdx` describes the default and the other two pages don't.

I didn't test the opt-in hermetic sandbox, which by its help mounts only what `--sandbox_add_mount_pair` provides. I don't know what that mode does with the network, and I did not run macOS. If those pages mean that mode, saying so would settle the part about reads.

body_text:
The reporter of #4963 wanted `--sandbox_block_path` "to prevent likely cases of loss of hermeticity". Its help is one line: "For sandboxed actions, disallow access to this path." On Linux I found two cases where an action read a path passed to this flag. Neither is in the flag's help or in the docs.

The first is a path that does not exist when an action's sandbox is set up. linux-sandbox skips it. That is what #4963 asked for, and b6bb800 made it so, released in 7.3.0. The same issue asked for the flag's description to "document what this is", and the help still reads as quoted above. I'm not asking for a warning. I mention the silence because it leaves the build no way to show that the path wasn't blocked. On 9.2.0 the console output with the flag and an absent path was the same as without the flag, apart from timings and the output directory's name. It was still the same at `--sandbox_debug -s` once timestamps and PIDs are removed, and at that verbosity an applied block prints a bind mount line naming the path. 7.2.1 failed the build instead: "Mount target '...' does not exist."

Because the check runs for each action, a path that appears during the build was blocked for some actions and not others. I ran two genrules, B depending on A, with the blocked file absent at the start. A host process created it after A had started. Action A read it. B, set up afterwards, got `Permission denied`. With the file present from the start both were denied, and without the flag both read it.

The second case is a block that was applied. While an action ran, I replaced the blocked file from outside the sandbox, once by renaming a new file over it and once by deleting and recreating it. Both times the running action read the new file. Rewriting the file in place kept it blocked, and actions started afterwards were blocked again. With a blocked directory on 9.1.1, the action's `/proc/self/mountinfo` listed the bind mount before the replacement and not after. That matches `mount_namespaces(7)`: a mount point replaced from another mount namespace is detached, as the kernel has done since Linux 3.18. Renaming a new file over the old one is the usual way to update a file atomically. So a blocked file that a host process updates that way while an action runs becomes an undeclared input of that action.

The mechanism isn't new. The kernel documents it, and another sandbox that hides paths with bind mounts ran into it and wrote it down when it changed its own cleanup (https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/pull/184). What I couldn't find in Bazel's help or tracker is that an action already running can read a blocked path that appears, or is replaced, after its sandbox was set up. The nearest issue, #24514, is a different limit of the same flag, which a maintainer traced to symlink resolution.

All of this was on Linux, Debian 13 with kernel 6.12, under linux-sandbox. On 9.2.0 I ran every case twice, each from a fresh workspace and output root. The absent path and the path that appeared mid-build gave the same results on 8.8.0, and on 9.1.1 with a blocked directory. I didn't run macOS, where these paths are passed to `sandbox-exec` (#4963), and I didn't run the hermetic sandbox. processwrapper-sandbox ignores the flag altogether: under it the file was readable with the flag set.

For linux-sandbox, one sentence in the help would cover both: for each action, the path is blocked only if it exists when that action's sandbox is set up, and only until something replaces it while the action runs.

body_text:
### Description of the bug:


`scripts/release/relnotes.py` catches every `Exception` around the release-tag lookup. As a result, programming errors such as `TypeError` or `IndexError` are converted into the misleading message `Not a release branch`, and the original failure is lost. Only the expected Git subprocess failure should be handled as a non-release branch.

### Which category does this issue belong to?

_No response_

### What's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.


1. Import `scripts/release/relnotes.py` in a small Python harness.
2. Replace its `git` helper with a stub that raises `TypeError("unexpected")`.
3. Invoke the release-notes entry point.

The script exits with the non-release-branch message instead of propagating the unexpected exception.

### Which operating system are you running Bazel on?


All platforms with Python

### What is the output of `bazel info release`?


development version (current master)

### If `bazel info release` returns `development version` or `(@non-git)`, tell us how you built Bazel.


Source inspection and isolated script-level reproduction against the current master revision.

### What's the output of `git remote get-url origin; git rev-parse HEAD` ?


```text
https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel.git
680f57bbe5f72e29ac091ba4fcfe12f5f53dc80b
```

### If this is a regression, please try to identify the Bazel commit where the bug was introduced with bazelisk --bisect.


Not bisected. The behavior is present on the current master revision.

### Have you found anything relevant by searching the web?

Searched open and closed bazelbuild/bazel issues using the affected file name and failure mode. I did not find an issue describing this specific behavior.

### Any other information, logs, or outputs that you want to share?

A focused fix and regression verification are available in #31321.

### Description of the bug:


`src/create_java_tools_release.sh` classifies the result of `gcloud storage objects describe` through `&& echo yes || echo no`. Permission, authentication, and network failures are therefore treated as if the destination object did not exist, and the script proceeds to upload. The separate check also creates a time-of-check/time-of-use race.

### Which category does this issue belong to?

_No response_

### What's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.


1. Put a `gcloud` stub first on `PATH` that returns a permission error from `storage objects describe`.
2. Run the Java tools upload path.
3. Observe that the failed lookup is interpreted as `no` and an upload is attempted.

An atomic create-only copy using `--if-generation-match=0` avoids both problems.

### Description of the bug:


`src/combine_distfiles_to_tar.sh` iterates over `$*`. This re-splits caller-provided archive arguments, so a valid archive path containing whitespace is processed as multiple files.

### Which category does this issue belong to?

_No response_

3. The script processes `input` separately and fails with `unknown archive type: input` instead of combining the archive.

Linux or macOS (POSIX shell)

development version (current master)

### Description of the bug:


`src/package-bazel.sh` expands several path values without preserving argument boundaries. A `TMPDIR` containing spaces makes the `mktemp` invocation split its template, and input paths containing spaces or glob characters can also be split or expanded unexpectedly. Cleanup uses the same unsafe expansion.

### Which category does this issue belong to?

_No response_

### What's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.


1. Create a temporary directory such as `/tmp/bazel packaging`.
2. Set `TMPDIR` to that directory and run `src/package-bazel.sh` with otherwise valid inputs.
3. Observe `mktemp: too many templates` before packaging starts.

Separately, pass an input path containing a space or literal `*` and observe that it is not kept as one path.

### Which operating system are you running Bazel on?


Linux or macOS (Bash packaging tooling)

### What is the output of `bazel info release`?


development version (current master)

### If `bazel info release` returns `development version` or `(@non-git)`, tell us how you built Bazel.


Source inspection and isolated script-level reproduction against the current master revision.

### What's the output of `git remote get-url origin; git rev-parse HEAD` ?


```text
https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel.git
680f57bbe5f72e29ac091ba4fcfe12f5f53dc80b
```

### If this is a regression, please try to identify the Bazel commit where the bug was introduced with bazelisk --bisect.


Not bisected. The behavior is present on the current master revision.

### Have you found anything relevant by searching the web?

Searched open and closed bazelbuild/bazel issues using the affected file name and failure mode. I did not find an issue describing this specific behavior.

### Any other information, logs, or outputs that you want to share?

A focused quoting fix with developer and normal packaging checks is available in #31322.

### Description of the bug:


In `scripts/ci/build.sh`, `create_index_html` is implemented as `create_index_md "${@}" | pandoc -f markdown -t html`. The script enables `set -eu` but not `pipefail`, so a failure in `create_index_md` is hidden when `pandoc` exits successfully. A release job can then continue with incomplete HTML.

### Which category does this issue belong to?

_No response_

### What's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.


1. Source `scripts/ci/build.sh` with external setup isolated.
2. Make a dependency used by `create_index_md` return nonzero (for example, stub release-page generation to fail).
3. Use a `pandoc` stub that consumes stdin and exits 0.
4. Call `create_index_html`.

The function returns success despite the Markdown producer failing. Expected: the producer failure is propagated and no incomplete index is accepted.

### Which operating system are you running Bazel on?


Linux (Bash release tooling)

### What is the output of `bazel info release`?


development version (current master)

### If `bazel info release` returns `development version` or `(@non-git)`, tell us how you built Bazel.

https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel.git
680f57bbe5f72e29ac091ba4fcfe12f5f53dc80b

### Description of the bug:


`tools/test/collect_cc_coverage.sh` accumulates LLVM runtime objects in a scalar string (`object_param+=" -object ${line_runtime_object}"`) and later expands it unquoted. An object path containing whitespace is split into multiple arguments passed to `llvm-cov export`.

### Which category does this issue belong to?

_No response_

### What's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.


1. Create a coverage manifest/runtime object list containing an object path such as `/tmp/coverage objects/foo.o`.
2. Put an `llvm-cov` stub in place that records its argv.
3. Exercise the LLVM coverage export path in `tools/test/collect_cc_coverage.sh`.
4. Observe that the one object path is received as separate `/tmp/coverage` and `objects/foo.o` arguments.

Expected: each `-object` value is stored and expanded as one array element.

### Which operating system are you running Bazel on?


Linux or macOS (LLVM coverage)

### What is the output of `bazel info release`?


development version (current master)

### If `bazel info release` returns `development version` or `(@non-git)`, tell us how you built Bazel.


Source inspection and isolated script-level reproduction against the current master revision.

```text

680f57bbe5f72e29ac091ba4fcfe12f5f53dc80b

Not bisected. The behavior is present on the current master revision.

### Description of the feature request

`MerkleTreeComputer` serializes each `Directory` proto to a `byte[]` via `toByteArray()` before hashing it:

```java
byte[] blob = directory.build().toByteArray();
Digest digest = digestUtil.compute(blob);

if (blobPolicy != DISCARD) {
  blobs.putIfAbsent(digest, blob);
}
```

Under `BlobPolicy.DISCARD`, that array exists only to be hashed and is then discarded — an avoidable allocation plus a second pass over the bytes.

### Description of the bug:


When using `--experimental_remote_cache_chunking` against a remote cache that does not support CDC, Bazel will print out:

> ERROR: Unable to write all BEP events to file due to 'com.google.devtools.build.lib.remote.common.RemoteExecutionCapabilitiesException: java.io.IOException: --experimental_remote_cache_chunking requested but remote does not support any chunking algorithm supported by Bazel (FastCDC 2020 or RepMaxCDC)'

This means usage of the flag needs to tailored to the remote cache; it would be preferable if Bazel would gracefully continue without chunking, as if the flag not been provided.

### Which category does this issue belong to?

Remote Execution

### What's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.


1. Use a remote cache backend that does not advertise CDC
2. Set `--experimental_remote_cache_chunking` in .bazelrc
3. Run a build using the remote cache

### Which operating system are you running Bazel on?


linux

### What is the output of `bazel info release`?


release 10.0.0-pre.20260911.2

### If `bazel info release` returns `development version` or `(@non-git)`, tell us how you built Bazel.

### Description of the feature request:


This idea originally came from [this discussion](https://bazelbuild.slack.com/archives/C05UNC5AANQ/p1790611492505819) on Bazel slack when discussing how to integrate Bazel into LLVM so that it can be used via Bzlmod.

The idea:

How about adding support for something like `set_source_root` function in MODULE.bazel which should be at the beginning of the file and would define a root for the repository relative to the current directory?

Then, a LLVM repository could have a folder bazel with all files related to the Bazel build, mimicking the repository hierarchy, but adding just the .bzl and BUILD.bazel files. Bazel would interpret that as if all Bazel files in the current folder are overlayed onto the folder given by `set_source_root`.

Is it possible to implement something like that in Bazel?

It would benefit multiple projects that treat Bazel as a second-class citizen, not just LLVM (OpenCV comes to my mind). By not installing itself at the project's root, the community might be more accepting of Bazel contributions and could even start experimenting with it and, once it sees it's a better build system, consider choosing it as the default.

So, the structure would be something like:

```
- LLVM root
|- bazel
|- clang
|- cmake
|- ... (all current LLVM folders)
```

And bazel folder would look something like this:

```
- bazel
|- MODULE.bazel
|- BUILD.bazel
|- clang
|  |- BUILD.bazel
|- llvm
|  |- BUILD.bazel
...
```

and MODULE.bazel would look something like this:

```
set_source_root("../")

module(
    name = "llvm",
    version = "23.1.3",
)

bazel_dep( ... )
...
```

Or maybe something like `source_root` could be a new parameter of the already-existing module function?

AFAIK, a similar approach with overlays is already used in BCR, but it's a "BCR thing", not a "bazel native thing", or am I wrong?

I see that the same idea is already implemented in LLVM, but uses [this hack](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/main/utils/bazel/extensions.bzl#L28-L33) to apply the overlay, and unfortunately, this trick does not work for downstream module users...

### Which category does this issue belong to?

Core

### What underlying problem are you trying to solve with this feature?


Allowing bazel build system integration into non-root folders of projects that may not want to accept bazel files in their root or mixed with their source code.

## Description of the feature request

`http_archive`'s `files` attribute (and any rule that uses `symlink_files` from `@bazel_tools//tools/build_defs/repo:utils.bzl`) places each file with `ctx.symlink`. When the label is in the main repo, the repo then contains a symlink into the workspace. `RepositoryUtils.replantSymlinks` treats that as unsafe to cache (`portableSymlinksOnly = false`), so `RepositoryFetchFunction` skips the repo contents cache for a repo that is otherwise reproducible. Nothing reports the skip.

`build_file` doesn't have this problem, because `workspace_and_buildfile` copies it with `ctx.file(..., ctx.read(...))`. A `files` overlay of the same file disables caching, while `build_file` keeps it.

Could `symlink_files` copy the file instead, at least when the label is in the main repo? The source is already watched (`ctx.watch(src_path)`), so changing it still refetches. The function's own comment notes that `ctx.symlink` "may be implemented as a copy" on Windows, so copy semantics look acceptable there already.

If symlinking is intentional, an opt-in such as a `files_mode = "copy"` attribute would also work. Separately, it would help to report when a repo that returns `reproducible = True` is excluded from the contents cache. Today the only sign is that `external/<repo>` is a real directory instead of a symlink into the cache.

## Which category does this issue belong to?

External Dependency

## What underlying problem are you trying to solve with this feature?

We run many git worktrees of one monorepo (largely agent-created), each with its own output base and a shared repository cache. Reproducible repos are fetched once and shared from the contents cache. A repo with a `files` overlay is downloaded from the repository cache and extracted again into every output base. For us that was an 8 GB prebuilt archive whose only overlay was a single license file, so every new worktree cost 8 GB and a ~3.5 minute fetch. Switching that one overlay to a copy made it shareable: the fetch in the second output base took under 5 seconds.

Minimal repro on 9.2.0 (Linux). A scratch workspace containing an empty `BUILD.bazel`, `overlay.BUILD` with `filegroup(name = "all", srcs = glob(["*.c"]))`, and this `MODULE.bazel`:

```starlark
http_archive = use_repo_rule("@bazel_tools//tools/build_defs/repo:http.bzl", "http_archive")

http_archive(
    name = "zlib_files",
    files = {"BUILD.bazel": "//:overlay.BUILD"},
    sha256 = "9a93b2b7dfdac77ceba5a558a580e74667dd6fede4585b91eefb60f03b72df23",
    strip_prefix = "zlib-1.3.1",
    urls = ["https://github.com/madler/zlib/releases/download/v1.3.1/zlib-1.3.1.tar.gz"],
)

http_archive(
    name = "zlib_build_file",
    build_file = "//:overlay.BUILD",
    sha256 = "9a93b2b7dfdac77ceba5a558a580e74667dd6fede4585b91eefb60f03b72df23",
    strip_prefix = "zlib-1.3.1",
    urls = ["https://github.com/madler/zlib/releases/download/v1.3.1/zlib-1.3.1.tar.gz"],
)
```

```sh
for ob in ob1 ob2; do
  bazel --output_base=/tmp/$ob fetch --repository_cache=/tmp/repocache \
    --repo=@zlib_files --repo=@zlib_build_file
  ls -ld /tmp/$ob/external/+http_archive+zlib_files /tmp/$ob/external/+http_archive+zlib_build_file
done
```

In both output bases, `+http_archive+zlib_build_file` is a symlink to the same entry under `/tmp/repocache/contents/`, while `+http_archive+zlib_files` is a separate real directory each time.

## Which operating system are you running Bazel on?

Linux (Ubuntu 24.04, x86_64)

## What is the output of `bazel info release`?

release 9.2.0

## If `bazel info release` returns `development version` or `(@non-git)`, tell us how you built Bazel.

N/A

## What's the output of `git remote get-url origin; git rev-parse HEAD` ?

N/A

## Have you found anything relevant by searching the web?

- #28582 added symlink replanting before caching. The `replantSymlinksIntoMainRepo = false` call in `RepositoryFetchFunction` says the local contents cache "can't handle any cross-repo symlinks", which is the case `files` produces.
- #29515 covers replanted `../_main` symlinks on Windows. It's related, but about a different path.
- I found no existing issue about `files` or `symlink_files` and the contents cache.

## Any other information, logs, or outputs that you want to share?

A copy loses the executable bit unless it's carried over, and `repository_ctx` has no way to read a file's mode that I could find. In our own `http_archive`-style rule we check it with `ctx.execute(["test", "-x", src])` and pass the result to `ctx.file(..., executable = ...)`. A built-in change could presumably do this natively.

  bazel --output_base=/tmp/$ob fetch --repository_cache=/tmp/repocache \
    --repo=@zlib_files --repo=@zlib_build_file
  ls -ld /tmp/$ob/external/+http_archive+zlib_files /tmp/$ob/external/+http_archive+zlib_build_file
done
```

In both output bases, `+http_archive+zlib_build_file` is a symlink to the same entry under `/tmp/repocache/contents/`, while `+http_archive+zlib_files` is a separate real directory each time.

release 9.2.0

body_text:
### Description of the feature request:


With `--windows_enable_symlinks`, Bazel creates real NTFS symlinks for files, but still creates **junctions** for directories. That includes targets that don't exist yet but are declared as directories (`SymlinkTargetType.DIRECTORY`). The cause is `CreateSymlink` in `src/main/native/windows/file.cc`: it rejects any directory target with `kTargetIsDirectory`, and `WindowsFileSystem.createSymbolicLink` then falls back to `createJunction`.

I propose that when `--windows_enable_symlinks` is set, Bazel creates directory symlinks for directories too, by passing `SYMBOLIC_LINK_FLAG_DIRECTORY` to `CreateSymbolicLinkW`:

- If the target exists, its type decides between a file and a directory symlink.
- If it doesn't exist yet, `SymlinkTargetType` decides.
- Without `--windows_enable_symlinks`, nothing changes: junctions are still used, and needing no special privileges is the main advantage of junctions.

### Which category does this issue belong to?

Core

### What underlying problem are you trying to solve with this feature?


**Compile performance with MinGW GCC 15.** When compiling C/C++ with the MinGW-w64 GCC 15 toolchain, resolving paths through directory junctions is noticeably slower than through directory symlinks. Bazel builds create many directory links (e.g. in the execroot and in sandboxes), and the compiler resolves its include paths through them, so this adds up to a measurable slowdown. With `--windows_enable_symlinks` the privilege needed for real symlinks is already there, but Bazel still creates junctions for directories, so this cost can't be avoided today.

Depending on the number of include paths, our performance could be increased by a factor of 2 to 5.

**General.** So the trees Bazel creates mix symlinks and junctions depending on whether the target is a file or a directory. Users who have opted into real symlinks would expect directories to get them too, as they do on Linux and macOS.

### Which operating system are you running Bazel on?


Windows 11 (build 26200)

### What is the output of `bazel info release`?


development version

### If `bazel info release` returns `development version` or `(@non-git)`, tell us how you built Bazel.


Built from `master` with `bazel build //src:bazel-dev.exe`.

### What's the output of `git remote get-url origin; git rev-parse HEAD` ?


```text
https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel.git
51be3f9ce006011c2ec55ecbb2c2486d09a35c15
```

### Have you found anything relevant by searching the web?

I found this git commit, that enables symlinks for files but not for directories https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/commit/0076a02308459e848f99f81628b39c0c90cc5758.

### Any other information, logs, or outputs that you want to share?

I had a brief chat with @tjgq about this topic on slack. As a result of our discussion, he asked me to file this feature request.

### Which category does this issue belong to?

Core

### What underlying problem are you trying to solve with this feature?


**Compile performance with MinGW GCC 15.** When compiling C/C++ with the MinGW-w64 GCC 15 toolchain, resolving paths through directory junctions is noticeably slower than through directory symlinks. Bazel builds create many directory links (e.g. in the execroot and in sandboxes), and the compiler resolves its include paths through them, so this adds up to a measurable slowdown. With `--windows_enable_symlinks` the privilege needed for real symlinks is already there, but Bazel still creates junctions for directories, so this cost can't be avoided today.

Depending on the number of include paths, our performance could be increased by a factor of 2 to 5.

**General.** So the trees Bazel creates mix symlinks and junctions depending on whether the target is a file or a directory. Users who have opted into real symlinks would expect directories to get them too, as they do on Linux and macOS.
